GetMaxMarines.doc: Marine capacity: the Big Ship value, but at least 8.

GetSize.doc: Total size of the ship's scene object (m3) when it exists, otherwise 30000.

2026.name: M6

2027.doc: Carrier-type warship (CarrierBase subclass) whose code is identical to M1 (2021): same squad, patrol and escalation logic. No page 2006 name; probably a second model or faction variant of M1.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler with the same escalation as M1 (steps in m48, 10 time units per step). Non-player attackers are attacked back and called for help.

Create.doc: Initializes the ship through the carrier base. Unless it is created player-owned (mode 10), fills the crew list m112 with a navigation officer (10014) followed by crew members (10013).

CreatePlayerOwned.doc: Creates the ship as player-owned (creation mode 10) and adds it to sector when one is given.

GetAnswers.doc: Dialog answers as in M1: for questions 20 and 30 adds 'Surrender!' (10021), and 10022 when m13 bit 4 is set and the player is not an enemy here. Player-owned ships get none.

GetNewSquadLeader.doc: Picks a squad leader from idle fighters of this owner: an M3 first, then M4, then M5, and assigns up to a random limit of followers. Returns the leader or 0. Same as M1.

comments.text: Enemy fleets heading for the sector, or present in it, reduce the strength to cover.
Enemies remain: squads are sent in a fork; otherwise attack or patrol.

ShipAttackedBy.doc: Reaction when one of the ships of this carrier (attackedShip) is attacked. Same logic as M1: scrambles a squad against the attacker when the enemy strength in range is too high, otherwise attacks or patrols. At most one reaction per 120 time units.

StartControlTask.doc: Background task started once. After a random wait it gives idle AI-controlled ships in table m108 a job every 60 time units, until the carrier becomes player-owned. Same as M1.

StartPatrolSquad.doc: Picks a new squad leader and sends it to patrol sector. Returns the leader or 0.

2027.name: CarrierSquad

203.doc: Debug and cheat helper singleton: equipment/notoriety cheats, test object spawning, time warp control, B3D reload. Called from the Client key handlers and from the cheat-string checker; most debug methods are stubbed out in the release script.

B3DReload.doc: Debug: reloads the B3D static data while staying in the sector. The player leaves and re-enters the sector and the ship position/rotation is restored afterwards.

CenterShip.doc: Debug: moves the player ship to the sector centre height position.

CheatEquip.doc: Adds a fixed list of equipment and upgrade wares (type 16) to the given ship, plus every upgrade product defined by class 5000 objects.

comments.text: game feature bit 1024 = script editor
game state low 2 bits set to 1 (probably 'cheated' state)

CheckStringForCheats.doc: Checks typed text against secret cheat phrases. 'Thereshallbewings' enables the script editor game feature (bit 1024) and loads all scripts; 'Makeanapplepiefromscratch' sets the low bits of the game state to 1. Returns 1 if a cheat fired.

DebugBattle.doc: Debug: spawns a large mixed fleet of hostile and friendly warships (classes 2021-2025) around the player.

DebugOreMine.doc: Debug: finds the asteroid nearest to the player ship in the current sector and, if within 500000 m, starts a build task (class 623) on it.

DebugTestObjects.doc: Debug: creates two class-2006 stations and a class-2044 object in the player's sector and connects them.

DecreaseTimeWarp.doc: Halves the time warp factor while it is above 4096 (fixed point, 65536 = 1x).

comments.text: cycle through all laser subtypes (type 8)
shields (type 9) stop at the best one

EquipmentCheat.doc: Cheat: gives the player ship a random missile, the next laser and shield types and the full upgrade set (CheatEquip).

IncreaseTimeWarp.doc: Doubles the time warp factor up to a limit of 1048576 (fixed point, 65536 = 1x).

IsCheatActive.doc: Returns whether a cheat has been activated.

MakeTestObj.doc: Debug: creates an object of class cls, gives it shields/lasers by kind (7 = ship with lasers, 5 = shielded object, 4 = plain) and puts it in the player's sector near the player ship.

MoveNearGate.doc: Debug: teleports the player ship to one of the four sector edges (near a gate), cycling through them on each call.

NotoCheat.doc: Cheat: sets the player's notoriety with races 5, 3 and 4 to 100000.

ToggleProfiling.doc: Toggles script VM profiling on and off.

TradeCheat.doc: Debug: if no regular menu is open, opens the trade menu (class 2217) for the object currently tracked by the main monitor when it is a class 2016 object.

Upgrade.doc: Debug: equips a freshly created ship with default items, places it in the player's environment and starts its action.

203.name: Cheats

2030.doc: TP trade ship (page 2006), a TradeShip subclass with a larger marine capacity.

GetMaxMarines.doc: Marine capacity: the Ship value, but at least 40.

2030.name: TP

2031.doc: TS trade ship (page 2006), a TradeShip subclass with no code of its own.
2031.name: TS

2032.doc: TL ship (page 2006, dobj SHIP_TL), a CarrierBase subclass. Can be hired by the player: a hired TL follows the player, pays a jump fee (GetFee) and builds stations from station wares (types 5 and 6 in the ware table m35). Its questions cover hire, fee and freight orders.

comments.text: Step 2 takes notoriety with m41.AddNotorietyAsPercent, while other branches use GetOwner(): inconsistent, check.
Step 3 against an enemy: shield under 1/8 of max sends step 4 and a call for help.
SendSquad with limit 1: one fighter is sent against the attacker.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler. Attacks by the player escalate in m48 (1 warned, 2 license withdrawn with notoriety loss, 3 hostile, 4 critical shield and call for help). Other attackers are answered with a counter-attack, a call for help and a squad.

comments.text: The build runs in a fork and waits 10 ticks first.
Waits while a menu of class 2225 is open (C503 = active menu).
C623.StartBuild starts the build; one ware of this type is then consumed.
No station ware left: the carrier is released (base SetHired(0)).

BuildStation.doc: Starts building the station described by buildOrder (ware object, ware id at index 7). Only station wares the carrier holds can be built. The build runs in a fork: wait, undock, wait for the station menu class 2225 to close, start the build with C623, consume one ware. Returns 1 when the build is queued.

comments.text: Opens menu 2270 (station build) for this carrier.

CmdConsoleCommandExec.doc: Executes console command 2110: opens the station build menu (class 2270) for this carrier and returns 3. Other commands go to the Carrier base.

comments.text: Text 13:131 'Command accepted'.

CmdConsoleCommandExecCallback.doc: Callback from the station build menu. If the chosen item (choice) is a ware object (expression type 8) and the build conditions hold, plays 'Command accepted' and starts BuildStation. Returns 1 when started.

comments.text: Crew list: first entry is the navigation officer (10014).
Loop starts at index 2, so m112[1] is never set. Probably a bug (M1 starts at 1). Check.

Create.doc: Initializes the ship through the Carrier base. Unless it is created player-owned (mode 10), builds a crew list in m112 and sets the pilot voice flag 8192.

CreatePlayerOwned.doc: Creates the ship as player-owned (creation mode 10) and adds it to sector when one is given.

GetAStationWare.doc: Returns the first ware id in the ware table m35 whose type is 5 or 6, or 0 if none. A ware id packs type in bits 16..23 and subtype in bits 0..15.

comments.text: Text 18:10060 'Please stop your engines' (order menu, hired ships).

GetAnswers.doc: Answers for the TL. Question 30: when hired, the order menu (10056 if it has a station and is in range, 10055 follow me, 10058, 10057, 10059, 10060 stop, 10046 release). When not hired and the owner's mask and subtype allow it: 10030 hire offer. With a station: 10020 freight. Questions 70 to 73 add 10040 (accept fee) and 10041 (decline). Then the Big Ship base answers.

comments.text: Hire offer: reply 63 when the carrier has a station, else 70 plus fee class.
Fee paid when the money is enough, then the carrier is hired (reply 65).
Not enough money: reply 64.
10056 opens the build-station menu (2270, paramType 10000). The answer text 18:10056 says 'Please drop my freight here.': check.
10058 opens the order menu (2228, paramType 19 = dock at a station: text 18:10058 'Please move to shipyard...').
10057 opens the order menu with paramType 3 = move to sector (text 18:10057 'Please move to sector...').
10059 opens the order menu with paramType 10001 = move to position (text 18:10059).

GetCapitalShipQuestion.doc: Replies to hire, fee, release and order questions of the TL. 10030 (hire offer): reply 63 with a station, else 70 plus fee class. 10040 (accept fee): if hired the carrier follows the player (command 5), else if the player can pay the fee it is charged and hired (reply 65), otherwise reply 64. 10046 releases it (SetHired(0), return home). 10055 follows the player, 10057-10059 open the sector, shipyard and position order menus, 10060 stops. Other questions go to the Big Ship base.

comments.text: Only menuType 0 and menuId -104.
Entry enabled (0) only when the carrier can build here: in the sector, has a station, not docked.
Entry {2110, enabled flag, 2020, 14}: 2110 is the build-station command.

GetCmdConsoleCommands.doc: Adds console entry 2110 (build a station) on the root station menu (menuType 0, menuId -104). Enabled (0) when the carrier is in the player's sector or player-owned, has a station and is not docked. Then the Carrier base entries are added. Returns the new count.

comments.text: Race 10: no fee.
Races 1, 17 and 18 share one fee table.

GetFee.doc: Jump fee in credits, from the owner race (m41 id) and the fee class of GetFeeClass (0 cheapest to 3 most expensive). Race 10 pays nothing; races without a table pay 0.

GetFeeClass.doc: Fee class from the owner's notoriety toward the player: 3 below -10, 2 below 10, 1 below 1000, else 0.

GetNumWareStation.doc: Total count of station wares (types 5 and 6) held in m35.

comments.text: Question 67 (after freight) uses lines 67 and 68.

GetQuestionArray.doc: Builds the text and voice line list for a question: 67 gives lines 67 and 68 with the pilot voice, 70 to 73 give line 60 plus the question, a negative id is a text object whose text is returned, other ids go to the Big Ship base.

HasStation.doc: True if the carrier holds a station ware (type 5 or 6).

comments.text: Command 12 = MOVE_SECTOR to the chosen sector.
Reply 10047 is a dummy answer: 'Dock to the same station as I do.' (forces Affirmative).
C200.PlayFailSample: refused order.
Command 19 = MOVE_POS: position vector with the sector as its fourth element.

ReceiveDialogParameter.doc: Handles the parameter the player picked in an order menu. paramType 3: move to sector (command 12). paramType 1: dock at a station (command 7, DOCKAT) if it can dock here. paramType 10000: build the station from the chosen ware. paramType 10001: move to a position (command 19). Returns a reply code (10047 accepted, 10048 station ordered) or -1.

RemoveAllStations.doc: Removes every station ware from the carrier one unit at a time (AddWare with -1).

SetHired.doc: Hires or releases the carrier. Flag 512 in m12 means hired. On hire the carrier follows the player (StartFollowLeader); on release it removes all station wares.

StartAction.doc: Idle action. Flag 4096 blocks it. Owner player: none. A hired carrier has no action of its own. Otherwise: docked at the target m42 means none; else it goes to its home sector m43 (command 12) or idles there (command 17).

StartReturnToHome.doc: Sends the carrier back to its home sector (command 12, MOVE_SECTOR) unless it belongs to the player or is hired.

comments.text: Message 64: the player cannot pay the fee; the carrier is released and returns home.
Fee is paid on every jump.

__LeaveHyperspace.doc: After a jump: a hired carrier (flag 512, not player-owned) pays GetFee() from the player's money. If the money is short, reply 64 is sent and the carrier is released and sent home in a fork. Returns the base result.

2032.name: TL

2033.doc: A carrier (page 2006: Carrier), a big ship with a hangar: it stores the ships docked in it (m117) and manages its dock ports (m119). Child classes are 2019, 2026 (M6 on page 2006) and 2141 (TM). Created by Create with an owner index; the parent is the big ship (2073).

0.doc: ships inside the hangar, keyed by object
0.name: dockedShips

1.doc: number of dock ports in use
1.name: occupiedDockPorts

2.doc: ship occupying each dock port slot, 0 when free
2.name: dockPortOccupants

Activate.doc: Activates the carrier and then each ship in the hangar, when the carrier has a scene. Returns the scene object.

AddShip.doc: Stores ship arg1 in the hangar: sets its environment to this carrier, registers it with C305 and, when the carrier has a sector, adds it to the sector's landed ships.

ChangePlayerShipTo.doc: When this carrier is the player ship, hands the player over to arg1. A ship that was docked here is put back into the hangar with 1000000 shield.

comments.text: A bay must be free: docked ships below the dock bay size.
C150 (CLIENT, per hints) is told the docking is allowed.
Text 13:1285 'Docking aborted' when no bay is free.

CmdConsoleCommandExec.doc: Executes console command 2100 (dock request): if a bay is free and the controlled ship may dock, requests a dock port and returns 1. Otherwise plays 'Docking aborted'.

Create.doc: Creates the carrier on top of the big-ship create. Clears the hangar table and allocates one dock slot per dock port of the carrier type. Starts the (empty) control task.

Deactivate.doc: Stops the carrier's scene object and deactivates the ships in the hangar, then runs the parent Deactivate.

DropIllegalFreight.doc: Drops illegal freight of this carrier and of its ships. Returns 1 if anything was dropped.

comments.text: Dock request only on the root console menu (menuType 0, menuId -100) of carriers with a dock bay.
Object the player currently controls (ship under monitor control).
Dock entry is enabled (0) only if the controlled ship may dock here and is in approach; 1 = disabled.
Entry -99 is probably a separator line.

GetCmdConsoleCommands.doc: Adds the carrier's console entries: a separator and a dock request (command 2100) when the carrier has a dock bay. Returns the new entry count.

GetDockBaySize.doc: Dock bay size of the carrier type.

GetNumOfDockedShips.doc: Number of ships in the hangar (m117).

GetNumOfLandedShips.doc: Number of landed ships. Same value as GetNumOfDockedShips: both count the hangar table.

GetSalePrice.doc: Sale value of the carrier: the sale value of the docked ships plus the value of the carrier itself. arg1 is the sale context passed to the parent.

GetShips.doc: Table of ships in the hangar (m117).

GetShipsIncludingDocked.doc: All ships in the hangar, including the ships in hangars of nested carriers.

HasFreeDockPort.doc: True when a free dock port exists for ship arg1. Nothing is reserved.

HasFreeDockPortGSubType.doc: True when a free dock port exists for the general subtype arg1. Nothing is reserved.

HasFreeDockPortSubType.doc: True when a free dock port exists for the subtype arg1 of the carrier type (type 7). Nothing is reserved.

HasIllegalGoods.doc: True if this carrier or any ship in its ship table (m117) carries illegal goods; otherwise the base answer.

HasPolice.doc: True when a fighter (class 2034) owned by this carrier is in its hangar.

comments.text: a player ship is refused by a non-capturable carrier of another owner, unless flag 8388608 in m12 is set and this carrier is the player ship

IsDockingAllowedForShip.doc: True when ship arg1 may dock here: not an enemy, the hangar has room, the owner's notoriety with the ship's owner is at least -10, and a player ship is not refused by a non-capturable carrier of another owner.

IsDockingPossibleOf.doc: True when the parent allows docking with ship arg1, or when the carrier type allows it for ship arg1's general subtype.

KilledBy.doc: When the carrier is killed, every ship in the hangar self-destructs (type 14) in its own fork. The flag bit 31 in m12 guards against a second call and is cleared again. Then the parent KilledBy runs. Invincible carriers are not killed.

comments.text: The player ship is never ordered out.
Each ship waits one more second than the previous one.
Command 15 = KILL_ENEMIES (page 2008).

LeaveShip.doc: Called when the pilot leaves the carrier. Unless this is the player ship, each ship in the table is ordered to command 15 (KILL_ENEMIES), one second apart; then the base LeaveShip runs.

ReleaseSlot.doc: Frees the dock slot that holds ship arg1 and lowers the occupied count (never below zero).

RemoveShip.doc: Removes ship arg1 from the hangar: clears its environment, unregisters it from C305 and from the sector's landed ships.

RequestDockPort.doc: Reserves a dock port for ship arg1 (its general subtype). arg2 is the large-port flag. Returns the port index, or -1.

SelfDestruct.doc: Self-destructs the ships in the hangar (type 14) in forks, then the carrier itself through the parent SelfDestruct. Bit 31 of m12 marks the carrier as self-destructing while this runs.

comments.text: The attacker's relation is set to hostile (-10000).
Command 14 (KILL_ENEMIES_AND_LAND); the last argument 1500000 is probably a timeout.
Stop once maxFighters are sent.

SendSquad.doc: Sends up to maxFighters owned fighters (class 2034) against the attacker of attackEvent. Fighters that may not forgive are switched off forgiveness first.

comments.text: Relation to group 8 set to -10000 (hostile) before the order.
Command 14 = KILL_ENEMIES_AND_LAND (page 2008), target: this carrier.
At most four fighters are sent.

SendSupport.doc: Orders up to four owned fighters (class 2034) to kill enemies and land with this carrier as the target. Probably used when the carrier is attacked.

SetDisowned.doc: Removes ship arg1 from the owned table. When the ship is marked for rebuild and was owned by this carrier's owner, a replacement is created at the nearest shipyard and transferred into this carrier's hangar (StartTransferToHangar). Ships with a job id are not rebuilt.

SetRelationsFromNotoriety.doc: Parent relation update. For carriers not owned by the player, the whole race group 8 becomes enemy (relation -1).

ShipAttackedBy.doc: Makes arg2 the current attacker of this carrier and sets its relation to arg2 to -10000 (hostile).

StartControlTask.doc: Empty stub: the carrier has no control task in this version.

StartOwnedShipsReturnHome.doc: Sends every owned ship under race logic control, and not docked in this carrier, back home (command 1).

StartPatrol.doc: Orders the carrier to patrol the given sector (command 25, PATROL).

comments.text: a port is usable when SA_GetTypeCanUseDockPort gives a non-zero value for the carrier type
usable ports flagged 1048576 are preferred and then taken without an entry in m119 (not recorded in the slot table; check whether that is intended)

__requestDockPort.doc: Finds a usable dock port for a ship of general subtype arg2. When arg3 is 0 the port is taken: the ship arg1 leaves its old slot, takes slot m119 and calls SetSlot. Returns the port index, or -1 when none is free. arg4 is passed as the large-port flag.

2033.name: Carrier

2034.doc: Fighter (page 2006), a Little Ship subclass and the parent of the squad fighters M3, M4 and M5. Carries its own escalation steps against the player (m48), answers trade and surrender questions, and returns to its home sector (m43) when idle.

comments.text: Attacker's max laser not above ours: step 1 with message 1, otherwise step 2 with message 2.
Enemy attacker at step 3: message 4; otherwise message 5.
Enemy at step 3 with shield under half: call for help and step 4.
Enemy with shield between half and four fifths: 50 percent chance of a call for help and step 4.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler with escalation steps in m48: 1 warned, 2 license withdrawn, 3 hostile, 4 shield critical and calls for help. An attack by the player sets step 2 at once when the owner's mask has bit 200. Other attackers get a counter-attack and a call for help.

Create.doc: Initializes the fighter through the Moveable Ship base, marks race 8 fighters with flag 134217728 in m12, sets the owner from the race table and the default formation type of that race.

comments.text: Illegal goods on a visible hull and the owner holds a license: 10020 only if freight is present.
Text 18:10021 'Surrender!' always offered.

GetAnswers.doc: Dialog answers for trade questions 20 and 21. Adds 'Surrender and drop your freight!' (10020) when freight is visible and the job is a group-2 (probably trade) job, or when the owner's license and illegal goods apply. Always adds 'Surrender!' (10021). Player-owned fighters get none.

comments.text: Asker's owner gains 1 notoriety: the surrender request is witnessed.
Morale check: pilot morale minus strength/10 plus 12 against a random 0..30 roll; below it the freight is dropped (reply 29).
Aggression check: the fighter attacks the asker's owner (relation -10000, attack signal, reply 27 or 4 with laser damage).
No bargaining (no morale threat, no visible cargo or home sector): reply 26 for group-2 jobs, else 25.
Strength in range under 50: reply 25.
Percent of freight given up: 3 plus a random percent, +5 when the owner's notoriety toward the player exceeds 1000, capped at 99.
Owner loses the license after the surrender (LoseLicense).

GetQuestion.doc: Answers the player's trade or surrender question (arg2 = question id, arg3 = asker). Only for voiced pilots and question contexts 7 or 17. Question 10020 (surrender freight) raises the owner's notoriety; the fighter drops illegal freight, fights back or gives up freight by a percent and loses the license. Returns a reply code.

Hit.doc: When hit by an object of another owner (attacker, arg4), calls for help from its group, then the base Hit runs.

comments.text: Docked fighter of the player: command 0 (none).
Flying player fighter: command 17 (IDLE).
Race 6: 80 percent chance of a patrol with a random radius from the sector size.
Race 7: 10 percent chance of no movement, otherwise a random multiple of a quarter sector.
Command 26 = KILL_ENEMIES_RANGE (page 2008), arguments: radius, position offset, flag.

StartAction.doc: Chooses the idle action of the fighter. Flag 4096 blocks it. A player fighter idles or lands; a docked fighter stops, and the others protect m15, return to their dock target (m42) or patrol around the home sector (m43) with a radius from their race.

StartPatrol.doc: Orders the fighter to patrol the sector arg1 (command 25, PATROL).

2034.name: Fighter

2035.doc: Pirate trade ship (page 2006 'TS(Pirate)'), a TradeShip subclass. Pirates demand freight and turn hostile when refused. The demand counter is stored in demandCounter. The class overrides CallForHelp with an empty body, so its handlers call the Ship version explicitly.

0.doc: probably cargo demands made: set to 3 after a demand, 0 = never demanded
0.name: demandCounter

comments.text: Explicit C2004::CallForHelp: bypasses the empty override in this class.
Shield under half at step 3: call for help, step 4, notoriety -1 with the attacker's owner.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Pirate attack handler with its own escalation ladder in m48 (1 to 4). The TradeShip handler returns at once for this class, so this body is the only one that runs. Pirates re-evaluate after 600 time units for a new attacker, and use the Ship CallForHelp explicitly.

CallForHelp.doc: Empty override: calls for help are suppressed for this class when they go through the virtual call. The handlers call C2004::CallForHelp directly.

comments.text: Race id is used as pilot subrace id.

Create.doc: Initializes the ship through TradeShip.Create, clears demandCounter, and stores the race id as the pilot subrace.

comments.text: Text 18:10020 'Surrender and drop your freight!'.

GetAnswers.doc: For reply 82 adds 'Surrender and drop your freight!' (10020) when the ship has freight. Does not call the base GetAnswers.

comments.text: Asker is already an enemy: reply 21.
Demand made: demandCounter 3, escalation 3, hostile to the asker, reply 82.

GetQuestion.doc: Pirate demand logic. Question 0 (hail): an enemy gets reply 21; otherwise the pirate sets demandCounter to 3, escalation to 3, turns hostile to the asker and replies 82 (the reply list for 82 offers 10020). Question 10020 (surrender freight): if already escalated or never demanded (demandCounter 0), the asker is made hostile and the reply is 4; otherwise reply 25. Returns a reply code, or nothing for other questions.

Hit.doc: When hit by an object of another owner (arg4), calls the Ship CallForHelp explicitly, then the TradeShip Hit.

2035.name: TSPirate

2037.doc: Shipyard (page 2006: Shipyard). Base for the small and big shipyards; a factory that buys and sells ships (ware type 7). Owned by an NPC or the player; it registers with its owner's shipyard list (AddShipyard/RemoveShipyard). Derives from Factory (2006).

0.doc: absolute time (ms) when mslState is re-rolled
0.name: mslStateExpiry

1.doc: random state 0-2 re-rolled every 30-60 game minutes; purpose not known
1.name: mslState

AddDefaultProductsAndResources.doc: Empty in this script: default products and resources are not added here.

CanSellWareType.doc: True when the shipyard sells the given ware (table m49).

comments.text: first state change within 0 to 3599 seconds

Create.doc: Creates the shipyard through the factory Create, then starts the state timer with a random offset of up to 60 minutes.

Destruct.doc: Removes the shipyard from its owner's list, then runs the factory Destruct.

comments.text: state still valid: return the cached value
re-roll: next change in 1800 to 3599 seconds

GetMSLState.doc: Returns a random state 0-2 that is re-rolled every 30-60 game minutes (MSL meaning unknown, probably a shipyard activity state).

GetNameFlags.doc: Name flags: the stored value, or 4 when none is set.

GetScaleFactor.doc: Shipyards use scale 65536 (1.0), not the factory type scale.

GetStatisticCycleTime.doc: Returns 0: shipyards keep no statistic cycle in this script.

GetWareStatistic.doc: Returns 0: shipyards keep no ware statistics in this script.

comments.text: ship store for shipyards is 10

GetWareTypeBestStore.doc: Ships (type 7) get store 10. Subtype 2086 uses the factory store logic; other shipyards get 1.

InitialFill.doc: Shipyard start stock: one unit of each sold ware, and the best store amount for each bought ware.

SetOwner.doc: Changes the owner. Non-player owners get the shipyard in their shipyard list; the player's own shipyards are kept out of it.

TradesWithWareType.doc: True when the shipyard buys or sells the ware.

UpdateWareStatistic.doc: Empty override: shipyards keep no ware statistics.

2037.name: Shipyard

2038.doc: Base of the trade-type little ships: TS (2031), TP (2030) and the pirate TSPirate (2035). Escalates against the player in steps stored in m48, answers freight surrender questions, and calls for help from its group. Name derived from the subclasses (no page 2006 name).

comments.text: Pirates (class 2035) skip this body: they have their own AttackedByHandler.
Home sector: an enemy goes to step 2; a weaker attacker gets step 1 and message 1, a stronger one step 2 and message 3.
Escalation steps at most every 5 time units.
Home sector, step 3 against an enemy: shield under half leads to step 4.
Home sector, step 4: shield over half drops back to step 3; shield under a fifth calls for help.
Outside the home sector, step 2: shield under a quarter gives step 3 and notoriety -4 with the attacker's owner.
After that: 20 percent just a message, otherwise DropFreight and message 29, else message 7.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler. Attacks by the player escalate in m48 with two branches: in the home sector the ship warns and then loses the license; elsewhere the escalation is faster. Attacks by other owners are answered with a counter-attack and a call for help. Pirate ships (class 2035) return at once here and use their own handler.

Create.doc: Initializes the ship through the Moveable Ship base, marks race 8 ships with flag 134217728 in m12, sets the owner from the race table and the default formation type of that race.

comments.text: Text 18:10020 'Surrender and drop your freight!'.

GetAnswers.doc: Adds 'Surrender and drop your freight!' (10020) for questions 20 and 21 when the ship has freight, then the Ship base answers.

comments.text: Asker's owner gains 1 notoriety here.
The same AddNotoriety(..., 1) call is repeated inside the drop branch: the owner probably gains 2. Check, possible bug (same in TM, 2141 at 0x0d9e71).
Illegal freight dropped toward the asker's owner (reply 29).
Morale check failed: freight dropped (reply 29).
Aggression check: attack the asker's owner (relation -10000, attack signal).
No bargaining (no morale threat, no visible cargo or home sector): reply 26.
Strength in range under 50: reply 27.
Percent of freight given up: 3 plus a random percent, +5 when the owner's notoriety toward the player exceeds 1000, capped at 99.
Owner loses the license after the surrender.

GetQuestion.doc: Answers the freight surrender question (10020) from a player or NPC asker arg3, for voiced pilots and question contexts 7 or 17. The asker's owner gets 1 notoriety. Illegal freight is dropped (reply 29), or the ship fights, or it gives up a percent of its freight and loses the license. Other questions go to the Ship base. Returns a reply code.

comments.text: this->CallForHelp: TSPirate overrides CallForHelp with an empty body, so pirates do not call for help through this path.

Hit.doc: When hit by an object of another owner (arg4), calls for help from its group (virtual call, so TSPirate's empty override applies), then the base Hit runs.

comments.text: Player ship in a station: command 0 (none).
Player ship elsewhere: command 17 (IDLE).
Docked at the target m42: command 0; otherwise RETURN_HOME (1) to it.

StartAction.doc: Chooses the idle action. Flag 4096 blocks it. A player-owned ship inside a station (class 2016) stops, otherwise it idles. Other ships return to their dock target m42 (command 1) or stop when already docked there or without a target. The home sector is stored in m43.

2038.name: TradeShip

2039.doc: Goner Ship (page 2006), a Little Ship subclass that escalates in six steps (m48) against the player and answers hail and surrender questions with lines 90 to 97.

comments.text: Message 91 on the first non-enemy attack.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler with six escalation steps in m48. The player's attack goes to step 1 (message 91) or 2 (enemy). Steps 2 to 4 send messages 92 and 94, step 5 calls for help when attacked, step 6 is reached when the shield falls under 1/8 of max.

Create.doc: Initializes the ship through the Moveable Ship base, marks race 8 ships with flag 134217728 in m12 and sets the owner from the race table. Unlike Fighter, sets no formation type.

comments.text: Text 18:10021 'Surrender!'.

GetAnswers.doc: For reply 90 adds 'Surrender!' (10021). Player-owned ships get none.

GetQuestion.doc: Hail (question 0) gets reply 95 when the asker is an enemy, else 90. Question 10021 gets reply 96 when not escalated or in the home sector, else 97. Returns nothing for the player's ship and for other contexts.

GetQuestionArray.doc: Returns the voice and the question id as the line list for a question. Player-owned ships get none.

comments.text: Command 27 (page 2008 name COMMAND_PREACH).

StartAction.doc: Idle action: docked ships stop (command 0); player ships idle (command 17); others run command 27 (named COMMAND_PREACH on page 2008, probably a leftover name). Flag 4096 blocks it.

2039.name: GonerShip

204.doc: Helper for ship destruction. Probably called from the death code of ship objects (class 2004). A dying ship first flies to a random grave point and then either jumps away and self-destructs or explodes; the choice is random. Holds no fields.

AbandonShip.doc: Stub. Abandoning a ship is not implemented in this script.

DeallocShip.doc: Destroys a ship with a random death: fly to the grave, then either jumpdrive out and self-destruct, or explode. Runs as a forked task.

Explode.doc: Shows a dummy explosion on the ship's game object, then self-destructs it after 1 second in a forked task.

comments.text: random grave point: a span of about 705 million units, half of it on each side of the centre
poll the command every 5000 time units

FlyShipToGrave.doc: Orders the ship to fly (command 19) to a random point around the sector centre and waits until the command ends.

comments.text: self-destruct reason 17 with no killer (same reason code as the silent destruction in the ware code)

JumpdriveAndDestroy.doc: Plays jumpdrive effect 46 on the ship if it has a game object, then self-destructs it after 1 second in a forked task.

SellShipToFreetrader.doc: Stub. Selling a dying ship to a freetrader is not implemented in this script.

204.name: ShipDisposal

2042.doc: A Goner dock (page 2006: Goner Dock). Adds one behaviour: when it is attacked it passes the attack on to a random other dock of the sector, so the Goners can retaliate from any of their docks.

AttackedBy.doc: Notifies listeners and forwards the attack to a random other dock in the same sector.

2042.name: GonerDock

2043.doc: A nebula in a sector (GType 21). Has an inner and outer range, fog settings, dust particles and optional gameplay effects: shield reduction, hull damage and visibility reduction. The DoNebulaEffect task damages objects inside while the effect values are non-zero.

0.doc: radius where the full effect applies, default 5,000,000
0.name: innerRange

1.doc: radius where the effect fades out, default 7,500,000
1.name: outerRange

10.doc: visibility reduction strength (0 = none)
10.name: visibilityReduction

2.doc: body index used for the outer shell
2.name: outerBodyIndex

3.doc: fog near distance
3.name: fogNear

4.doc: fog far distance
4.name: fogFar

5.doc: colour hue shift
5.name: hueModifier

6.doc: array of 8 dust body spawn rates
6.name: dustBodyRates

7.doc: number of dust particle instances
7.name: numDustInstances

8.doc: shield drain strength (0 = none)
8.name: shieldReduction

9.doc: hull damage strength (0 = none)
9.name: hullReduction

Activate.doc: Creates the engine nebula with all properties and starts it in space.

AddTo.doc: Adds the nebula to a sector through AddNebula and activates it when the sector has a native object id.

Create.doc: Creates a nebula; starts the effect task if it damages shields or hull.

Deactivate.doc: Saves position and frees the engine object.

Destruct.doc: Removes the nebula from its sector, then runs the base destruct.

comments.text: short period when the player sector or an updating sector
random shield drain proportional to strength
StartKilled(3, 0): player killed by the nebula

DoNebulaEffect.doc: Effect loop (4.5 s period in the player's/active sector, 30 s elsewhere). For ships, stations and flying wares between inner and outer range, with strength fading linearly outside the inner range, it randomly drains shields and damages the hull; kills the player if hull reaches 0.

GetDustBodyRate.doc: Returns the dust body rate for one of the 8 dust body slots.

GetDustBodyRateArray.doc: Returns the table of 8 dust body rates (field 13). It is read per index by the galaxy export.

GetFogFar.doc: Returns the far fog distance of the nebula (field 11).

GetFogNear.doc: Returns the near fog distance of the nebula (field 10).

GetGSize.doc: Returns the game size. It is the same field as GetSize (field 8).

GetHueModifier.doc: Returns the hue modifier of the nebula (field 12).

GetHullReduction.doc: Returns the hull reduction of the nebula (field 16).

GetInnerRange.doc: Returns the inner range of the nebula (field 7).

GetName.doc: Returns the constant name NEBULA.

GetNumDustInstances.doc: Returns the number of dust instances (field 14).

GetOuterBodyIndex.doc: Returns the index of the outer body of the nebula (field 9).

GetOuterRange.doc: Returns the outer range of the nebula (field 8).

GetShieldReduction.doc: Returns the shield reduction of the nebula (field 15).

comments.text: size and outer range share field 8 (probable copy of the same value)

GetSize.doc: Returns the nebula size. It is the same field as the outer range (field 8).

GetTypeCode.doc: Returns 1376256, which is 21 << 16: the nebula type code.

GetVisibilityReduction.doc: Returns the visibility reduction of the nebula (field 17).

Remove.doc: Deactivates the nebula if active, then removes it from its sector.

SelfDestruct.doc: Destroys the nebula: kills its native object with the given arguments when active, then runs the destruct.

SetDustBodyRate.doc: Sets the spawn rate for one dust body index.

SetFogFar.doc: Sets the far distance of the nebula fog.

SetFogNear.doc: Sets the near distance of the nebula fog.

SetHueModifier.doc: Sets the hue modifier of the nebula colours.

SetHullReduction.doc: Sets the hull reduction value of the nebula.

SetInnerRange.doc: Sets the inner range value of the nebula (GetInnerRange returns it).

SetNumDustInstances.doc: Sets the number of dust instances drawn for the nebula.

SetOuterBodyIndex.doc: Sets the outer body index of the nebula (GetOuterBodyIndex returns it).

SetOuterRange.doc: Sets the outer radius of the nebula. The size reported by GetSize equals this value.

SetShieldReduction.doc: Sets the shield reduction value of the nebula.

SetVisibilityReduction.doc: Sets the visibility reduction value of the nebula.

2043.name: Nebula

2044.doc: Factory complex hub (dobj: Obj_2044, no page name). Groups a set of member factories that are linked by factory connections (SA_CreateFactoryConnections) and acts as their complex hangar. On destruction, money and stock are shared back to the members. Derives from Factory (2006).

0.doc: table of member factory objects in the complex
0.name: factories

1.doc: connection records [parent, child, connector points...] (dobj var_2044_1)
1.name: connections

2.doc: per-ware sum of member best store values
2.name: wareBestStoreSum

comments.text: connections are processed from the last to the first
spawn connector helper only when the object was created
flags 1 and 144 on connector helpers: make them non-findable and keep them in space

ActivateConnections.doc: Links the connection objects: with arg1 true also spawns connector helper objects (type 20) at each stored connector point, then sets each child factory's connection parent.

AddDefaultProductsAndResources.doc: Empty override: the complex starts with no default products.

CanBuyIntermediates.doc: True when the complex buys intermediate products (bit 4096 of field 15, probably).

CanSellIntermediates.doc: True when the complex sells intermediate products (bit 8192 of field 15, probably).

CanSellWareType.doc: True when the complex sells the ware (product table m49 or m52).

comments.text: any member without resources: the complex is short too

CheckNoResources.doc: Sets flag 2 when any member factory has no resources, else clears it. Also sets or clears ship flag 32768 to match.

comments.text: disconnects the hub's tractor from its own connection first
fails when a member is itself a complex or already in one
for each member: move its money to the hub and free its stock
product keys become hub products; a key present on both sides is shared
stop all of the member's script tasks
activate the connection objects and check resources

CreateConnections.doc: Builds the complex from a table of factories: checks they are not already in a complex, creates factory connections, and moves stock, money, products and resources into the hub. Returns 1 on success.

Deactivate.doc: Stores the position of each connector helper, frees the helper objects, then runs the station Deactivate.

comments.text: money is divided equally; the rest goes to the first member
stock is returned to the members that produce or use each ware
docked ships and owned ships are moved to a random member; m16/m21 lists are reassigned

DestroyConnections.doc: Kills the connector helpers and splits the hub's money and stock among the member factories, then clears the complex. Members are moved to random remaining members.

GetConnectionParent.doc: Returns the parent factory of a member factory, from the connection records, or nothing.

GetConnections.doc: Returns the connections between the member factories (field 72).

GetFactories.doc: Returns the member factories of the factory complex (field 71).

GetWareTypeBestStore.doc: Best store of a ware summed over the member factories (m72).

GetWareTypePrice.doc: Price of a ware. Player-owned complexes and pseudo wares use the factory price. Others use the average price adjusted by the stock level.

KilledBy.doc: On destruction by an attacker, destroys the connection helpers once (bit 31 guards re-entry) and then runs the station KilledBy.

NoResources.doc: True when flag 2 (no resources) is set.

Production.doc: Empty override: production runs in the member factories.

SelfDestruct.doc: Self-destruct of the complex: sets bit 31, destroys the connections, then runs the station SelfDestruct.

SetBuyIntermediates.doc: Sets flag 4096: the complex buys intermediate wares for its members.

SetNoResources.doc: Forces the no-resources state: sets flag 2 and ship flag 32768.

SetSellIntermediates.doc: Sets flag 8192: the complex sells intermediate wares from its members.

StartTasks.doc: Empty override: the complex runs no tasks of its own.

Trade.doc: Empty override: trade runs in the member factories.

comments.text: flag 4096 adds the intermediate list to the resource station update

UpdateGalaxyWareStation.doc: Registers the complex's buy and sell lists with the galaxy ware station (C300), including intermediates when flags 4096 and 8192 are set.

2044.name: FactoryComplex

2046.doc: Player headquarters (class key 'hq' in addon/types/hq.xml; GetClassCode text 1263:19705 'HQ'). A Dock (2007) subclass with upgrade levels read from hq.xml. Runs the player's production, reverse engineering, repair and recycling queues, and holds save, spray and loadout helpers. g8 keeps the single HQ reference (GetHeadquarters). No dobj name.

0.doc: upgrade levels from hq.xml: [subType, cargo size, blueprints, production, repair, reverse, recycle factors]
0.name: upgradeTable

1.doc: current upgrade level index into upgradeTable, -1 when unset
1.name: upgradeIndex

10.doc: game age when the current production started
10.name: productionStart

11.doc: time of the current production in ms
11.name: productionTime

12.doc: units produced in the current production step
12.name: productionCount

13.doc: objects waiting for reverse engineering
13.name: reverseQueue

14.doc: 1 while the reverse loop runs
14.name: reverseActive

15.doc: script task id of the reverse loop
15.name: reverseTaskId

16.doc: main type of the object being reversed, -1 when idle
16.name: reverseMainType

17.doc: subtype of the object being reversed, -1 when idle
17.name: reverseSubType

18.doc: game age when the current reverse started
18.name: reverseStart

19.doc: time of the current reverse in ms
19.name: reverseTime

2.doc: cargo volume used by stock, excluding pseudo wares
2.name: totalVolume

20.doc: objects waiting for repair, the HQ itself included
20.name: repairQueue

22.doc: script task id of the repair loop
22.name: repairTaskId

24.doc: game age when the current repair started
24.name: repairStart

25.doc: time of the current repair in ms
25.name: repairTime

26.doc: hull percent points repaired in the current step
26.name: repairCount

29.doc: script task id of the recycle loop
29.name: recycleTaskId

3.doc: resource ware key to factor table, from hq.xml resources
3.name: resourceFactors

30.doc: main type of the object being recycled, -1 when idle
30.name: recycleMainType

31.doc: subtype of the object being recycled, -1 when idle
31.name: recycleSubType

32.doc: game age when the current recycle started
32.name: recycleStart

33.doc: time of the current recycle in ms
33.name: recycleTime

35.doc: save-game option bits, bits 0-2 set by default
35.name: saveFlags

37.doc: save name; Create initialises it with an unresolved call
37.name: saveName

38.doc: table set in Create; no reader in this batch, probably loadout data
38.name: loadoutSlots

4.doc: ware keys this HQ can produce, filled from the upgrade level
4.name: blueprints

41.doc: copy of the default save flags bits 0-2; no reader in this batch
41.name: defaultSaveFlags

5.doc: queued production items [mainType, subType, count]
5.name: productionQueue

6.doc: 1 while the production loop runs
6.name: productionActive

7.doc: script task id of the production loop
7.name: productionTaskId

8.doc: main type of the item in production, -1 when idle
8.name: productMainType

9.doc: subtype of the item in production, -1 when idle
9.name: productSubType

comments.text: only wares with a non-zero production factor for the current level become blueprints

AddBlueprints.doc: Adds a blueprint for a ware if the current upgrade gives it a production factor and it is not known yet.

AddLoadout.doc: Creates a loadout record [name, type, wares] in the table m91 and returns its id.

comments.text: same blueprint as the last item: add to its count instead of a new entry
negative count removes instead

AddProductionItem.doc: Adds units of a blueprint to the production queue at a position (-1 or past the end appends). A count below zero removes units. Merges with a neighbouring item of the same blueprint.

AddRecycleItem.doc: Adds an object to the recycle queue at a position (appends when out of range).

AddRepairItem.doc: Adds an object to the repair queue at a position (appends when out of range).

AddResources.doc: Adds a resource table to stock; credits (1048655) go to money.

AddReverseItem.doc: Adds an object to the reverse queue at a position (appends when out of range).

comments.text: g46 bit 1 marks pseudo wares, which take no cargo space

AddWare.doc: Adds a ware through the dock and, for stored wares (pseudo wares excluded), adds its volume to totalVolume.

comments.text: loadout wares leave the dock stock; flag 1 wares are not stock-tracked
the ship's upgrade wares (flag 8) are not returned to the dock
upgrades: only the missing part is installed and paid for
remaining ship wares go back to the dock
flag 1 wares given back to the dock are paid out at the average price

ApplyLoadout.doc: Applies a loadout to a ship after CheckLoadout passes: moves the wares between the dock and the ship, installs upgrades and pays for them. Returns 0 on success or the CheckLoadout code.

CanBeRecycled.doc: True when the object is in this HQ, owned by the player, not the player ship, not invincible or unsellable, has a recycle factor for the current level, and is not the repair target. With ignoreQueue false it must also not be queued.

CanBeRepaired.doc: True when the object is this HQ or inside it, owned by the player, below max hull, and has a repair factor for the current level. With ignoreQueue false it must also not be queued.

comments.text: player ship (g9) and invincible objects cannot be reversed

CanBeReversed.doc: True when the object is in this HQ, owned by the player, not the player ship, not invincible or unsellable, its blueprint is unknown, it is not the current reverse or repair target, and it has a factor for the reverse operation. With ignoreQueue false it must also not already be queued.

comments.text: precedence as written: (object && exists) || class 2004

CanBeSaved.doc: True when the object is a ship in this HQ, owned by the player. The condition checks the object and then its class (2004 ship); the grouping of || is as written.

comments.text: key 459124 = type 7 subtype 372 cannot be sprayed

CanBeSprayed.doc: True when the object is in this HQ, owned by the player, and is not type 7 subtype 372 and not of default race 2.

comments.text: code 1: not a ship object (class 2004)
code 2: subtype does not match the loadout type
code 3: wares missing in the dock
code 4: volume mismatch
code 5: money

CheckLoadout.doc: Checks whether a loadout can be applied to a ship. Returns nothing when it can; otherwise a code: 1 not a ship, 2 wrong ship type, 3 wares missing, 4 not enough cargo space, 5 not enough money.

comments.text: wareKey packs main type << 16 | subtype
upgrades (g46 flag 8) cost the price of the missing upgrades
other flag 1 wares are priced at the average price

CheckLoadoutMoney.doc: Money the ship lacks to pay for a loadout's upgrades and priced wares, minus the allowance in field m30. Returns 0 when the ship can pay.

comments.text: adds min(volume in stock, wanted count): mixes a volume and a count, probably a bug
positive: volume beyond the ship's free space
negative branch uses the dock's free space (no ship argument), unlike the positive branch: probably inconsistent

CheckLoadoutSpace.doc: Volume mismatch of a loadout swap. Positive: the ship cannot take the wares; negative: the dock cannot take the ship's wares back. Zero when it fits.

comments.text: flag 256: loadout type is not checked

CheckLoadoutType.doc: True if the ship's subtype matches the loadout type. Flag 256 skips the check. Returns nothing for a non-ship or an unknown loadout.

comments.text: main type 9 needs filter bit 1
main type 8 needs filter bit 2
main type 10 needs filter bit 4
g46 category 2048 needs filter bit 8
g46 category 8 needs filter bit 32
g46 category 1 needs filter bit 16
all other wares need filter bit 64

CheckLoadoutWareFlags.doc: True if a ware passes the category filter bits arg3. Wares of main type 8, 9 or 10 use fixed bits; other wares use the category flags of table g46.

comments.text: flag 512 skips the ware check
wares with g46 flag 1 are not checked against stock

CheckLoadoutWares.doc: Wares the ship (dock) still lacks for a loadout, multiplied by count arg3. Returns a table of missing amounts, empty when all are present. Flag 512 skips the check.

comments.text: bits 0-2 of saveFlags and defaultSaveFlags are set to 1
reads addon/types/hq.xml; the upgrade table comes from it
match the upgrade by subtype; if none matches, upgradeIndex stays -1 (see GetTradeContainerSize)

Create.doc: Creates the HQ through the dock Create, resets all queues and flags, loads hq.xml, and selects the upgrade whose subtype equals the given subType.

Destruct.doc: Clears the player's HQ reference if it is this object, stops all work queues and runs the dock Destruct.

comments.text: 'hq' maps to 2046 itself; keys m1-m8 map to the 2021-2027 and 2142 classes

EvalClass.doc: Maps a class key from hq.xml (hq, dock, factory, station, m1-m8, ts, tp, tm, tl, gonership, fighter, freighter, carrier, littleship, bigship, hugeship, ship) to a class id. Unknown keys return nothing.

EvalRaceMask.doc: Parses a pipe-separated race list (argon|boron|...) into a bit mask: argon 2, boron 4, split 8, paranid 16, teladi 32, xenon 64, khaak 128, pirate 256, goner 512, atf 131072, terran 262144, yaki 524288. Empty input returns nothing.

EvalTypeList.doc: Parses a pipe-separated list of ship or ware type names into a table keyed by type code.

FilterLoadoutWares.doc: Subset of a wares table whose entries pass CheckLoadoutWareFlags with the given filter bits.

GetAllLoadoutIDs.doc: Returns the keys of the loadout table (field 92).

comments.text: time (1048599) is not a cost, it is handled by GetBaseTime

GetBaseResources.doc: Resource cost table of an HQ operation, keyed by ware key. The time pseudo ware is skipped.

GetBaseTime.doc: Time of an HQ operation in ms: the time resource value times 1000.

GetBlueprintCount.doc: Count used for a blueprint operation: always 100.

GetBlueprintProducts.doc: Output units of one blueprint run: 1 when known, nothing otherwise.

GetBlueprintResources.doc: Resource cost of a blueprint's production with blueprint count 100, or nothing when the blueprint is unknown.

GetBlueprintTable.doc: Returns the blueprint table (field 58), keyed by main type << 16 | subtype.

GetBlueprintTime.doc: Production time of a blueprint in ms (blueprint count 100), or nothing when unknown.

GetClassCode.doc: Returns the HQ text 1263:19705 ('HQ') as the class name.

GetCurrentProductionStart.doc: Returns the start time of the current production (field 64).

GetCurrentProductionTime.doc: Time of the production run in progress, in seconds.

GetCurrentRecycleStart.doc: Returns the start time of the current recycle item (field 86).

comments.text: field 87 is in milliseconds; divided by 1000

GetCurrentRecycleTime.doc: Returns the time of the current recycle item in seconds (field 87).

GetCurrentRepairCount.doc: Returns the count of the current repair (field 80).

GetCurrentRepairStart.doc: Returns the start time of the current repair (field 78).

comments.text: field 79 is in milliseconds; divided by 1000

GetCurrentRepairTime.doc: Returns the time of the current repair in seconds (field 79).

GetCurrentReverseStart.doc: Returns the start time of the current reverse item (field 72).

comments.text: times are stored in milliseconds and divided by 1000

GetCurrentReverseTime.doc: Returns the time of the current reverse item in seconds.

GetFactorPrimary.doc: Primary flag of the first matching factor (the ware is the main input or output of the operation).

GetFactorValue.doc: Value of the first matching factor, or 1 when the value field is zero; 0 if nothing matches.

GetLoadoutFlags.doc: Returns the flags of the current loadout (field 95).

GetLoadoutIDsByType.doc: Ids of all loadouts whose type (element 1 of the record) equals the argument. Returns an array.

GetLoadoutName.doc: Name of a loadout (element 0), or an empty string if the id is unknown.

GetLoadoutShips.doc: Ships of the dock's owner (from GetShips) that pass CheckLoadout for this loadout. Returns a table keyed by ship.

GetLoadoutType.doc: Type of a loadout (element 1), or 0 if the id is unknown.

GetLoadoutWares.doc: Wares of a loadout (element 2) filtered by the category flags arg2. Returns an empty table if the loadout is unknown or has no wares.

GetNumBlueprints.doc: Returns the number of known blueprints (size of table 58).

GetNumLoadouts.doc: Returns the number of loadouts in table 92.

GetNumProductionItems.doc: Returns the number of items in the production queue (field 59).

GetNumRecycleItems.doc: Number of recycle queue items after removing those that cannot be recycled.

GetNumRepairItems.doc: Number of repair queue items after removing those that cannot be repaired.

comments.text: the reverse queue is refreshed before it is counted

GetNumReverseItems.doc: Returns the number of items in the reverse queue (field 67) after updating it.

GetNumUpgrades.doc: Returns the number of upgrades (size of the array in field 54).

GetProductMainType.doc: Returns the main type of the current production (field 62).

GetProductSubType.doc: Returns the subtype of the current production (field 63).

GetProductionCount.doc: Output units of the current production item.

GetProductionItemCount.doc: Returns the count of production queue item index, or nothing when index is out of range.

GetProductionItemMax.doc: Queue limit for an item: 10 runs' worth of output.

GetProductionItemProducts.doc: Returns the products of the blueprint of production queue item index, or nothing when index is out of range.

GetProductionItemSubType.doc: Returns the subtype of production queue item index, or nothing when index is out of range.

GetProductionItemType.doc: Returns the main type of production queue item index, or nothing when index is out of range.

GetProductionResourcePercent.doc: Resource coverage percent of the first production queue item, or nothing when the queue is empty.

GetProductionResources.doc: Resource cost of one production run of a blueprint.

GetProductionTime.doc: Production time of the current item in seconds (m64 / 1000).

GetRecyclableObjects.doc: Table of ships in this HQ that CanBeRecycled accepts.

GetRecycleCount.doc: Hull percent of the object; the recycle count scales with it.

GetRecycleItem.doc: Returns recycle queue item index (field 81), or nothing when index is out of range.

GetRecycleMainType.doc: Returns the main type of the current recycle item (field 84).

GetRecycleResources.doc: Resource cost recovered when the object is recycled: operation 6 with count = hull percent. Note that recycling returns these resources, it does not pay them.

GetRecycleSubType.doc: Returns the subtype of the current recycle item (field 85).

GetRecycleTime.doc: Recycle time in ms (operation 6, count = hull percent), or nothing.

GetRepairCount.doc: Hull percent points missing on the object (100 minus hull percent).

GetRepairItem.doc: Returns repair queue item index (field 74), or nothing when index is out of range.

GetRepairResourcePercent.doc: Resource coverage of the first repair queue item, or nothing when the queue is empty.

GetRepairResources.doc: Resource cost to repair the object (operation 4, count = missing hull percent), or nothing.

GetRepairTime.doc: Repair time in ms for an object (operation 4, missing hull percent), or nothing.

GetRepairableObjects.doc: Table of repairable objects: this HQ and ships inside it, filtered by CanBeRepaired.

comments.text: key 1048655 (credits) uses the money count m30 instead of stock

GetResourcePercent.doc: Percent of a resource table covered by stock (credits counted from money). Returns 100 when fully covered and nothing when the table is empty.

comments.text: key 1048599 = time pseudo ware 16:23: scale from the time field, factor divided by 60
primary factor: the result is at least 1
any zero input gives no cost

GetResourceValue.doc: Resource cost of one HQ operation for a ware, from the price average, the factor values and the operation percent. Operation: 3 blueprint, 4 repair, 5 reverse, 6 recycle. The time resource (1048599) is divided by 60.

comments.text: constant 100 (probably the maximum count of one reverse order)

GetReverseCount.doc: Returns the count limit of a reverse item. Always 100 in this script.

GetReverseItem.doc: Returns reverse queue item index, or nothing when index is out of range.

GetReverseMainType.doc: Returns the main type of the current reverse item (field 70).

GetReverseResources.doc: Resource cost of reverse engineering the object (repairable check, count 100), or nothing. Not used by Reverse itself (see its comments).

GetReverseSubType.doc: Returns the subtype of the current reverse item (field 71).

GetReverseTime.doc: Reverse engineering time in ms for an object, or nothing if it cannot be reversed.

GetReversibleObjects.doc: Table of ships in this HQ that CanBeReversed accepts.

GetSavableShips.doc: Table of ships in this HQ that CanBeSaved accepts.

GetSaveName.doc: Returns the name of the saved item (field 91).

GetSaveObject.doc: Returns the object used for saving (field 90).

GetSprayHue.doc: Hue modifier of the spray object, wrapped to 0-359 degrees.

GetSprayObject.doc: Returns the object used for spraying (field 88).

GetSpraySaturation.doc: Saturation of the spray object, decoded from the stored value (divide by 256, minus 256).

GetSprayableObjects.doc: Table of ships in this HQ that can be sprayed.

GetTotalVolume.doc: Returns the total volume value (field 56, probably of the stored wares).

GetTradeContainerFree.doc: Free cargo volume: container size minus totalVolume.

GetTradeContainerSize.doc: Cargo volume of the current upgrade level. Fails with an index error when upgradeIndex is -1 (see Create).

GetUpgradeIndex.doc: Returns the index of the current upgrade (field 55).

GetWareTypeBestStore.doc: Best storage amount for a ware, taken from the trade store calculation.

GetWareTypeContainerSize.doc: Stock count plus free space for a ware.

GetWareTypeCount.doc: Units of a ware held. Credits (16:79, key 1048655) return the money count (m30), other wares the dock count.

comments.text: key 1048655 = credits pseudo ware 16:79

GetWareTypeFree.doc: Free units of a ware. For credits (16:79, key 1048655) this is 2000000000 minus the money count; other wares use free cargo volume divided by ware volume.

comments.text: pseudo wares (credits, time) are unlimited

GetWareTypeMaxStore.doc: Maximum units of a ware that fit: pseudo wares 1000000; stock wares container size divided by ware volume.

Production.doc: Production loop. StopRecycling.doc: Stops recycling, clears its fields and kills its task.

StopRepairing.doc: Stops repair, clears its fields and kills its task.

StopReversing.doc: Stops reverse engineering and kills its task.

StopTasks.doc: Stops trading, production, reverse, repair and recycle.

Named 'Astronaut' via text 35:1100061.

Invincible astronauts keep the timer running at 0 instead of dying.

IsAvailableForDefaultJob.doc: Never available for the default job.

IsCapturable.doc: Always false: astronauts cannot be captured.

IsInvincible.doc: True when the Ship base says so, or when the parent ship m97 (the ship that launched it) is invincible.

IsMarine.doc: True when entry 11 of the ship table m18 is positive (the astronaut is a boarding marine).

Voice line 102 when the run starts.
SA_MovePosContinue to a random point within 500 units of the target.

100 ms later the followers and this astronaut self-destruct (reason 17).

MoveToBoard.doc: Boarding run: the astronaut (and optional followers in arg2, which are sent with MoveToBoardFollower) flies to a random point near the target arg1 and cuts through its hull. Voice lines 101 and 102 are played. Pilot speakers become marines: an existing pilot speaker is used, otherwise a new marine object (class 1700) is trained. Marines are sent with MarinesCutThroughHull. The astronaut and its followers self-destruct after 100 ms. If the target is gone, the astronaut returns home and the music changes.

OnContextMenuUpdateInfo.doc: For the player's astronaut adds the info line 'Supply: O2 n%' (text 35:1102400 'Supply'). Otherwise the Ship base updates the menu.

SetMarineName.doc: Appends the marine kind name (ware 16, subtype 107) to the astronaut name: 'Name (Kind)'.
