Destruct.doc: Removes the fly from the custom galaxy-object list of its sector, then runs the base Destruct.

GetAnswers.doc: Returns 0: no answers are available.

comments.text: class code 'LI' (lifeform)

GetClassCode.doc: Returns the class code text: 'LI' (lifeform, text 1263:19700).

GetDetailsMenu.doc: Returns menu class 2323, the details menu of space flies.

GetWareTypeCode.doc: Returns 1048581, which is 16 << 16 | 5: the ware type code of a space fly.

Hit.doc: Empty override: space flies take no hit through this hook.

IsAvailableForDefaultJob.doc: Returns 0: space flies do not take a default job.

comments.text: killed by a space fly: no death handling (no chain)
destroyed through Destruct

KilledBy.doc: Death handler. A fly killed by another space fly is ignored. Otherwise notifies listeners, kills the native object, detaches from formation and patrol lists and destroys the object.

comments.text: info line text: subtype name and ware volume

OnContextMenuUpdateInfo.doc: Adds a line with the ware subtype name and its volume to the info panel for the owner's view; otherwise calls the base.

Remove.doc: Removes the space fly: deactivates it when active, then removes it from the custom galaxy object table of its environment.

Repair.doc: Empty override: space flies are not repaired through this hook.

comments.text: listeners get the reason code, except for reason 11
signal killed with no killer

SelfDestruct.doc: Destroys the fly with an explicit reason code arg1 (17 means it was collected). Notifies the collector and listeners as needed.

SendMessage.doc: Empty override: space flies do not receive messages.

comments.text: stop tracking this fly in the main monitor if it was tracked
close the container window if it shows this fly
a newly disabled fly is checked by the space-fly manager (C205)
hidden when not disabled (arg = 0), so the fly is visible only while disabled

SetDisabled.doc: Disables or re-enables the fly. A disabled fly is visible and can be looted; an enabled one is hidden.

StartAction.doc: Starts the default command 17 unless flag 4096 (no default action) is set.

2070.name: SpaceFly

2073.doc: A big ship (page 2006: Big Ship), a moveable ship that can own other ships and be boarded by marines. Base of the carrier (2033) and class 2142. Created by Create with an owner index into g7. Holds the owned-ship table and the boarding state (marines inside, marines on the way).

0.doc: table of ships owned by this ship
0.name: ownedShips

1.doc: probably count of owned fighters, reset on create and destroy
1.name: ownedFighterCount

2.doc: probably count of owned freighters, reset on create and destroy
2.name: ownedFreighterCount

4.doc: speaker objects (marines, pilots) contained in this ship; they can talk
4.name: speakerObjects

5.doc: table of marines currently boarding this ship
5.name: boardingMarines

6.doc: table of marines on their way to board this ship
6.name: incomingMarines

7.doc: owner object of the first marine that started boarding
7.name: boardingAttackerShip

8.doc: owner (faction) of the boarding attackers, probably
8.name: boardingAttackerOwner

AddSpeakerObj.doc: Adds speaker object arg1 to the front of the speaker list and makes this ship its container.

AddWare.doc: Adds arg3 units of ware arg1/arg2 to cargo. Forwards to the parent class.

AllowBoardingStartVoice.doc: Clears flag 262144 in m13 so that the boarding-start voice can play again.

AllowHullCuttingAgain.doc: Clears flag 65536 in m13 so that the hull-cutting announcement can play again.

CanGetMonitorControl.doc: True when the ship exists and is owned by the player.

comments.text: threshold is halved (v1); the warning flag is cleared below threshold/4
speech 103 played for the player, once per shield rise

CheckBoardingShieldRise.doc: Warns once when the shields climb back above the boarding threshold. Flag 131072 in m13 is the warning state: it is cleared when the shields fall below a quarter of the threshold.

comments.text: speech 13/608: the player is told that the shields are still up

CheckBoardingShields.doc: Checks that the shields are down enough for boarding. If not, the attack is cancelled: the marines in arg2 are removed and destroyed, music is reset, and 0 is returned. arg3 is the speech flag for the player ship.

CheckForMarineEvacuation.doc: Starts the marine evacuation in a fork when the hull is at 5 percent or less. Returns 1 when the evacuation started, nothing otherwise.

comments.text: owner index 8 gets flag 134217728 (the flag is not set for class 2021 with zero max speed)
m17 = 3 (state of the ship is reset)
boarding is disabled for every owner except index 10

Create.doc: Creates the big ship on top of the moveable-ship create. arg5 is the owner index into g7; owner 8 sets flag 134217728 unless the ship is a class 2021 with zero max speed. Clears boarding tables; boarding is disabled unless owner index 10.

CreateBoardingLog.doc: Empty stub: the boarding log is not written in this version.

comments.text: invincible speakers (marines) are ejected from the ship, others are destroyed

Destruct.doc: Releases everything tied to this ship when it is destroyed: owned ships are told the owner is gone, contained speakers (marines, pilots) are ejected or destroyed, boarders are ejected, music is reset and incoming marines are stopped. Then calls the parent Destruct.

ExcuseOwnerShips.doc: Makes this ship and the owned ships of the same owner, which are enemies of the player, neutral to the player (relation 0) and forgives their followers.

comments.text: boarding speech line 305: hacking failed
speech 13/606 for the player when the attack failed

FailedHackingEvacuation.doc: Called when the hacking attempt of the boarders fails: part of the boarders is killed, the rest are turned into suits and leave, the boarding ends and music is reset. arg1 is the voice of the leading marine.

comments.text: node 102000: the request-for-help answer (10002) is offered to attacked ships of class 2021
answer 10011 (comm with person aboard) is offered when the asker's owner id bit matches the mask 918334
answer 10022 (request for help) is offered when flag 4 of m13 is set and no enemy is here

GetAnswers.doc: Appends the answer ids for dialog node arg1 to the answer array arg2 starting at index arg3, and returns the new index. arg4 is the asking object. Player-owned ships have no answers. Node 102999 lists the names of the people on board, sorted and without duplicates.

GetBoardingMarines.doc: Returns the number of marines boarding the ship (field 114, probably).

comments.text: questions 10008 (shipyard, class 2037) and 10009 (equipment dock, class 2075) search within 4 sectors
route answers need notoriety of at least 100 with the asker's owner
the target is within 7500000 units: a voice line plays after 100 ms and the player's monitor tracks it
surrender (10020): node 31 if hostile or notoriety below -10, otherwise node 30
help requests (10022): the title threshold is randomised, doubled when the ship is not attacked by the player
help granted: enemies of the same owner in the sector that can be forgiven become neutral

GetCapitalShipQuestion.doc: Answers for the capital-ship dialog: the way to the nearest shipyard or equipment dock (questions 10008 and 10009), surrender (10020) and help requests (10022). Refuses hostile askers, askers with notoriety below 100 for route answers, and makes ships of the same owner neutral when help is granted. Returns the next dialog node.

comments.text: owner index 6 defence: base defence plus 85 times the marine capacity

GetDefenceLevel.doc: Defence level against boarding: base defence, plus the fighting skill of the marines in passenger table m98. The owner index 6 gets a fixed bonus of 85 per marine capacity. Ware 16/103 (predefined) adds 200.

GetDustScene.doc: Big ships have no dust scene: always 0.

GetFormationDist.doc: Formation distance of the ship: 1.125 times its size (73728 / 65536 fixed point).

GetGSize.doc: Fixed galaxy size of a big ship: 50000.

GetGalaxyScene.doc: Big ships have no galaxy scene: always 0.

GetIncomingMarines.doc: Returns the number of marines on the way to board (field 115, probably).

GetMarinesAttackLevel.doc: Attack level of the marines currently boarding: sum of their fighting skills.

GetMarinesCanBoard.doc: How many more marines can board: capacity plus one, minus marines already on board.

GetMaxMarines.doc: Marine capacity of the ship: base value from the parent class, at least 8.

GetNumberAtkMarinesOnBoard.doc: Number of attacking marines inside the ship; nothing when the boarding table is empty.

GetOwnedShips.doc: Returns the table of owned ships.

comments.text: string question: a named speaker on board, or a menu choice from the open comm menu
the chosen speaker is put into the open menu as the target
a temporary marine (class 1700) is created to talk to the player and removed when the menu closes
text 18:10011 request comm with person aboard: node 102999 lists the speakers
text 18:10002 'Please help me, I am under attack': refused (102311) for enemies or negative notoriety; otherwise police support (102312) when the ship has police, costing the owner 1 notoriety

GetQuestion.doc: Dialog node for a question addressed to this ship. arg1 is the node kind (0 for the root menu), arg2 the question id or a chosen speaker's name, arg3 the asking object. Capital ships (classes 2142, 2141) use the parent. Returns a dialog node id such as 102311 (refused), 102312 (police support) or 102999 (speaker menu).

comments.text: route search from this sector to the question sector; -1 means no route, 0..5 is the direction

GetQuestionArray.doc: Returns the speech sequence (voice and text ids) for dialog node arg1. Route answers use the direction from the route search (GS_Route), giving text nodes 45..50.

GetSectorScene.doc: Big ships have no sector scene: always 0.

GetSize.doc: Size of the ship in the scene: total model size, or 50000 when there is no scene object.

GetSpeakerByName.doc: Finds a speaker in the speaker list (m112) whose pilot name is arg1. Falls back to the parent class lookup.

IsAvailableForDefaultJob.doc: Always 0: big ships never take a default job.

IsBeingBoarded.doc: True when marines are boarding this ship or are on their way to it.

IsCapturable.doc: True when the ship is owned by the free-ship owner g7[12], capture is not disabled, race logic allows control and the ship has no command.

MarineBeingSent.doc: Registers marine arg1 as heading to board this ship and points its board target at this ship.

comments.text: boarding refused (suit spawned) when no room is left or the marine belongs to the same owner

MarineBoardsShip.doc: Called when marine arg1 reaches this ship. If there is no room or the marine has the same owner, its suit is spawned instead. Otherwise the marine boards, and when this is the first boarder the boarding process starts after 10 seconds (arg2 false) or 2 seconds (arg2 true). Returns 1 when boarding started.

comments.text: boarding music track 8234 starts while the ship is not yet boarded
boarding by the player lowers the owner's notoriety by 30 percent
attackers become enemies (relation -1), the owner sends a squad and calls for help
ware 16/105 (predefined) raises the defence by 150 when on board
player statistic 8080 counts the marines that reached the hull
fast boarding doubles the attack value
both attack and defence get a random spread of 10 percent
marines lose when the attack value is below the defence: speech 13/111, marines respawn as suits
marines win: speech 13/108 and 13/109, then all marines board

MarinesCutThroughHull.doc: Runs the boarding sequence for the marine group arg1: the marines are sorted by mechanic skill, there are several timed checks with speech, and the defence of the ship is compared with the marines' mechanic skill. On success the marines board one by one. arg2 is fast boarding, arg3 the speech flag for the player ship.

PlayBoardingVoice.doc: Plays boarding voice line arg1 spoken by the voice of marine arg2. Only when the player is the boarding attacker (m116 == player) and in the same sector.

PlayBoardingVoiceHeavyDefence.doc: Plays one of the heavy-defence lines (206, 207, 208) with the voice of marine arg1.

PlayBoardingVoiceLostMarine.doc: Plays one of the lost-marine lines (203, 205, 208) with voice arg1.

PlayBoardingVoicePreparation.doc: Plays one of the preparation lines (201, 209, 212, 213, 214) with the voice of marine arg2. Line 202 is added when arg1 is 0, i.e. when marines are still inside.

PlayBoardingVoiceProgress.doc: Plays one of the progress lines (204, 210, 211, 215) with the voice of marine arg1.

PlayBoardingVoiceWithPage.doc: Plays boarding voice line arg2 with speaker voice arg1. Same player and sector conditions as PlayBoardingVoice.

RemoveMarineBeingSent.doc: Unregisters marine arg1 from the incoming table, clearing its board target. Drops the table when it becomes empty.

RemoveSpeakerObj.doc: Removes speaker arg1 from the speaker list and returns 1 when it was there. Non-negative ids are ignored. Other ids are passed to the parent class first.

comments.text: the attacking ship becomes an enemy
the attacker's ship sends a squad and calls for help
hull damage pool: 60 percent of max hull, split between the decks
player-led boarding: owner notoriety drops by 10 percent on every deck
deck attack value is reduced by the average engineering skill of the boarders
pause of 5 to 8 seconds between rounds
marines per round: capacity plus one spread over the decks, modified by the deck roll
attack-defence balance: far outweighed (over 2x capacity) changes the losses, far outweighed the other way causes the opposite
defence overwhelmingly stronger (over 20x capacity): heavy-defence voice line
per round: marines are picked for combat weighted by fighting skill and removed
freed passengers from the passenger table (m98) join the boarding fight
defence wins or no boarders remain: 10 percent of the boarders join the crew if there is space, the rest are destroyed
boarders won: start hacking the ship

RunBoardingProcess.doc: Runs the boarding fight over the ship's decks, one round per deck. Each round: hull damage from the attackers, a random number of marines is lost on each side, and the defence is compared with the marine attack level. If the boarders win, the ship is taken over with StartHacking. If the owner's side wins or the boarders are gone, the boarders are killed or rejoin the crew.

comments.text: pilot objects (class 2064) are never rebuilt

SetDisowned.doc: Removes ship arg1 from the owned table and decrements the fighter or freighter count (never below zero). If the ship was lost to an enemy and is marked for rebuild (rebuild flag), a replacement is created at the nearest shipyard of this ship's owner.

SetOwned.doc: Adds ship arg1 to the owned-ships table (m108) and counts it as a fighter (class 2034) or freighter. Marines (class 1700) and ships of other classes are ignored.

comments.text: owner 6: 80 percent chance to move, targets chosen from the sector size
build mode (C300.IsBuild) uses a random offset, otherwise the ship's start position m0
owner 7: 10 percent chance to stay put, otherwise a multiple of a quarter sector

StartAction.doc: Starts the default action of a big ship. Returns unless flag 4096 is set. Sets the home sector if needed. A ship already docked to the target runs its default command; other ships pick a movement target depending on their owner (type 6 and 7 use the sector size, and build mode uses a random offset).

comments.text: music track 8236 during hacking
statistic 8030 counts the two leading hackers
ware 16/102 (predefined) adds 70 to the hacking security, with an extra warning line
hack succeeds when the hacking skill reaches security, or with a 2 percent random chance
after the hack there is a 5 percent random failure check
statistic 8040 counts the two capturing hackers
ware 16/39 is granted once to the player on a captured ship (probably a trophy item)
statistic 8020 per boarder, and fighting skill rises by 5 to 9
speech 13/603: the sector where the ship was captured is named

StartHacking.doc: Last phase of a successful boarding: the boarders hack the ship's systems. Compares the best hacking skills of the two leading boarders with the ship's hacking security. On success the ship is captured (CaptureShip) and the boarders become its crew. Calls FailedHackingEvacuation on failure.

StartMarineEvacuation.doc: Evacuation sequence of the boarders when the hull is nearly destroyed: speech lines 401..404 with delays, then all boarders are turned into suits and leave, and music is reset.

StartReturnToHome.doc: Sends a ship that is not owned by the player back to its home sector m43 (command 12). Player-owned ships are not moved.

StopIncomingMarines.doc: Stops all marines on their way to this ship: those inside a marine container (class 2085) get their suits spawned. Clears the incoming table and resets music.

2073.name: BigShip

2074.doc: A Trade Dock (page 2006: Trade Dock). Behaves exactly as the base Dock; the class exists to be recognised by type checks (menus, trade lists).
2074.name: TradeDock

2075.doc: An Equipment Dock (page 2006: Equipment Dock). Behaviour comes from the base Dock, which treats this class specially: it buys and stores ship, laser and shield class wares (main types 8 to 10) without listing them as tradeables.
2075.name: EquipmentDock

2076.doc: A Pirate Dock (page 2006: Pirate Dock). The base Dock forces its owner to race 8 (pirates) and makes it neutral to race 10.
2076.name: PirateDock

2078.doc: A Kha'ak Dock (page 2006: Kha'ak Dock). The base Dock forces its owner to race 9 (Kha'ak).
2078.name: KhaakDock

2079.doc: Base class of satellites (GetClassCode 'SA'). A satellite is placed by a ware module, scans its sector for objects and is stationary. Subclasses are Nav. Satellite and Nav. Satellite MKII (page 2006), plus two variants. Owner race is set in Create2.

comments.text: flags2 bit 16 on the native object

Activate.doc: Activates the satellite: sets flag 16 in the native object's flags2 and disables the safe-position check.

AllowRaceLogicControl.doc: Returns 0: race logic does not control satellites.

CmdConsoleCommandExec.doc: Returns 0: no console command is executed.

CmdConsoleEntryExec.doc: Returns 0: no console entry is executed.

CollisionWarn.doc: Empty: satellites do not react to a collision warning.

comments.text: not placed in a safe position on activation
owner race from g7 by index arg6
equipment is added before the satellite joins the container

Create2.doc: Creates a satellite of ship type arg1 in container arg2 at the given position for owner race arg6. Activates and scans if a container was given.

CreateCommMenu.doc: Returns 0: satellites have no communication menu.

EquipOnEject.doc: Equips a satellite that is ejected from a ware module: one shield unit.

GetAnswers.doc: Returns 0: no answers are available.

comments.text: class code 'SA' (satellite)

GetCmdConsoleCommands.doc: Returns the incoming count unchanged: no console commands.

GetCmdConsoleEntries.doc: Adds no console entries. Returns the incoming count unchanged.

GetDetailsMenu.doc: Returns 0: satellites have no details menu.

GetScannerRange.doc: Returns 0: satellites have no scanner range in this script.

IsAvailableForDefaultJob.doc: Returns 0: satellites do not take a default job.

comments.text: scanner range from GetScannerRange()
lists: stations, stationary ships, asteroids, gates, flying wares
objects within range that are unknown and not hidden in the sector map become known

Scan.doc: Marks objects in scanner range as known. Only the player's satellites scan. Checks stations, stationary ships, asteroids, gates and flying wares of the sector.

SelfDestruct.doc: Destroys the satellite through the Ship implementation.

SendMessage.doc: Empty: satellites do not receive messages.

2079.name: Satellite

2080.doc: Improved navigation satellite (page 2006 'Nav. Satellite MKII'). Created by NavSatelliteMkIIWare. Uses ship type 278 and global parameter 8 for scanner range.

comments.text: ship type 278

Create.doc: Creates an MKII nav satellite (ship type 278) in the container at the position for the owner race.

GetDetailsMenu.doc: Returns menu class 2323, the details menu.

comments.text: SA_GetGlobalParameter(8, 0): scanner range

GetScannerRange.doc: Scanner range from the global parameter 8.

GetWareTypeCode.doc: Returns 1048621, which is 16 << 16 | 45: the ware type code of an improved navigation satellite.

2080.name: NavSatelliteMkII

2081.doc: Small Shipyard (page 2006: Small Shipyard). Shipyard subclass (2037) with no own fields or methods; its subclass 2086 exists.
2081.name: SmallShipyard

2082.doc: Big Shipyard (page 2006: Big Shipyard). Shipyard subclass (2037) with no own fields or methods; it differs only by its type data.
2082.name: BigShipyard

2084.doc: A ware (container) floating in space (page 2006: Ware in Space). Created when cargo is ejected or from scene files; has a ware type, an amount, hull points, and self-destructs after 15-45 minutes.

0.doc: number of units in the container
0.name: count

1.doc: ware main type
1.name: wareMainType

2.doc: ware sub type
2.name: wareSubType

3.doc: 1 while unknown to the player
3.name: notKnown

4.doc: current hull points
4.name: hull

5.doc: 1 no find, 4 hidden, 8 goodie, 16 invincible
5.name: flags

Activate.doc: Creates the engine object with the saved count, hull and flags and starts it in the sector at a safe position.

AddTo.doc: Adds the container to the sector's flying-ware list; activates it if the sector is active.

Create.doc: Creates a ware with full hull.

CreateEject.doc: Creates an ejected ware, adds it to a sector, starts its self-destruct timer and notifies the ejecting object's listeners (event 65536).

Deactivate.doc: Saves position and hull, then frees the engine object.

Destruct.doc: Removes the object from its sector's flying-ware list, then runs the base destructor.

FillContextMenu.doc: Adds the details button (601, text 35:812) when a details menu exists, then calls the base.

GetCount.doc: Returns the amount of the ware in this container (field 7).

GetDescriptionID.doc: Returns the description text id of the ware type and subtype.

GetDetailsMenu.doc: Menu id of the details menu (2323).

GetGSubType.doc: Returns the ware subtype (field 9) as the game subtype.

GetGType.doc: Returns the ware type (field 8) as the game type.

GetHull.doc: Hull value; reads it from the engine object when active.

GetHullPercent.doc: Hull as a percentage of max hull, 0 when max hull is 0.

GetMaxHull.doc: Max hull of the ware container type (m7, m8).

GetName.doc: Returns the name of the ware type and subtype.

GetNameID.doc: Returns the name text id of the ware type and subtype.

GetNoFind.doc: Flag bit 1 of m11: the object cannot be found by the finder.

GetSize.doc: Size of the engine object, or 1000 when inactive.

comments.text: ware key packed as type << 16 | subtype (type in field 8, subtype in field 9)

GetTypeCode.doc: Returns the ware key: type << 16 | subtype.

GetUnknown.doc: m9: the container is not yet known to the player.

GetWareTypeCode.doc: Returns the ware type code, the same as GetTypeCode.

Hit.doc: Applies damage: arg2 absolute (or arg1 if negative) plus arg3; destroys the ware 100 ms after hull reaches 0 unless invincible.

IsGoodie.doc: Flag bit 8 of m11: goodie (bonus pickup), probably.

IsHidden.doc: Flag bit 4 of m11: hidden object.

IsInvincible.doc: Flag bit 16 of m11: the container cannot be destroyed.

comments.text: no check for m3 here (SelfDestruct checks it); SA_KillObject may get 0 when inactive

KilledBy.doc: Destroys the container unless it is invincible (bit 16 of m11), then runs the base kill path.

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Opens the details menu for this container when item 601 is picked.

OnContextMenuUpdateInfo.doc: Info panel: tech class 'TC' and (for non-special wares) volume 'Vol', then the amount.

Remove.doc: Deactivates the container and removes it from the sector's flying-ware list.

SelfDestruct.doc: Kills the engine object if active and destroys the script object.

SetCount.doc: Sets the number of units in the container and updates the engine object.

SetHidden.doc: Hides the object on the map (flag 4, engine bit 16).

SetHull.doc: Sets hull clamped to 0..max and updates the engine; returns the new value.

SetHullPercent.doc: Sets hull from a percentage of max hull.

SetInvincible.doc: Sets the invincible flag (16, engine flags2 0x800000).

SetKnown.doc: Marks the container known (clears m9, engine flag 8) or unknown.

SetNoFind.doc: Sets or clears flag bit 1 of m11 (no-find).

SetTargeted.doc: When targeted and unknown, marks it known; then calls the base SetTargeted.

StartSelfDestructTimer.doc: Forks a task that destroys the ware after 15 to 45 minutes.

2084.name: WareInSpace

2085.doc: A decouple/boarding missile carrying marines (created from an engine SECOBID via CreateDecoupleMissile). Holds the marines on board, can eject them as marine suits (class 2064) and tracks the boarding target. Removes itself when empty.

0.doc: engine object subtype
0.name: subType

1.doc: table of marine objects on board
1.name: marines

2.doc: voice id of the marine leader
2.name: marineLeaderVoice

3.doc: ship being boarded
3.name: boardTarget

Activate.doc: Creates the engine object (type 10, subtype m6) in the sector at the stored position and attaches this script object as its event handler. Returns the engine object id or 0.

AddMarine.doc: Loads a marine into the pod (status 11).

AddTo.doc: Registers the pod in the sector's custom-object list and activates it if the sector is loaded.

comments.text: only the ship the pod was aimed at (boardTarget) can be boarded
target must be a Ship (class 2004) that allows boarding
never board a ship of the marines' own owner
marine table keys = marine objects; 1 = flag, m8 = marine leader voice (probably)

BoardTargetShip.doc: Called when this marine boarding pod touches its target. If the target is a boardable ship of a different owner than the pod's marines, the marines start cutting through its hull, then the pod's marine list is cleared.

CheckBoardingDistance.doc: For player marines: polls every 0.5 s; once the pod is within 500 m (distance/500 < 500) of the target plays the marine boarding voice (102).

ClearMarines.doc: Sets the carried marine count to zero.

Create.doc: Creates the pod at x,y,z with the given subtype.

CreateFromSECOBID.doc: Wraps an existing engine object (a launched pod) in the script object, placing it in the player's sector as a custom galaxy object.

Deactivate.doc: Stores the current position and frees the engine object.

Destruct.doc: Removes the pod from the sector and destroys the remaining marines.

EjectMarines.doc: Ejects each marine with 70% chance as a spacesuit.

GetClassCode.doc: Short class code text (page 1263) built from the pod's type/subtype.

GetDecoupleMissilesCutScene.doc: Cut-scene id used when this missile-type object is decoupled; the type's cut id plus one.

GetDescriptionID.doc: Returns the description text id of the ware type 10 and this subtype.

GetMarineLeaderVoice.doc: Returns the voice id of the marine leader of the pod (field 9, probably a speaker id).

GetName.doc: Returns the name of the ware type 10 and this subtype.

GetNameID.doc: Returns the name text id of the ware type 10 and this subtype.

comments.text: g7[12]: fallback owner, probably the unowned/neutral group

GetOwner.doc: Owner race of the engine object (looked up by its group), or the neutral owner g7[12] when the pod is not active.

GetSize.doc: Engine size when active, otherwise a fixed 1000.

comments.text: boarding pods are the ware type 10

GetType.doc: Returns the ware type code 10 (boarding pod).

GetTypeCode.doc: Type code: object type 10 in the high word, subtype in the low word.

GetUnknown.doc: Always 0: a pod is never an unidentified object.

comments.text: reason 2 = destroyed by damage

Hit.doc: Any hit destroys the pod after a short delay.

comments.text: voice 13:605, priority 99, when the marines belonged to the player

KilledBy.doc: The pod is destroyed: marines are ejected, and if the player's marines were aboard a voice line is played. Then the engine object is killed and the script object destroyed.

Remove.doc: Deactivates the pod and removes it from its sector's custom-object list.

RemoveMarine.doc: Removes a marine; the pod destroys itself when it is empty.

SelfDestruct.doc: Removes the pod without a kill credit.

SetBoardTarget.doc: Sets the ship this marine group will board.

SetMarineLeaderVoice.doc: Sets the voice id of the marine squad leader.

SetOwner.doc: No-op: this class does not store an owner.

SetPos.doc: Moves the pod. With an engine object the position is applied as a safe position and read back, otherwise the stored position array is written directly.

comments.text: stagger suits alternately left/right behind the pod
notify listeners (event 65536) about the new suit

SpawnMarineSuit.doc: Ejects a marine as a spacesuit pilot (ship class 2064, subtype 267) next to the pod and sends him home; removes him from the pod.

2085.name: BoardingPod

2086.doc: Small shipyard subclass (2081) with no own code of its own. Shipyard.GetWareTypeBestStore checks for this class and then uses the factory store logic (probably a small shipyard that keeps stock). No page 2006 name was found.
2086.name: SmallShipyardStocked

2092.doc: Freight drone (page 2006 names no class; the freight-drone menu is 2266). Ship type 294, carries wares in its own cargo and can unload them into a carrier. Created by FreightDroneWare; a lifetime counter ends it.

0.doc: task id of the lifetime loop, 0 when not running

comments.text: owner race loses 1 notoriety with the attacker's owner

AttackedByHandler.doc: The player's own drone ignores attacks. A hostile attack from the player costs the owner race notoriety and its license with the player.

AllowBoarding.doc: Sets or clears the 'boarding allowed' flag (16384), allowing invincible ships to be boarded.

CanBeBoarded.doc: True if the ship may be boarded: not a Khaak-type (race 7 default) ship, must be a BigShip, must be able to move, not invincible unless boarding is allowed, and must have decks.

CanLaunchMarines.doc: True if the ship can launch boarding pods: type 262, or marine capable carriers (class 2026, 2030).

CanWeBoard.doc: True if this ship has marines and can launch them.

CheckValidBoardingTarget.doc: Checks all conditions for boarding a target: marines available, target exists and is a ship of another owner, can be boarded, neither docked, same sector, within 1500 km plus ship sizes, shields low enough. Plays the failure voice (609 too far, 607 shields up) for the player. Returns 1/0.

Create.doc: Constructor: calls Ship::Create and stores the launch time.

GetMarinesCanBoard.doc: Free boarding slots; 0 for small ships.

GetOwner.doc: Owner race; for ships with flag 134217728 owned by race 8 (pirates) it is replaced by the race of the pilot's subrace.

voice 101 of the marine leader

LaunchBoardingPod.doc: Launches up to 5 random marines as a boarding pod. If a pod object is passed the marines are added to it, otherwise they are returned in an array {voice, marine...}. Marks them as sent to the target, plays the leader's voice line 101 for the player and starts the pod's distance check.

LoadMarines.doc: Marks the given marines (keys of the passenger table) as loaded in m105.

NotValidBoardingTargetVoice.doc: For the player ship, plays the voice complaint matching the invalid boarding target kind (ship 611, station 613, other 614).

sort ascending by skill, best marines at the end
number of pods = ceil(marines / 5)
command 71 board ship with the pod members as script array

SendMarinesToBoardShip.doc: Sends the best marines (by overall skill) of this ship to board the target in pods of 5. Marks them as incoming, ejects them as passengers, and starts command 71 (board) on each group leader.

ShieldsReadyForBoarding.doc: True if the shield percentage is at or below the boarding threshold (plus 1 when strict is off).

place the suit just outside the ship hull

SpawnMarineSuit.doc: Puts a marine out into space in a space suit (Astronaut class 2064, type 267) next to the ship, with a jetpack ware, and sends it home to its owner object.

SetTargeted.doc: When targeted, the object becomes known to the player; then base handler.

Create.doc: Creates the ship through Carrier.Create with all five arguments, marks race 8 ships with flag 134217728, sets the owner from the race table and the default formation type of that race.

GetAnswers.doc: Adds 'Surrender and drop your freight!' (10020) for questions 20 and 21 when the ship has freight. Other answers come from the Big Ship base.

comments.text: Notoriety gain of 1 is repeated inside the drop branch as in TradeShip (probably +2, check).

GetQuestion.doc: Freight surrender question 10020, as in TradeShip.GetQuestion, with the Big Ship base for other questions. Returns a reply code.

Hit.doc: When hit by an object of another owner (arg4), calls for help from its group, then the base Hit runs.

StartAction.doc: Chooses the idle action, as TradeShip.StartAction: a player-owned ship in a station (class 2016) stops, otherwise IDLE; other ships return to their dock target m42 or stop. The home sector is stored in m43.

2142.doc: Big Ship subclass (2073) that cannot be boarded: no marine capacity (GetMaxMarines 0, CanBeBoarded 0), fixed size 20000, formation distance four times its size. No page 2006 name; name derived from its behaviour.

AttackedByHandler.doc: Attack handler with the Big Ship escalation ladder in m48 (1 warned, 2 second warning, 3 license withdrawn, 4 hostile) and 5 time units between steps. Non-player attackers are attacked back and called for help.

CanBeBoarded.doc: Always false: the ship cannot be boarded.

comments.text: DisableCapture is called with 0 here but with 1 in the other classes (2064, 2068, 2131). Check whether 0 enables capture: possible inconsistency.

Create.doc: Creates the ship through the Big Ship base. Unless it is created player-owned (mode 10), calls DisableCapture(0).

CreatePlayerOwned.doc: Creates the ship as player-owned (creation mode 10) and adds it to sector when one is given.

GetFormationDist.doc: Formation distance: four times the ship size.

GetGSize.doc: Fixed size value 20000 (probably the group size used by the formation code).

GetSize.doc: Total size of the ship's scene object (m3) when it exists, otherwise 20000.

AddClickArea.doc: Adds a clickable rectangle for this pass: group, id, x, y, width and height. Areas are reset by Update.

AddHeadLine.doc: Adds a header line with text, if the line is visible.

AddInfoLine.doc: Adds an info line with text, if the line is visible.

AddInfoLineCol.doc: Adds an info line with a bar and text in the given palette colour.

comments.text: no capacity check: m7 and m8 are allocated with 30 slots (SE_ArrayAlloc(30)), so more than 30 instances would overflow (not verified)

AddInst.doc: Returns the 3D instance for a body and key. Reuses the instance with the same key, or allocates a new one in the menu scene. Returns 0 when allocation fails.

AddMenuHeaderInfoLine.doc: Adds a header line with a left text and a right text at x.

AddMenuInfoLine.doc: Adds an info line with a bar, a left text and a right text at x.

AddMenuInfoLineCol.doc: Adds an info line with a bar in a colour, a left text and a right text at x.

AddMenuLine.doc: Adds a selectable menu line at the default text x. key is the shortcut key (mapped to line), line is the line index. Passes to AddMenuLineColX.

AddMenuLineCol.doc: Adds a menu line at x in a colour, using the default text x.

comments.text: append the translated key name to the text, in the key-name style (\x1bB..\x1bX markup)

AddMenuLineColX.doc: Adds a selectable menu line. If key is set, the key name is appended to the text, and the key is mapped to the line index in keyToLine. The line index is stored in selectedItem when this line is selected.

AddMenuLineWith2Values.doc: Adds a menu line with text, a value box and a right-hand text drawn at rightX.

AddMenuLineWith2ValuesL.doc: Like AddMenuLineWith2Values with one extra width parameter.

AddMenuLineWithValue.doc: Adds a menu line with text and a value box at the default text x. The value box is drawn by DrawValueBox with the given box x, value text and highlight flag.

AddMenuLineWithValueColX.doc: Adds a menu line with text at x in a colour and a value box.

AddMenuLineWithValueL.doc: Adds a menu line with text and a value box at the default text x, with one extra left parameter.

AddMenuLineWithValueLColX.doc: Adds a menu line with text at x in a colour, and a value box if the line is visible.

AddMenuLineWithValueLX.doc: Adds a menu line with text at x and a value box, with one extra left parameter.

AddMenuLineWithValueX.doc: Adds a menu line with text at x and a value box.

AddMenuLineX.doc: Adds a selectable menu line at x. Same arguments as AddMenuLine.

AddSelectLine.doc: Adds a select line with text and a value. Returns 1 if the line is selected.

AddSelectLineCol.doc: Adds a select line with text in the given colour. Returns 1 if the line is selected.

AddSelectLineColX.doc: Adds a select line with text at x in a colour. colorIndex 2 means the selection bar is not drawn and the line is not highlighted. Stores value in selectedItem when this line is selected. Returns 1 if the line is selected.

AddSelectLineX.doc: Adds a select line with text at x. Returns 1 if the line is selected.

comments.text: returns nothing when SA_AllocTextInst fails; the function has no else branch (not verified)

AddText.doc: Allocates a text instance with the given text and key, size 3000, in the menu scene. Returns the instance, or nothing when allocation fails.

AddTextArea.doc: Adds a multi-line text at the standard text x offset.

comments.text: x < 0: centre the line in the menu width

AddTextAreaX.doc: Adds a multi-line text, one line per '\n'. A tab splits a line into a left part at x and a right part at rightX. A negative x centres the line.

comments.text: y is offset by the first visible line (m14 in info lists, m18 in select lists) times the line height

BlitBlock.doc: Copies a block of a texture into the menu texture, clipped to the visible list window. Returns 1 when something was drawn, 0 otherwise.

comments.text: width 0 means the menu width minus 20 px
tab name '?' takes the leftover width instead of a tab
selected tab: m24 == index; with arg3 == index the tab blinks on the game age (g8.GetAge() & 1)
v15 is assigned here but not used afterwards (dead assignment)
blink state (age bit 0) and hover (m49 == 2) decide the button style

BuildTabBar.doc: Draws a row of tabs from an array of tab names. Each tab width comes from its text, with a '?' entry taking the free space. Tabs get click group 2. The selected tab and the tab under the mouse (m49 == 2) are highlighted.

CallInfiniteLoop.doc: Runs the engine's infinite loop helper for the given task id.

CancelInput.doc: Hook for cancelling an input in a value box. Empty here; subclasses override it.

ChangeValue.doc: Hook for the value arrows. delta is -1 or 1. Empty here; subclasses override it.

CheckClickAreas.doc: Looks for a click area under the point, newest first, and passes its group, id and local offset to OnClickArea. Returns 1 when one was hit.

CheckMouseOverClickAreas.doc: Looks for a click area under the point and calls OnMouseOverClickArea with its group and id. Calls it with -1, -1 when there is none. Returns 1 when an area was hit.

CheckSelected.doc: Registers the current line as selectable. The first selectable line becomes firstSelectable, the last becomes lastSelectable. Its row count is stored in lineSelectable, and the rows below it are marked -1.

CheckSelectionVisible.doc: Scrolls the select window so the selected line and its rows are visible, and resets the window at the first or last selectable line.

Create.doc: Creates a top-level menu for an object. Returns this, or nothing when the menu is already running.

CreateNext.doc: Creates a menu opened from another menu. Stores the previous menu, request and object, links the previous menu to this one and starts it.

CreatePrevious.doc: Returns to the previous menu with two arguments. If there is a previous menu, delegates to it, makes it active and starts the delete sequence. Otherwise restarts this menu without full setup.

DefaultSelectInput.doc: Key handler for select-type menus. Up and down move the selection, 766 and 767 scroll the info list when the pointer is over it (or no select window), 762 and 763 page up and down, 753 runs MenuAction.

Destruct.doc: Removes this menu as a listener from C502 and returns this.

Disable.doc: Stops the tasks and the menu's instances, sets state 0, clears the computer scene when this is the last menu, and calls ExitMenu.

DisplayMarineSkillStars.doc: Draws the marine skill stars from x to the right, one star icon per level, or '-' when the skill is 0.

DisplayMarineSkillStarsRight.doc: Draws the marine skill stars right-aligned at x, one star icon per level, or '-' when the skill is 0.

DrawActionInfoText.doc: Draws an action info text with guillemet markers on both sides, in the action colour (-1724872), cut to fit.

comments.text: channel scale 39321/65536 = 0.6

DrawBar.doc: Fills a bar. Flag 1 draws a solid colour from the palette; flag 128 draws the colour darkened to 60 percent (39321 of 65536), keeping alpha.

DrawBarCol.doc: Draws a bar over the current line in the given palette colour and flags.

DrawHeadText.doc: Draws a header text at the standard text x offset.

DrawHeadTextCenter.doc: Draws a text centred between x and rightX (rightX -1 = the menu text end).

DrawHeadTextX.doc: Draws a header text at x in the header colour (palette entry 3 of the alternate pens).

DrawInfoText.doc: Draws a text in the info colour (-2960686), cut to the menu width.

DrawLine.doc: Draws a line with the palette colour at colorIndex.

comments.text: frame at 0,0 with menuHeight, flag 1 with windowFlags
click areas: group 4, button 1 and 2, 30 x 17 px

DrawMenuWindow.doc: Draws the window frame with icon and title, plus two buttons at the top right (click areas 4/1 and 4/2). The button is pressed when hoverGroup is 4.

DrawPanelBottom.doc: Draws the bottom cap of a list panel under the last visible line.

comments.text: switch on sectionState chooses the frame texture row: 45 top, 65 middle, 82 bottom, 96 and 113 single/alt styles (meanings from texture layout, not verified)

DrawPanelLine.doc: Draws the frame of one list line, choosing the frame texture from sectionState and the current line. Only lines inside the window are drawn.

DrawRawInfoText.doc: Draws an info text line at the left edge, 30 px below the top of the menu.

DrawRawLine.doc: Draws a line in the menu texture with a raw colour.

DrawRawRect.doc: Fills a rectangle in the menu texture with a raw colour.

DrawRawText.doc: Draws a text block in the menu texture at the given position, font 129.

DrawRawTextMat.doc: Draws a text block into the given texture, font 129.

DrawRect.doc: Fills a rectangle with the palette colour at colorIndex.

comments.text: first time: enable the scrollbar margin and request a redraw (redrawRequested)

DrawScrollBarInfo.doc: Draws the scrollbar of an info list when it has more lines than fit. The first time a scrollbar is needed it only sets scrollbarShown and requests a redraw, so the text margin can change first.

DrawScrollBarSelect.doc: Draws the scrollbar of a select list when it has more lines than fit. Same logic as DrawScrollBarInfo, with selectScrollbarShown.

DrawSelectBar.doc: Draws the selection bar of the current select line with the default colour. Returns true when the line is the selected one.

comments.text: walk back while the row count of this line is negative (a row inside a multi-row item); a line with no start row would loop past index 0 (possible, not verified)

DrawSelectBarCol.doc: Draws the selection bar for the current line: flag 1 for the selected line, 128 for the hover line. Walks back to the first row of a multi-row line. Returns true when the line is selected.

DrawShieldHullBars.doc: Draws the shield and hull bars of an object on the current line.

DrawText.doc: Draws a text at the standard text x offset. The text is drawn in the highlight colour when the line is selected in a select list.

DrawTextCheckColX.doc: Cuts a text to fit between x and rightX, draws it at x in colorIndex and returns the text drawn.

DrawTextCheckX.doc: Cuts a text to fit between x and rightX, draws it at x and returns the text that was drawn.

DrawTextCol.doc: Draws a text in palette colour colorIndex at the standard text x offset.

DrawTextColX.doc: Draws a text on the current line at x in the palette colour colorIndex, cut to the menu width.

DrawTextIconX.doc: Draws an icon from the UI atlas (787, 422) at the given position on the current line.

DrawTextObjectSymbolX.doc: Draws the symbol of an object (INS_DrawObjectSymbol) on the current line.

DrawTextX.doc: Draws a text at x, in the highlight colour for the selected line of a select list.

comments.text: width 0 means 100 px

OnAbort.doc: Called when the abort button is pressed. Returns 1 to allow Stop.

OnKill.doc: Called when the close button is pressed. Returns 1 to allow Kill.

OpenNextMenu.doc: Opens another menu. Stores it as nextMenu, disables this menu and makes it the active menu. Returns the new menu, or the argument if it is 0.

PlayMoveSample.doc: Plays the menu move sound, sample 957.

PlaySuccessSample.doc: Plays the menu success sound, sample 955.

SelectTab.doc: Switches to a tab. Selecting the current tab plays the fail sound. Otherwise resets the window and selection, plays the move sound and updates. Returns 1 on change.

SetIgnoreKill.doc: Sets the ignoreKill flag, which keeps Kill from closing the menu.

SetRepeatDelay.doc: Sets the key-repeat delay between repeats.

SetupPens.doc: Fills the two ARGB palettes: normalPens for the normal style and alternatePens for the alternate style. Each entry is a text colour.

SetupTexture.doc: Sets the texture size to 384 x 1024 and the texture border to 20.

ShouldHandleKeyRepeat.doc: True for the keys that auto-repeat in menus: the arrow and page keys (758 to 761, 766, 767).

ShouldUseHoverLine.doc: True while a dropdown menu (C641) is open, so the pointer only highlights a line.

ShowText1.doc: Draws a text in the info colour (-2960686) on a given row.

ShowText2.doc: Draws a text in the highlight colour (-16711423) on a given row.

comments.text: raw key 294 or 295 always counts as a new press

SpecialInput.doc: Input filter before Input. Keys that auto-repeat are passed through only after the initial delay, then at the repeat delay. Returns 2 to swallow a repeat. Records the time of each event.

StartFace.doc: Plays a speech face animation in a separate task. Calls C200.PlaySpeechFaceDirect with the speech ids and face type 3.

Create.doc: Creates the menu for a source object and a packed ware to build. Stores the maximized preference and runs the shared setup.

CreateCommon.doc: Shared setup after creation: resets selection and flags, decides the asteroid or station build mode from the build ware subtype, and selects the build ware or the player's ship.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the sector map as the next dialog after previousMenu. Copies the previous menu's custom description if it has one.

CreateNextForBuildComplex.doc: Opens the sector map in build mode (request 29) for a station complex. Like CreateNextForBuildStation, plus two extra options that are stored for the build code.

CreateNextForBuildStation.doc: Opens the sector map in build mode (request 29) to pick a site for a station built by buildingShip. Returns 0 when the base menu creation fails.

CreatePrevious.doc: Passes the call to the base menu chain.

Destruct.doc: Frees the map data and the helper object, then destructs the base menu.

comments.text: v1 is the typed value from m106, or -1 when none

action codes: 1 owner, 2 background type, 3 sector radius, 4 radius update, 5 music track, 6 population, 7 toggle m102, 8 core sector, 9 and 10 nebula and star index, 30 to 45 picked object edits, 50 to 72 nebula and dust settings, 80 to 82 clipboard, 90 to 94 war objects, 100 to 131 background type settings
owner cycles over the faction ids whose bit is set in mask 918526
owner ids wrap within 1..19
background type change: stop the galaxy take, apply, restart it in a fork
rebuild nebula outer bodies, load the type data, and update the three cockpit monitors (C605)
sector radius is stored as metres times 500, steps of 2500000 (5 km)
radius limits: 2500000 to 500000000 (5 km to 1000 km)
game radius m99 = m98 * 1.125 (fixed point 73728 / 65536), only when m101 is clear
music track check: ids 1 to 10 and 100 to 999 are reset to 0 (probably the valid ranges)
mission quota index: 0 trade, 1 fight, 2 build, 3 think (see the C2001 getters)
toggles the core sector flag of the sector
action 90 clears the picked object, 90 and 91 leave the object list mode
war object id of the picked object; must be above 0
war record field 3 of the picked object
subtype change: the object is deactivated and reactivated when the galaxy is live
colour components: 31 red, 32 green, 33 blue, step 5
resource subtype cycles over the class 17 subtypes
reset the station's default wares by its type (C300.SetStationDefaultWares)
the player ship (g9) cannot be destroyed
self-destruct the picked object with code 21, in a fork, then clear the pick
copy to clipboard: clears the clipboard table and stores the picked object
pasted nebula: outer body index reset when it is past the count of the background type
after a paste the new object becomes the pick when it fits the menu kind m24 (0 ship, 2 station class 2016)
ambient colour change also moves the fog colour m118 when they were equal
fog near step: 50000, or 500000 above 5000000; typed values are multiplied by 500
all dust rates zero: no dust instances
outer range is 1.5 times the inner range
all dust rates zero: no dust instances
the typed value m106 is consumed after every action

EditorAction.doc: Galaxy editor command dispatcher for the sector and the picked object. action is the command code m20 (see the switch), step is the direction from the input (0 means the action was clicked, not spun). It parses the typed value from m106, runs the command and clears m106 at the end.

ExitMenu.doc: Turns the sector camera off, clears the update focus, frees the helper object, then exits the base menu.

comments.text: Gates are always listed here (no visibility filter); CheckKnown decides if the player knows them.
Ships with action 13 are skipped (meaning not known, probably not relevant to the map).
The tracked object is always listed. Other ships pass CheckKnown with a flag that is 1 for every ship except stationary ones (class 2135).

FindMapObjects.doc: Fills the sector map's selection tables from the current sector: gates, asteroids, flying wares, docks, factories and ships. Factories with a complex hangar go to their own table. Unknown objects are skipped through CheckKnown.

FindNearestObjectOnMap.doc: Returns the map object (ship, station, dock, asteroid, ware or gate) nearest to a map point, or 0. Distances are measured in the x-z plane in top view and in the x-y plane when tilted. With the strict flag, only objects within 500000 divided by zoom (1500000 for stations) are returned.

comments.text: request codes to hint texts: 1,4,5,11,13,20-25 = station; 2,16,17 = object; 7,18 = warp gate; 9,10,12,40 = ship; 14,15,19 = station or carrier; 26 = position; 27 = asteroid; 28 = ware container; 29 = build, see below
build request 29: asteroid (m94) 2020:28, station with complex flag 35:4265, station 2020:20, otherwise position 2020:25

GetActionInfo.doc: Hint line for the request code m2 (for example 2020:20 'Select a station', 2020:23 'Select a ship', 2020:25 'Select a position with the cursor'). Returns the user description when one is set.

GetContext.doc: Returns the context id m140 (1027 or 1028) used by the input layer, see SpecialUpdate.

comments.text: Cursor 1103 for any hovered object, refined to 1105 (own) or 1104 (enemy) for ships and stations.

GetCursorIcon.doc: Chooses the cursor for the map. Over a hovered object: 1103 default, 1104 enemy ship or station, 1105 own ship or station. Toolbar buttons show a tooltip after one second.

comments.text: out of range: wrap to the other end when wrap is set, otherwise clamp; -16777215 is a lower sentinel (probably)
typed value (negative means none) is accepted only inside [min, max]

GetEditorInputValue.doc: Applies one editor change. A non-zero step changes the value and wraps or clamps it to [min, max]; a zero step takes the typed value when it is inside [min, max]. Plays the success sample, or the fail sample and returns the old value when a typed value is rejected.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Menu height from the base setup (m80).

GetMenuMaxHeight.doc: Map menu maximum height: same value as GetMenuMaxWidth (512 when not maximized).

GetMenuMaxWidth.doc: Map menu width: the smaller of screen width minus 512 and screen height minus 128, clamped to 512..1024. 512 when not maximized.

GetSelectedObject.doc: Object picked on the sector map (field m82).

HidesMonitor.doc: Returns true for monitor states 1 and 2, which this menu covers (meaning not verified).

comments.text: Time step since the last input in ticks, clamped to 1..32.
Key 860: select the object nearest to the cursor and centre the map on it (only when no zoom animation runs). Success or failure sound.
Keys 848-851 and 856-859: move the map cursor (see MoveCursor).
Keys 852-855 in build mode (29) with a ghost ship and no zoom animation: rotate the ghost (852/853 alpha, 854/855 beta) by 256 units per 32 ticks. Otherwise they move the cursor.
Keys 709-713 open a monitor layout for the selected body (class 1000). Blocked while client state flag 4 is set.
Key 610 opens the details menu of the selected object in mode 0.
Key 820 opens menu class 2217 for a selected station that is owned or dockable.
Key 592 opens the communication menu for a ship, station or class 9001 object when C150.CanCommunicateWith allows it.
Key 597 opens menu class 2265 for an owned ship or station.
Key 762 pages the list up.
Key 763 pages the list down.
Key 759 moves the list selection down.
Key 758 moves the list selection up.
Key 767 moves the secondary selection down.
Key 766 moves the secondary selection up.
Key 642: stop the menu (same as the cancel action).
Keys 760 and 761 cycle the tabs (0 ships, 1 all, 2 stations) in the modes that show the tab bar.
Keys 609 and 753 run MenuAction. Key 609 does nothing in modes other than 0.
Unhandled keys return 0.

Input.doc: Keyboard and controller handler of the sector map. arg1 is the key code, arg2 the previous key (equal values mean a held key). Handles cursor movement, rotation of the build ghost, selection and zoom hotkeys, monitor layout hotkeys and tab switching. Returns 2 when the key is consumed, 0 otherwise.

IsMaximizePossible.doc: True when the screen is large enough for the maximized map (the computed size is above 512).

comments.text: Filter: when the no-mine option is set, asteroids reporting GetNoMine are skipped.

ListAsteroids.doc: Adds the asteroids of the sector to the selection list and returns how many were added. In the no-mine filter asteroids that have no ore left are hidden.

comments.text: Group bits in the row value: 0 own, 0x10000000 enemy, 0x20000000 highlighted (tracked or guidance target), 0x30000000 neutral (see ListShips).

ListDocksFacs.doc: Adds a table of docks or factories to the selection list, sorted by name, tagging every row with the group bits arg2. Returns the number of rows added.

ListFlyingWares.doc: Adds the flying wares (cargo in space) of the sector to the selection list, sorted by name, and returns the count.

comments.text: Mode 7 (probably route plotting) keeps only gates with a destination. Mode 18 (jump) keeps gates the jump target can use. Other modes keep all gates.
Each row gets the current section base plus a running row index; the index-to-object table is updated at the same time.

ListGates.doc: Adds the known gates of the sector to the selection list, sorted by name, and returns how many were added. Only active in tab 1 (all objects). The filter depends on the menu mode: route modes need a destination, jump mode needs a jumpable gate.

comments.text: Source is the player ship g9, unless a specific jump target is set (field m123).

ListJumpBeacons.doc: Lists the jump beacons (class 2062) of the sector that the jump source (player ship or the jump target) can jump to. Used in jump mode. Returns the count.

ListShipType.doc: Adds one table of ships to the selection list, sorted by the player's name for their own ships, and returns the count. Each row carries the group bits arg2.

comments.text: Ships are bucketed by SE_IsClass (class ids from page 2006); civilians first, unknown classes last.
The order of these calls is the order of the groups on screen.

ListShips.doc: Splits the given ships into groups by object class (civilian, M0 to M6 and other ship classes, TS, TP, TM, TL, goner ships) and lists each group through ListShipType. Returns the total count. Not used in tab 2 (stations).

ListWings.doc: Lists wings (ship groups keyed by their wing object) sorted by wing name. Each wing's ships are added through ListShipType. Returns the number of rows added.

comments.text: background types are the subtypes of class 2 (sectors)

LoadBgTypeData.doc: Copies the background settings of type bgType (body family, star, nebula and dust counts, dust rates, ambient colour, hue, fog, stardust) into the editor fields m107..m118. Does nothing unless the edit-sector-types mode is on.

MapZoom.doc: Starts a zoom animation in the given direction (arg1 1 zoom in, 0 zoom out) when allowed. Without a selected object it resets the zoom to 1x and cancels the tilt and zoom states.

MapZoomPossible.doc: Tells whether the map can zoom in (arg1 nonzero) or out (arg1 zero) from the current zoom m130. Zoom in is allowed below 256x, zoom out above 0.5x. Without a selected object returns nothing.

comments.text: Nothing is selected and the mode is not free placement (26 or 29): nothing to do.
Class 9001 objects cannot be acted on in modes other than 0.
Modes 35 and 40: request wares from an owned object (menu class 2249). Not for objects of other owners.
Mode 29 with the complex flag m95: the first pick needs a factory with connection points within 500000000 m of the carrier m125. Otherwise the failure sound plays.
Mode 29 complex flag, second pick: the target must be buildable (C623.CanBuildComplex). Class 2044 parts are recorded in m3 and the menu stops.
Mode 29 with the second anchor m97: both anchors must be within 500 times global parameter 99/20000 of the ghost m93. (m96 is used without a null check here.)
Mode 29 single build: the ghost m93 must be within 500000000 m of the carrier m125. The placement (position, rotation, body) is returned in m3.
Mode 26: the cursor position is returned in m3.
Modes 20, 21, 22 (trade): docking must be allowed for the ship g9; then the wares menu (2249) opens.
Mode 10: an own class 2033 ship is returned as the result.
Mode 5: a station's products are offered in menu 2249.
Modes 1, 9, 11 to 17 return the object as the result. Docking must be allowed for stations (modes other than 1 and 16).
Modes 2, 7, 18, 27, 28, 34 return the selected object as the result.
Any other mode: call the object's FillContextMenu when it exists, otherwise open its object menu.

MenuAction.doc: Acts on the selected object according to the menu mode m2: returns it as the result of the menu (m3 and Stop), requests trade wares or products, starts the build-placement steps, or opens the object's context menu. Called from the map on double-click and from the Enter key.

comments.text: Keys: 848 left, 849 right, 850 forward, 851 back, 856 left-forward, 857 right-forward, 858 left-back, 859 right-back. Forward and back act on z in top view and on y when tilted.
Clamp to five times the sector size.
Cursor clamped at the limit: failure sound. Otherwise the repeat counter grows.

MoveCursor.doc: Moves the map cursor (the camera focus m105 to m107) for a movement key arg1, with step size scaled by arg3 (1..32 ticks). Speed grows with repeated input, and the focus is clamped to five times the sector size.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Clears the selected map object when the list selection changes, then runs the base handler.

comments.text: Toolbar on the top right: 120 to 90 px from the edge toggles the camera mode (m103), 90 to 60 toggles side view, 60 to 30 zooms in, 30 to 0 zooms out.
Clicks on the maximise corner toggle the window size.
Only clicks inside the map area (below the title bar) continue.
Pixel to map coordinates: undo the zoom, pan and scale of the view.
Mode 26 or free build placement (29 without m94, m95): a click near the current target (within 1000000 / zoom) runs MenuAction, otherwise the target point moves there.

Click on empty space in a sector without a selection: a second click within 4 px of the first one sends a move command (StartExecuteCommand4, type 19) to the player ship. If the player cannot accept commands, speaks 13:135 Command rejected.
Clicking the already selected object: modes 1-40 in the list run MenuAction; other modes open the context menu.
Selecting an object switches to tab 1 unless the object fits the current tab (ship tab for ships, station tab for stations).
Select sound 955 on a new selection.

OnMapClick.doc: Handles a click on the map. arg1 and arg2 are map-window pixels, arg3 and arg4 screen pixels for the context menu. The toolbar buttons are tested first, then the move or selection behaviour depends on the mode and on the click distance.

comments.text: Toolbar hover ids: 14 camera mode (only when the sector has an object), 8 side view, 5 zoom in, 6 zoom out, 3 maximise.

OnMapMouseMove.doc: Updates the hover state m146 under the pointer. A toolbar button or the nearest map object is stored as the hover value; a negative value clears it.

OnMouseMove.doc: Passes the mouse position to the base menu, then refreshes the map hover state (-2 means outside the menu). Negative coordinates clear the hover.

comments.text: mark 'c' for SA flag 2 (meaning not verified)
mark 't' for SA flag 1 (meaning not verified)
mark 'd' for an active SQUASH mine (IsActive returns -1)

RapidCheckStr.doc: Returns a short colour-code mark for an object in a list: one mark for SA flag 2, another for SA flag 1, and a third for an active SQUASH mine (class 2066). Returns an empty string otherwise.

comments.text: nebulas with an index inside the count keep it

ResetNebulaOuterBodies.doc: Clamps the outer body index of every nebula in the sector to the outer body count of its background type. Indices past the count are reset to 0, and live nebulas are deactivated and reactivated around the change.

comments.text: bgType equal to the type count is accepted: it appends a new type (action 130)
sector uses this type: indices above the new counts are reset to 0 and the galaxy take is restarted in a fork

SaveBgTypeData.doc: Writes the edited fields m107..m118 back to background type bgType. When the sector uses that type, clamps its star and nebula indices to the new counts and restarts the galaxy take.

comments.text: Ships (2004) fit tab 0, any object fits tab 1, stations (2016) fit tab 2.

SelectTab.doc: Switches the list tab (m24): 0 ships, 1 all objects, 2 stations. Keeps the selected object only when it fits the new tab. Returns 1.

SetMapCameraPosition.doc: Computes the map viewport from the screen size and the menu width, in fixed point.

SetupTexture.doc: Sets the map texture size: 384 wide, 1024 high, 20 pixel margin.

comments.text: key codes 925 and 926 (probably the left and right arrows)

ShouldHandleKeyRepeat.doc: Key repeat filter: key codes 925 and 926 repeat in the object edit modes (m24 3 or 4) when an action is selected and m155 is clear. Other keys use the base rule.

comments.text: request 19 with no target: default object 2025
game tip 12 is shown once for build requests (C631)

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets up the map: update focus, object size, scaled camera height, zoom reset, background and map instances, title (the object's name), layout code 51, and a game tip for build requests after 500 ms.

comments.text: viewport for aspect 2.0 is halved; 3.0 uses a third plus an offset (probably multi-monitor setups)

SpecialResize.doc: Moves the map instances and the sector camera viewport after a screen resize.

comments.text: Format string takes m75 twice with the same argument. Probably a marker prefix; possibly a bug (verify).
Modes 0, 2, 16, 17, 26, 29 show a tab bar with three tabs: Ships (35:683), All (35:1102452), Stations (35:1102457). Tab index is m24.
Sector not visible to the player: only stored information is available, text 35:1102541.
Mode 7 or 18 lists gates (and jump beacons in 18). Mode 28 lists flying wares. Mode 27, or 29 with asteroid mode, lists asteroids. Other modes list the sector objects by group.
Modes 9, 10, 12, 34, 35, 40 do not partition the sector objects at all.
Mode 19 (docking) needs a docking target m123. Objects must allow docking with it.
Mode 29 with the complex placement flag: only own factories with factory connection points that can build the complex (C623.CanBuildComplex) are listed.
Own objects go to the own tables: shipyards (class 2037), factories (class 2006), other docks. Own objects are not listed again as enemies.
Modes 13, 15 and 17 show only own objects.
Modes 1, 5, 11, 13, 20, 21, 22 do not list the non-own objects. Mode 29 with the complex flag also stops here.
v31 is always 0, so the previous-menu object branch never runs (dead code).
Mode 19 keeps only targets that allow docking for the ship m123.
Mode 34 keeps only classes 1700 and 2064 (meaning not verified).
Mode 35 keeps only objects that have passengers.
Mode 10: own wing-capable ships of class 2033 only. Ships in a wing go into the wing table; the others into the free list.
Modes 14, 15: docks with a bay (bay size above 0) only.
Sections: own, highlighted (0x20000000), enemy (0x10000000), neutral. A section header is added only when its list is not empty.
Neutral docks and factories are added with group bits 0, but neutral ships with 0x30000000. This may be an inconsistency (not verified).
Drop a trailing empty section header.
Scroll the list so the previously selected object (m83) stays in view.
Own ship row state: 4 attacked by someone, 6 the player's ship g9, 2 the controlled target, 5 other own ship.

Symbol flag bits: 1 tracked object, 2 enemy, 8 own, 128 active squash mine, 256 attacking you, 1024 shield below 30 percent, 8192 own selected control target other than g9, 32768 highlighted, 65536 civilian.
Info line: own ships show class, hull, shield and laser; other military ships hull and shield; civilians hull and shield only.
If the selected object has an owner, its race body is set on the 3D model m87.
Grid lines every 2000000 m, scaled by the zoom.
Layer 2 (complex factories) also draws the hangar connection line, even when the object is off the visible area.
Each object is drawn as a symbol with flags v107 (the same bits as the list rows).
Zoom text: zoom scale times 100 percent.
Build mode (29): a ghost ship m93 follows the cursor. m123 packs the object type: class in bits 16-23, subtype in the low 16 bits.
The ghost is pulled back to a safe position when it drifts more than 5000 units from the cursor.
Ghost out of range when it is more than 500000000 m from the build carrier m125 or from the anchors m96 and m97 (distance limit is 500 times global parameter 99/20000).
Window title: Sector Map (35:694).
Maximise button is shown only when the window can be enlarged.

SpecialUpdate.doc: Per-frame redraw of the sector map. It resets the selection tables, sorts the sector's objects into own, enemy, highlighted and neutral groups per type, builds the list rows, scrolls to the selected row and draws the map: grid, objects, camera marker, zoom and tilt buttons, scale text. Probably the SpecialUpdate of the sector map (page 35:694 Sector Map).

comments.text: blink phase toggles every 750 ms
fast mode (after the zoom finished): 50 ms wait and animation step 5

StartMenu.doc: Starts the menu update task: while the menu is active it blinks the cursor, decrements flashCountdown, redraws and updates the camera. Waits 250 ms per step, or 50 ms with fastAnim set. Stops the sector camera when it exits.

ToggleMaximised.doc: Toggles the maximised window flag, stores it on the class, clears the hover state and relayouts the window.

ToggleSideView.doc: Starts the tilt animation between top view and side view. From top view (m132 0) it starts raising the view (state 4), otherwise lowering it (state 5). Blocked while another animation runs.

TrackSelectedObject.doc: Makes the selected body (class 1000) the monitor's tracking target when the monitor can track it. Otherwise the failure sound plays.

UpdateCamera.doc: Sets hasNavSatellite (a Nav. Satellite MKII is among the player's ships) and sectorCamAvailable, then switches the sector camera on or off while the menu is open.

comments.text: possible issue: when the refresh is more than 5 s overdue the function returns and never resets rangeUpdateTime, so refreshes stop for the rest of the session (probably harmless: the menu calls it every frame)

UpdateRangeData.doc: Refreshes scannerRanges once per second: collects position and scanner range of the player's objects and compresses them into one list.

comments.text: 1000 to 1063: war state ids, toggled in the active set (C300)
2000 to 2063: war state of the picked object, set when not set yet
clearing needs another state of the object that is also active (probably keeps one state on)

WarEditorAction.doc: War state editor command. Codes 1000 to 1063 toggle a war state in the galaxy's active set. Codes 2000 to 2063 set a war state of the picked war object, and clear it only when another of the object's states is also active. Acts on a click (step 0) only, otherwise plays the fail sample.

YZProjection.doc: Projects a map point onto the screen vertical axis for the current tilt. Tilt 0 (top view) returns z, tilt 16384 (side view) returns y, values in between are blended.

comments.text: frame colour -11180510 (ARGB, probably a yellow-green marker)
frame drawn when not reversing, or when reversing past frame 116
frame drawn around the element's current cell
animation state for this element is stored in 10 slots
animation finished: m135 = 3 (fast redraw mode)

___doZooming.doc: Advances the zoom and pan animation of one map element (10 slots in zoomAnimData, selected by arg2). Moves the frame position toward its target, draws the frame and, in mode 2, updates the zoom scale and view centre.

___drawZoomFrame.doc: Draws a square corner-bracket frame around a point on the map. The frame size is the given size plus a margin.

___sectorCamOff.doc: Removes the sector camera from the scene, frees it and its carrier object.

comments.text: camera focus 16384 (fixed point)

___sectorCamOn.doc: Creates the sector camera and its SA carrier object in the selected object's space scene, with the viewport for the screen aspect ratio.

2216.name: MenuSector

2217.doc: Trade and station-management menu (page 35 title 'Trade' or 'Adjust station parameters' for own stations). Lists wares to buy and sell, funds transfer, ship repair/sell/upgrade, blueprints, production, reversing/recycling, spraying, loadouts and station parameters for a partner object (station, dock or ship) opened from a trading ship. Derived class 2263 is the ship equipment variant.

0.name: selectedType

comments.text: Skip flagged wares when the trade ship is not the player's ship.
Upgrade wares (flag 8) show the remaining upgrades, other wares show the stock of the partner.
Fixed-price special case: ware 16/11 (packed 1048587) costs 3000 per unit times the amount.
Ship-equipment screen (2263): prices are multiplied by the number of selected ships.
Selected row: flag 1 selects selection mode 1, otherwise mode 3.
Upgrade row: the bar maximum is the upgrade capacity when the container size is set.

AddSortedWareList.doc: Draws the ware list of the trade screen, sorted by ware type name. For each ware it shows the available stock or remaining upgrades, the unit price and the volume. Wares with flag 4 are hidden when the trade ship is not the player's ship. Ware type 16/11 (packed 1048587) has a fixed price of 3000 per unit.

comments.text: Marine ware: 1 if the ship is marine capable (IsMarineCapable(1)), else 0.
Marine ware where the player cannot cover the unit price: no units.

CapMaxWareCount.doc: Caps a requested amount so the player can pay for it and the free volume allows it. For marine wares the result is 1 if the ship can take a marine. Returns the capped count, 0 when nothing is affordable.

comments.text: Mode 21: toggle docking not allowed for NPCs.
Mode 22: intermediate trade bits: bit 1 = buy intermediates, bit 2 = sell intermediates; cycles through 4 states.
Mode 31: production item count, clamped to 0 .. max minus current production.
Mode 38: spray hue or saturation with the same range as the key handler.
Mode 39: save option bit toggle (m107 1..3).
Mode 40: loadout flag bit toggle (m107 1..3).
Mode 20: max trade jumps, bounded by 50 total.

ChangeValue.doc: Changes the pending amount by one step in the direction given (positive or negative), or toggles a flag for the current mode. Used for modes 20-22, 31, 38-40 and the default branch of the key handlers.

CheckTLAvailable.doc: Returns the first ship of the partner's dock that has general subtype 0, is docked there and is owned by the player or hired. Returns 0 when there is none. (TL is probably a transport ship.)

CheckTLFree.doc: Sums the free capacity of one ware type (arg1 class, arg2 type) over the ships counted by CheckTLAvailable: docked at the partner and owned by the player or hired.

comments.text: Convert the pixel-like volume to units: round away from zero by the unit volume.
Trade not allowed (no trade or no partner): reset amount, fail sample, and speech 13/57 and 13/62 for a positive click.
Mode 2 click: resources are not sold (speech 13/1289).
Price higher than the player money: search for the largest affordable amount, as in the key handler.
Amount larger than free volume: clamp to m113/m119 and play fail.
Station not owned by player and the player cannot pay: amount reset, speech 13/1254.
Negative click: mode 1 gives speech 13/1290 (products not bought); modes 2 and 3 set the amount directly with the negative stock limit.
Zero click: amount reset to zero with a move sample.
Positive amount with no trade allowed: amount reset, speech 13/57 and 13/62.

ClickTradeBar.doc: Click on the trade bar: arg1 is a signed volume delta. Converts it to units with the unit volume m119, then sets the pending amount m115 for the current mode, clamped by stock, money and free volume. Positive clicks buy, negative clicks sell.

Create.doc: Creates as first menu; a complex station is replaced by its complex hangar.

CreateCommon.doc: Common creation: stores partner and trade ship and resets selection state.

CreateNext.doc: Creates as a follow-up menu in a chain.

Codes 609/610 open the identify/details menu, 756/757 are sell-all/buy-all, 760/761 step the amount down/up, and the rest go to DefaultSelectInput. inputArg is the second code the caller passes along; it is compared with inputCode for some keys.

MenuAction.doc: Action of the trade menu for the current mode (m106) and the selected line. Mode 9 builds the marine training dropdown, 20 sets max trade jumps, 1/2/3 execute the trade (wares, marines, upgrades, ship purchase, equipment), 7 transfers between own ships, 4/5 price edit, 6 money, 8 repair, 10 opens the equipment menu, 30-37 add or remove blueprint/reverse/repair/recycle items, 38 spray, 39/40 flags and loadouts.

Three layouts: own station (partner owned by player: wares, funds, parameters, blueprints, production, reverse/repair/recycle/spray, ship loadouts), foreign ship-type partner (class 2006: ship selling, repair, equipment, product lists) and foreign station (class 2007: goods sections).
