2217.name: MenuTrade

2225.doc: Dialog menu with a speaking partner (pilot ship or station officer): shows the question text, plays the speech and offers numbered answers. Runs the conversation state machine: question, answers, reply, end. dobj: MENU_DIALOG. Created by menus that talk to a ship or station (OpenParameterMenu, CreateNext with a question id); answers come from C3001 and from the partner's own GetAnswers.

0.doc: answers offered for the current question; -1 = answers disabled, 0 = none
0.name: answerCount

1.doc: topic or question id passed in by the caller (18 is mapped to 0)
1.name: questionId

10.doc: value handed back to the caller when the dialog ends
10.name: callbackParam

2.doc: question id to speak; 0 = none to fetch, -1 = no speech
2.name: questionValue

3.doc: answer ids of the current question (from GetAnswers)
3.name: answerIds

4.doc: wrapped question text lines; 0 when there is no text
4.name: questionLines

5.doc: object the dialog is with (pilot ship or station)
5.name: partner

6.doc: object that opened the dialog; default is the player ship g9
6.name: caller

7.doc: state machine value set by SetDialogState; 5 = answer list shown
7.name: dialogState

8.doc: nonzero if the player may leave the dialog with Escape
8.name: escapeAllowed

9.doc: id of the running speech task; stale callbacks are ignored
9.name: speechTask

ChangeTarget.doc: Changes the partner to another object (targetOffer) and refreshes the comm window and face.

Create.doc: Opens the dialog for a target object. arg2 is the question id, arg3 the question value, arg4 the caller (player ship when empty).

CreateNext.doc: Opens the dialog as the next menu in a chain; same arguments as Create after the parent menu and mode.

comments.text: class 2307 is the sub-menu that is already running

CreatePrevious.doc: Re-opens the dialog when returning from a sub-menu. If a ship is docked to the dialog (2307 'ask' menu), it switches to state 7. Otherwise it reloads the question and closes when there is nothing to say.

Destruct.doc: Clears the comm-window pointer and the answer array, then forwards to the base destructor.

DisableAnswers.doc: Disables the answers (answerCount = -1) when arg1 is set; otherwise sets it to 0 if it was negative.

comments.text: 15 pixels per text line

DrawMenuWindow.doc: Sets the window height: the full menu height in state 5 (answers), 64 + line count * 15 when there is text, otherwise 45. Then draws the base window.

comments.text: answer kind 7 gets prefix text 18:10007 + the object name; kind 17 gets 18:10006 + the object name

GetAnswerString.doc: Returns the text of an answer. Handles text values, conversation lines (class 313 with {param@} substitution), and pairs of table and text id. Type 2 and 11 values are returned as they are.

GetAnswers.doc: Fills answerIds with the answers of the question, from C3001 first and then the partner's GetAnswers.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Returns the fixed height 384 of the dialog window.

GetMenuRequest.doc: Returns the pending menu request id m2.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns -1: the dialog shows no object body.

GetQuestion.doc: Asks the question tables for the reply text. Tries C3001 first, then the partner's own GetQuestion. Returns a question id, -1 for no reply, 0 for end.

comments.text: returns early unless menu mode m5 is 1 or 2 and dialogState is not 6 (closing)
no answers: closing state 6 and stop after the idle loop

InitAnswers.doc: Loads the answers for a question and chooses the next state: none (closes), a single answer list, or a question to speak.

comments.text: 785..793 = number keys 1..9 for answers
answer index m20 = key - 785; text-only answers (10011) are skipped in the count
text-only lines are not numbered

Input.doc: Key handler. Codes 785..793 choose answers 1..9 (skipping answers that are only text). 752 is the abort key, 800 the kill key; both are handled only in state 5 or when the dialog is the active menu.

comments.text: not active and not on the stack: nothing to kill

Kill.doc: Kills the dialog. Speech is cut short (SpeakWithPriority 99). Returns 1, or nothing when there is no active dialog.

MenuAction.doc: Activates the selected answer in state 5, or closes the dialog when no answers are left. In state 3 with a question it starts the answer list again.

MyKillHelper.doc: Hides the comm window, clears the idle face and stops the speech, then forwards to the base helper.

OnAbort.doc: Abort (key 752): in the active dialog, closes the dialog and cuts the speech when escape is allowed.

OnKill.doc: Kill (key 800): in the active dialog, closes the dialog with a hard kill when escape is allowed.

comments.text: a dialog within a dialog: 2225 with the same partner

OpenParameterMenu.doc: Opens a sub-menu for a dialog parameter. Id 2225 opens another dialog, 2228 gets two extra args, and a parameter-kind 6 gets the object's environment. Stores arg4 as the callback parameter.

ReceiveDialogParameter.doc: Passes a dialog parameter. Tries C3001 first, then the partner. Returns -1 if there is no partner.

comments.text: question 102000 keeps the title empty

SetCommWindowTitle.doc: Sets the comm window title to the partner's pilot name, except for question 102000.

SetDialogState.doc: Sets the dialog state machine value (dialogState).

SetEscapePossible.doc: Sets escapeAllowed: whether the player may abort the dialog.

ShowCommWindow.doc: Shows the comm window with an empty title.

comments.text: question text from C3001 first, then the partner
face: pilot face for ships, 1141 for stations (2016), 0 otherwise
no face while music or cutscene audio C620 is playing
speech task id check: skip the answer init if a newer speech started

SpeakQuestionWithDuration.doc: Speaks a question. In states 0 and 1 it only sets state 1. Otherwise it fetches the question text and speaks it through the partner's face; arg3 is a duration flag that also slows game time (TI_SetTimeWarpFactor). After speech it re-initialises the answers.

comments.text: question id 18 is the generic 'no topic' id
pilot speaker of the ship or fighter becomes the speaker for the dialog

SpecialCreate.doc: Sets up the partner and the first question. Returns this if there is text to show, 0 if no question is available, and this when there is nothing to speak.

comments.text: fork: plays the face speech without waiting

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the title (partner's question header, or text 35:827 'Comm'), starts the comm face speech and shows the comm window.

comments.text: answer id 10011 as the last answer is the closing choice: drawn as info text, not selectable
ActorHasMissionOffer: index of the mission the speaking actor offers, 0..4
icon ids 89..93 = mission offer markers for offers 0..4

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the partner name info line, the question text, and in state 5 the numbered answer list. Answers that offer a mission get an icon from the sector's ActorHasMissionOffer index. Answer 10011 is the closing choice.

comments.text: question value -1: a state without speech

StartMenu.doc: Chooses the dialog state when the menu starts: answers (state 4 or 2 when there is no question), answer list, or speaking.

comments.text: face state 2 = idle loop; 3 = stopped

StopIdleLoop.doc: Stops the idle face loop, plays the closing speech and hides the comm window, when the face is in the idle loop state 2.

StopSpeechTask.doc: Clears the speech task id and cuts the speech short.

comments.text: the question text is a list of (table, id) pairs; missing texts are skipped
text is wrapped to the window width

StoreQuestionString.doc: Converts a question's format array into text lines (at most 10) and stores them in questionLines. Each pair is a text table id and text id.

comments.text: question id 18 is mapped to 0 here as well
the next question is -2 or 0: the dialog closes

UseAnswer.doc: Uses an answer: plays the answer's action and relays its outcome to the partner, then continues with the next question, or closes the dialog. Returns 1 if the dialog continues.

WriteAnswers.doc: Stores the answer list and count, and shows it (state 5).

2226.doc: Load and save game menu (engine name MENU_LOADSAVE, base class MENU_PLAYER C2202). One class serves both modes: load (m85 = 1) lists all save slots, save (m85 = 0) lists slots 0 to 9 and shows slots 10 and up as autosaves. Saving outside a station uses one salvage insurance ware. dobj name: none.

0.doc: save slot table from X2_LoadSaveNames; entry = [names, title, ?, version, play time]
0.name: saveSlots

1.doc: 1 once a slot is chosen; ExitMenu saves or loads only then
1.name: slotConfirmed

2.doc: 1 = load game menu, 0 = save game menu
2.name: isLoadMode

3.doc: 1 when saving outside a station: one salvage insurance (ware 16/11) is used
3.name: needsInsurance

4.doc: widest play-time string in pixels, used for column layout
4.name: timeLabelWidth

comments.text: Base creation failed: return without the slot setup.

Create.doc: Creates the menu in load mode when arg1 is true, else save mode, by calling CreateCommon. Returns the result of the base creation or nothing when it fails.

comments.text: Save mode outside a station (not docked, or no environment): m86 = 1, so saving will take a salvage insurance.
Read the save slot table through X2_LoadSaveNames.
No save data: in load mode close the menu and start deleting, else return this without slots.
Width of the widest play-time string (format from text 35:4210).
Show slots 0-9 in save mode, all slots in load mode.
Newest slot = the one with the largest play time (index 4 of the slot entry).

CreateCommon.doc: Shared setup. Reads the slot table with X2_LoadSaveNames, sets the widest time string width, and selects the newest slot (largest play time) as the default selection. Sets needsInsurance when not docked. With no slots in load mode the menu is closed and deleted; otherwise returns this.

CreateNext.doc: Creates the menu as a child of the parent menu arg1 (stored in m0), with arg2 stored in m2. The mode is taken from arg3 through CreateCommon.

Destruct.doc: Clears the slot table and runs the base destructor.

comments.text: Only act when a slot was confirmed (m84).
Save outside a station: remove one salvage insurance (ware 16/11) from the player ship g9 before saving. No check that a unit is held before this call (open question).

ExitMenu.doc: On close: if a slot was confirmed, load it (DoLoadGame in a fork) in load mode, or in save mode take one salvage insurance from the player ship when needsInsurance is set, then save (DoSaveGame in a fork). Then runs the base ExitMenu.

GetIcon.doc: Returns the window icon id: 32 in load mode, 50 in save mode.

GetName.doc: Returns the window title: Load Game (35:727) or Save Game (35:728).

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns the object body shown in the menu panel: ware 16/11, the salvage insurance item.

Input.doc: Input handler: passes the input to the default select input.

IsEmpty.doc: True if the save slot arg1 has no saved game.

comments.text: Mark the slot as chosen; the work is done on close.

MenuAction.doc: Confirms the selected slot: sets slotConfirmed (m84) and closes the menu through Stop. The actual load or save happens in ExitMenu.

comments.text: Selection list is started here; the head line shows the Load/Save title and the date column header (text 35:4209).

Opened by menus that need a sector selection; the jump device menu (mode 18, CreateForJumpDevice) is the main case. It owns a 3D galaxy scene (class 600), a camera and the selected sector. No dobj name in the hints.

1.name: sectorY

17.name: mapCamera

19.name: galaxyFrameInst

AddMenuInfoLineCutoff.doc: Adds a label and value line. The label is cut to fit before valueX; the value is cut to the space right of valueX minus reservedWidth.

CancelInput.doc: Clears the search filter and resets the list selection.

ClearFilter.doc: Clears the search text and the filtered list.

ClearGalaxyMap.doc: Frees the galaxy scene and its camera and clears the references. Called on exit.

comments.text: Objects without an owner: the menu deletes itself at once.
Maximised flag is read from the class singleton, so the window keeps its size between openings.

Create.doc: Creates the map for the menu object arg1. arg2 and arg3 are initial values of the menu's own state. The map is restored from the class singleton (maximised flag). Returns the base result.

comments.text: Menu mode 18 is the jump mode.

CreateForJumpDevice.doc: Creates the map as the jump device menu for the object arg1: base Create, then menu mode 18 (jump) and cleared flags.

comments.text: The user description is taken from the parent menu.

CreateNext.doc: Creates the map as a child of the previous menu arg1. Keeps the parent's user description. Returns the base result.

comments.text: Menu mode 18 is the jump mode.

CreateNextForJumpDevice.doc: Same as CreateForJumpDevice, for a menu opened from a previous menu (CreateNext).

comments.text: Jump mode (18) with no parent menu (m0 == 0): starts the jump (class 5006).

CreatePrevious.doc: Creates the previous menu. In jump mode with no parent menu, starts the jump through C5006.StartJumping.

ExitMenu.doc: Frees the galaxy map objects, then runs the base ExitMenu.

comments.text: only pointer positions with x and y >= 0 are tested (negative = outside)
top bar: zoom buttons at its left end (5 zoom in, 6 zoom out)
maximise button (3) at the top right, only when maximising is possible
centre column: next sector up (11) and down (12)
side columns: next sector left (9) and right (10)
filter result line (16) is hit while a filter is active
anywhere else on the map: the sector under the pointer (INS_GalaxyMapFindSector returns grid coordinates)

FindMapHoverObject.doc: Hit-test on the galaxy map at (x, y). Returns a control code (zoom 5/6, maximise 3, next sector 9-12, filter line 16), the sector object under the pointer, or nothing.

comments.text: a gate counts only when its destination is owned, known, not the temporary sector and has a gate
hub gate: continue through the hub to the sector on the opposite side
no usable gate: nearest sector in that direction; modes 41/42 also search unknown sectors

FindNextSector.doc: Moves the selection to the neighbour sector in direction (0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, probably). Uses the gate on that side if it leads to a sector that can be shown; otherwise the nearest sector found by INS_GetGalaxyMapNextSector. Fails with a sound when nothing is found.

comments.text: Text 2020:26 Select a sector.

GetActionInfo.doc: Returns the user description when set. Otherwise returns 'Select a sector' when the menu is not in mode 0, or nothing.

comments.text: hover code 5 (zoom in) and 6 (zoom out): tooltips 1903:10863 and 1903:10864

GetCursorIcon.doc: Returns the cursor icon from the base menu. Over the zoom buttons it shows a tooltip after one second.

comments.text: The matching prefix is wrapped in the colour escape codes \x1bY and \x1bX.

GetHighlightedName.doc: Returns the sector name with the part that matches the filter text highlighted by colour codes. Returns the name unchanged when there is no match.

GetMapGateState.doc: Returns 1 if the sector at (gridX, gridY) has a known gate in direction, 0 if the gate is missing or unknown, and nothing if the sector is not visible.

comments.text: the viewed and selected sector is state 2, except in attack mode
player's current grid position
attack mode: own factory under attack gives state 3
attack mode: own factory without resources gives state 4
the player's own sector: state 5
war sector (not in attack mode): state 7
jump mode: a sector the jump ship can reach with its energy gives state 2
owned by the player: state 6; otherwise plain 1

GetMapSectorState.doc: Returns the display state of a sector on the galaxy map: 0 not visible, 1 plain, 2 the viewed sector or a sector the jump ship can reach, 3 own object under attack, 4 own factory without resources (attack mode), 5 the player's own sector, 6 owned by the player, 7 war sector.

comments.text: Window fits to the left of the galaxy frame area: base height m80.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Returns the window height. A narrow window keeps the base height; otherwise the height fits the screen, limited to the base menu limits.

GetMenuMaxHeight.doc: Maximum window height. Same rule as GetMenuMaxWidth.

comments.text: Not maximised: fixed 512 width.

GetMenuMaxWidth.doc: Maximum window width: 512 when not maximised, otherwise the screen size (width minus 512, height minus 128) clamped to 512..1024.

GetText2Inst.doc: Returns the galaxy frame graphic instance (galaxyFrameInst).

comments.text: Name of the sector at the origin grid position.

GetTitle.doc: Returns the name of the origin sector while the map is still centred on it, otherwise an empty string.

GetUserDesc.doc: Returns the description set by SetUserDescription.

HidesMonitor.doc: True when the cockpit monitor must be hidden for monitor mode monitorMode (modes 1 and 2).

comments.text: key 752: clears the search filter first, if one is set
keys 766/767 (up/down): with a filter they move the list; without one they fall through to the zoom keys 863/864 (probably intended)
keys 760/761 without a filter: next sector in direction 2 (left) and 3 (right)
keys 758/759 without a filter: next sector in direction 0 (up) and 1 (down)
key 644: stop the ship (Stop())
cheat warp: move the player's ship to the selected sector, then QuickWarp
key codes 516 and up (except 769) are not handled here
auto-repeat guard: the same key is ignored for 75 ms; repeat starts after 750 ms (250 ms for codes 516 and up)
backspace (769): deletes the last character of the filter
printable characters extend the filter, up to 30 characters
easter egg: typing 'do a barrel roll' starts a two second camera roll and unlocks ACH_BARREL_ROLL
otherwise the typed text is matched against sector names; the first match is selected

Input.doc: Main key handler of the galaxy map. Returns 2 when the key is used, 0 when the key is passed on. Search filter typing, list movement, tab and zoom keys, cheat warp and the barrel roll easter egg are handled here.

IsMaximizePossible.doc: True when the screen is large enough for a window bigger than 512.

IsSectorVisible.doc: True if the sector at grid (gridX, gridY) is owned, known and not the temporary sector.

comments.text: timer has run out: the target becomes the displayed sector and the filter is cleared
still moving: zoom distance is interpolated linearly over the move time
barrel roll mode (m97): camera orientation is rolled
zoom reached an end (0 or 65536): roll mode ends and ACH_BARREL_ROLL is unlocked

MapUpdate.doc: Advances the galaxy map camera towards the target sector (the displayed sector changes when the move timer ends), interpolates the zoom distance, and updates the 3D map view. redrawNow decides whether the full Update() runs at once or when the timer has ended.

comments.text: zoom in only while the wanted distance is above the minimum

MapZoom.doc: One zoom step. zoomIn halves the wanted camera distance, otherwise it doubles it, clamped to the min and max distances. Plays the zoom sample and returns 1 on change; otherwise plays the fail sound and returns nothing.

MapZoomPossible.doc: Returns true when the map can still zoom in (zoomIn set) or out (zoomIn clear).

comments.text: not enough energy cells for the jump: spoken warning 13:1100056
no gate or beacon to the target: start the jump only if the sector is jumpable, else fail sound
modes 3 and 36: the picked sector is the result; reply code 65544 (0x10008) is stored before it
other modes: open the sector submenu (2216)

MenuAction.doc: Acts on the selected sector. Mode 18 starts a jump after checking the jump energy and the gate or beacon route. Modes 3 and 36 return the picked sector as the result and close. Other modes open the sector submenu (2216) in the same mode.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Resets a cached hover index when the list selection changes.

comments.text: buttons (click areas) get the click before the list
second click on the same row: act on the selected ship or sector

OnClick.doc: Mouse click on the list: click areas get the click first; a click on a row selects it; a second click on the selected ship or sector acts on it.

comments.text: map clicks only work in map mode (m5 == 2)
hit codes: 5/6 zoom in/out, 11/12/9/10 next sector up/down/left/right (FindNextSector 0 to 3, probably in that order), 3 maximise, 0 fail sound
clicking the already selected sector runs the menu action; the first click only moves there

OnMapClick.doc: Handles a click on the galaxy map at (x, y). The hit-test code selects a zoom step, a next-sector jump, the maximise toggle, or a sector. A second click on the same sector runs the menu action.

OnMapMouseMove.doc: Updates the map object under the pointer and refreshes the map when it changes.

comments.text: coordinates -2 mean the pointer is outside the list (probably)

OnMouseMove.doc: Forwards the mouse move to the base menu; a move outside the list clears the map hover object.

RebuildGalaxyMap.doc: Clears the galaxy scene and redraws it, when the scene exists.

comments.text: Window background colour -267775718.
Tool icons come from texture Interface/interface_template_blackpearl_diff. A hovered icon uses sprite row 687, others 735.
Maximise button only when the window can be enlarged.

RefreshMapWindow.doc: Draws the window: background fill, title 'Universe Map' (35:826), zoom buttons (5 and 6), four tool icons on the edges (9 left, 10 right, 11 top, 12 bottom) and the maximise button. Areas outside the window are blacked out.

SetMapCameraPosition.doc: Fits the galaxy map camera viewport and aspect ratio to the window size m81 by m80.

SetMaximized.doc: Stores the maximised flag on this instance.

SetUserDescription.doc: Stores the free-text description shown as the action line (see GetActionInfo).

SetWantedDistance.doc: Stores the camera distance to restore on the next opening.

SetupTexture.doc: Sets the menu texture id and its size (384 by 1024, texture id 20) in the inherited texture fields.

ShouldUseHoverLine.doc: Enables the hover highlight for this menu.

comments.text: Wanted distance is read from the class singleton, so the zoom is kept between openings.
Without an argument the player's current sector is used.

SpecialCreate.doc: Centres the map on the given sector, or on the player's current sector when none is given. Restores the wanted camera distance and records the creation time.

comments.text: Background graphic: effects/x3ap/menugfx/menu_sector.
Frame graphic: effects/x3ap/menugfx/galaxy_map.
Creates the galaxy map scene (class 600) named Galaxy Map Scene.
Scene state 1 for this menu's class id 2228.
Jump mode (18) or mode 36 shifts the list rows down by 3. With the debug cheat active, by 2.

SpecialMenu.doc: Builds the galaxy map window: sets the menu type 26, creates the background and frame graphics, the galaxy map 3D scene and its camera, lays out the list rows and starts the menu.

SpecialResize.doc: Moves the background and frame graphics to the new window size, updates the list height, refits the camera and redraws the map.

comments.text: a selected action target (gate, planet, ship) gets its own info text first
race flags 918526: sector has a security level line (35:751)
population -2 means unknown: shown as 35:4413 'Unknown'
planets: every entry is counted except subtype 128
sum of the sun energy factors, shown as percent (35:1102502 'Suns')
size line: integer rounding to steps of 5; units not verified
jump modes 18 and 36: show the energy the jump ship needs for the jump
NeededEnergyForJump(ship, from, to). Ware type 11 = energy cells (35:4659 'Available')
virtual keys 863/864 = zoom in/out (35:1100033/1100034); 993/994 are cheat keys
cheat-only hints: warp to sector, show all sectors
search line: the typed filter if any, else the hint text 35:4050
blinking caret toggles every second game tick (age % 2)
icon 134 when the filter is active (m49 and m50 both 3), else 133 (probably a search or clear icon)
the highlighted list row changed: recentre the map on it and start the move timer
no filter: draw the sector description wrapped into the info area

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the info panel for the sector on the galaxy map: owner, race, security level, population, planets, suns, size and, in jump modes, the energy needed for the jump ship. Also draws the search line, the keyboard hints, the description of the sector and the action info of the selected target.

comments.text: Blink flag toggled once per second.
INS_BuildGalaxyMap(scene, originX, originY, selectedX, selectedY, 0, scale in pixels).
INS_GetGalaxyMapPos fills the map positions table m86.

StartMenu.doc: Starts the menu's two background tasks: one toggles the blink flag every second and redraws the map, the other redraws it every 10 ms while the menu is open. Then builds the galaxy map for the origin and selected sectors and reads back the map positions.

ToggleMaximised.doc: Toggles the maximised flag, stores it on the class singleton, clears the hover state and relayouts.

comments.text: candidates: visible sectors, or in modes 41/42 sectors with a known name (text table 7)
case-insensitive prefix match against the typed text
matches are sorted by name; the first one is selected

UpdateFilteredSectors.doc: Rebuilds the list of sectors matching the search text: visible sectors (and, in modes 41/42, sectors with a known name) whose name starts with the text, sorted by name. Returns the first match, or the current sector when the text is empty.

2228.name: MenuGalaxyMap

2229.doc: Details page for a ship or ship type. It is created by ObjectActionMenu's details row and, in other modes, for station repair, reverse engineering, recycling, blueprints, ship-type preview and encyclopedia entries. The mode (m90) picks the title: 1 repair, 2 reverse engineering, 3 recycle, 4 blueprints, 0 ship details. Probably the game's ship details screen (no dobj name known).

0.name: laserArray

3.name: previewData

5.name: menuTarget

6.name: menuTargetArg

7.name: mode

8.name: encyclopediaMode

CreateNextForEncyclopedia.doc: Opens the encyclopedia entry for the type in arg3 (sets encyclopediaMode).

CreateNextForPreview.doc: Opens a preview of a ship type (arg3) for the player's ship. arg4 to arg6 are stored as the preview argument, table and flag.

CreateNextForRecycle.doc: Opens the details in recycle mode (3) for the ship given in arg4, with the station in arg3.

CreateNextForRepair.doc: Opens the details in repair mode (1) for the ship given in arg4, with the station in arg3.

CreateNextForReverse.doc: Opens the details in reverse-engineering mode (2) for the ship given in arg4, with the station in arg3.

comments.text: type views (previewData or encyclopediaMode set) use the type's body (type 7 in the body lookup)

GetObjectBody.doc: Body id of the displayed type in preview or encyclopedia mode (or when previewData is set); otherwise the base body.

GetSpeechID.doc: Speech id: for type views the ware name id plus 1, otherwise the object's description id.

comments.text: mode 0 = ship details; 1..4 = repair, reverse, recycle, blueprints
class 2064 ship types use a different title text (page 17)
lasers of the displayed ship, used by the weapons row

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the title for the current mode: repair, reverse, recycle or blueprints (texts 35:1102715, 1102716, 1102729, 1102701). Mode 0 shows the ship details text (35:821), or the class text 17:4741 for ship types of class 2064. Then loads the laser array.

cargoInfoVisible: operator precedence is && before ||, as written in the code
target not visible and not a preview: only the name line is shown

m91 preview of a ship type: description text from page 17 (GetWareDescriptionID)
m86 stored-ware table: lists type 9 entries (shields) and then type 8 entries (lasers); text 35:4511/4512 when empty
switch on m90: 1 = repair, 2 = reverse, 3 = recycle (drawn by C2303 helpers)
flight time is shown only for visible player-controlled ships of class 2134 (probably ships) that are not in the g43 hidden set
ID code and class code of the object, e.g. ABC-123 (XY)
shield values: 1000000 threshold switches to thousands display (text 35:962 vs 35:965)
speed line only for ships (2134) with a max speed, while the environment is a Sector (page 2006: 2001)
command, action and actionTarget are shown only to the owner or with the cheat flag
action 12: list of collision objects (SA_GetCollisionObjects); text 35:4002 when there are none
shield list: bay index shown from 1; this shows the shields installed on the object
upgrade bonus stored in the m86 table at key 1048593 (0x100011, probably ware type 16 subtype 17); speed is scaled by (10 + bonus) / 10
upgraded speed = base * extra percent / 10 + base
acceleration units: value / 500 gives m/s squared
transport class names from page 1999 (10 + class)
turret colour masks drawn via C2236.DrawMaskColors
wares not allowed for the owner race are tagged with the illegal text (35:964)
shipyards for this ship type: C300.FindAllShipyards(0x70000 | type, 0x200000)

installed lasers and shields are counted separately and shown with (*)
passenger list: names of the owners are shown in a column at passengerColumnX
marine skill shown as stars when the player may see it
script task debug info: only with script editor debug or cheat active
task table: [0] pid, [1] priority, [2] stack depth, [4] interrupt request, [5] stack, [6] interrupts blocked, [7] task id
relation to group: -1 enemy, 0 neutral, 1 friend
no object selected: three empty lines and the text 35:399

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the detail panel for the object in the target field (m33): ship identity, owner, sector, shields, hull, turrets, speed and wares. Modes: m90 selects repair, reverse, recycle or blueprint views, and m86 or m91 switch to a ship-type preview or stored-ware list instead of a live object. Stats of an unidentified type stay hidden.

2229.name: ShipDetailsMenu

2230.doc: Base of the ship-list screens (C2200 child). Shows a scrolling list of ships on the ship-list monitor texture and an info panel for the selected ship, with monitor views, tracking, comms and context menus. Children C2232 (landed ships), C2233 (owned ships), C2256 (change ship), C2305, C2325. Not named on page 2006.

0.doc: ship chosen in the list; -1 selects the header line, 0 none
0.name: selectedShip

1.name: sectorBackgroundInst

2.doc: instance of the ship-list frame (menu_shiplist)
2.name: shipListInst

comments.text: class 2016 objects give their complex hangar instead

Create.doc: Creates the menu on a target object; a complex hangar (class 2016) is replaced by its hangar object before the base Create.

CreateNext.doc: Same as Create for the next menu in a chain; the third argument is the target, replaced by its complex hangar when needed.

DrawScrollBarInfo.doc: Clears the redraw flag m65 and sets m67 when the scroll bar info is pending.

GetName.doc: Returns 0 for the base menu; the child menus return their own title text id.

GetText2Inst.doc: Returns the ship-list frame instance m84.

GetTextInst.doc: Returns the sector background instance m83.

HidesMonitor.doc: Returns true for monitor state 2, and for state 1 while the menu C640 is open.

client state flag 4 (probably a modal state) blocks the monitor keys
unknown objects (GetUnknown) only get a refusal line from page 13
view index 0 to 4, must be below the number of layout monitors
tracking only works for objects the monitor can track
comm menu: ships (class 2004) or class 2016 objects that are not complex hangars
details menu: the object must be visible to the player, else the no-equipment notice (7)

comments.text: no sensor/equipment: notice 7 for the player

SetupTexture.doc: Sets the texture sizes (384 x 1024) and the texture slot 20 used by the list.

comments.text: the background instance is created only when AddInst succeeds; the frame is created the same way

SpecialMenu.doc: Creates the background and ship-list frame instances, clears the menu texture, takes the menu title from GetName when it is not zero, then starts the menu.

SpecialMenuAction.doc: Default action for a menu without a special row: plays the failure sound. Child menus override it.

comments.text: the panel is drawn only for an existing object; otherwise the window is left empty
wing marker bar for own wingmen, coloured by the wing id
wing markers are drawn at the list row of the object
status line: docked (35:641) or in space (35:645)
owner object and its sector (text 35:730 Home)
destination (text 35:731 Dest.): a sector or an object; objects also show their sector
command and action lines are shown only to the owner or with the cheat flag; the player ship is skipped
order block: only for ships of another owner; wanted freight for commands 9, 10, 28 and 29
route distance through the gates (GS_RouteDist); -1 means no route, shown as ???
route distance plus a 5 percent margin, divided by max speed for the ETA

SpecialUpdateShip.doc: Draws the info panel for the ship arg1 (or an empty panel when it is null or gone): ID and class code, pilot, owner, home and destination sectors, commands and orders, route ETA, and shields, hull, lasers, speed and cargo summary lines.

CreateNext.doc: Creates this menu as the next menu on top of parentMenu for targetObject; delegates to the base CreateNext of 2200.

run the action of this line

switch on the action code m20

conditions: player ship docked at m33, owner is the player, client state bit 512 clear
start the self-destruct sequence

comments.text: sound 956 when the picked monitor differs from the tracking monitor
