CreateNext.doc: Creates the menu as a child of arg1 with the page mask in arg4 (0 or absent means all pages, 31).

comments.text: Reopen monitor (m20 - 1000) with the default external view mode.

CreatePrevious.doc: Going back: if the menu was opened for a monitor (m20 1001 or 1002) and the object still exists, reopens that monitor in its default external view mode. Then creates the base previous menu with 0, 0.

GenOnOff.doc: Returns the localized Yes (1102301) or No (1102302) text for a boolean, used by the on/off option lines.

GetLayoutMonitorsNum.doc: Maps a window layout index to the number of extra monitors it shows (0 for none).

comments.text: Only the gameplay page or the full menu use the base height.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Returns the base menu height for the full menu (pages 1 or 31), else a fixed height of 256 for a single page.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns object body id 190 for the menu panel (probably the options background).

GetScriptOptions.doc: Returns the table of script option entries (m96).

comments.text: option table: key code -> option id; 0 means the key is not an option
previousKey equals the key: auto-repeat ignored
radar range row advances on confirm; other rows run MenuAction
760/761 step left/right, 756 sets the minimum or off, 757 sets the maximum (see ChangeValue)
756 path: sound volumes to 0; warp, gamma and focus to minimum; toggles off
option 2003: relative mouse mode default
focus minimum comes from global parameter (89, 70)
gamma minimum is 1
option 9221 toggles D3D flag 128
client state bit 16384 blocks the overlay option: fail sound
option 9194 switches the key delays between 200/50 and 400/75 (initial/repeat)
option ids 1, 65536 .. 8388608 are game feature bits: XOR toggles the bit named by the id
after the 756 switch, break leaves the outer switch to the default select handling
757 (maximum) on the voice volume plays 'Command accepted' (13:131) unless speech is busy
warp factor maximum: 50 with the cheat active, otherwise 10

Input.doc: Key handler for the options screen (video, sound, input, debug rows). The key is mapped through the option table (m42) to an option id, and the id is then changed: 760/761 step the value, 756 sets the minimum or off, 757 sets the maximum. Confirm keys run MenuAction or ChangeValue. Returns 2 when handled, else the default select handling runs.

comments.text: rows 9900 to 9999 run the script bound to that numbered key (SE_TableNumberedKey)
row 9218 opens the sub-menu 2292 unless client state bit 1 blocks it
row 9224 resets the C631 state (tips or hints) and plays the success sound
row 9197 opens a confirm box with texts 35:4904 and 35:4905
rows 1000-1002: monitor context menu 153 for monitor row - 1000
monitor 0 (external view) has no connect entries

MenuAction.doc: Activates the selected option: toggles flags, runs the numbered scripts, opens sub-menus, or opens the context menu of a monitor (rows 1000 to 1002, monitor = row - 1000).

comments.text: Gamma is reset here, so a cancelled change is not kept.

MyKillHelper.doc: Restores the gamma value saved when the menu opened (m94), then runs the base kill helper.

comments.text: accepted: STA_DIDTransition(0) runs first, then the feature bit is set
game feature bit 65536 is set (probably the 'seen' flag of this prompt)

NotifyMsgBoxReturn.doc: When box 0 is answered with 1, ends the DID transition 0 and sets game feature bit 65536.

comments.text: 1002 Connect (text 35:4110): the sector map 2228 lets the player choose the target for this monitor
1003 Disconnect (text 35:4111): monitor mode is cleared
1006 Auto Target (text 35:4114): monitor switches to the default auto-target view
1007 Auto Missile (text 35:4118): monitor switches to the default auto-missile view

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Applies the monitor context menu choice: 1002 Connect opens the sector map 2228 to pick a target, 1003 Disconnect, 1006 Auto Target and 1007 Auto Missile switch the monitor to the default view for that mode.

comments.text: entry 1006 (auto target) is disabled when mode bit 8 is set
entry 1007 (auto missile) is disabled when mode bit 16 is set

OnContextMenuUpdate.doc: Enables or disables items of the monitor context menu (menu id 153) for the monitor in the selected row (row - 1000). Probably the auto-target and auto-missile entries are disabled from the monitor mode bits.

RemoveScriptOptions.doc: Removes the entry registered for the script id arg1.

comments.text: Volumes from SFX_GetFXVolume, SFX_GetMODVolume and SFX_GetVoiceVolume (0..255), scaled to 0..10000.
Title by page mask: 2 = Graphics (1904:110401), 4 = Audio (1904:110501), 1 = Gameplay (1904:110601), anything else = Options (35:4203).
Game features bitmask from C150.GetGameFeatures().
SETA warp factor; a stored 0 is treated as 6.
Default warp factor 6.
Layout index copied to the monitor layout field.
Radar range steps in metres (m91).
Radar range labels: first is Auto (35:4222), then 500 m, 1 km, 10 km, 25 km and 50 km.
Current radar range from C605.GetRadarRange().
Find the largest step not above the current range.
Chosen step; 0 when none matches.

SpecialMenu.doc: Reads the current volumes and graphics state, sets the page title and height from the page mask, reads the game features, warp factor, gamma, layout and radar range, then runs the base menu setup.

comments.text: Gameplay page (bit 1): SETA factor line (1102307, shown as x) and gravidar view range line (4202).
Graphics page (bit 2) starts here.
Gamma is only available when the system flag 64 is set; otherwise a greyed info line.
Field of view in degrees; the degree sign is UTF-8 bytes.
Post-process filter line (4040) is available only with shader quality 2; otherwise greyed.
View distance name from the 1912 table (Low, Medium, High, Very High).
Monitor section: shown in the gameplay page or the monitor-only bit, and not in client state 4.
Number of extra monitors for the current layout (GetLayoutMonitorsNum).
Monitor object id code; '(No Signal)' (4115) when the object has no object id or is outside the player's sector, '(Player)' (809) for the player ship g9.
Monitor mode text: bit 8 = auto target mode (4109), bit 16 = auto missile mode (4117), otherwise the object: cockpit name (2020:13), external view (4104), target view (4105).
No monitor object: 'Disconnected' (4108).
Monitor label: text 35:4640 + index (4640 Full Screen, 4641 Left Monitor, 4642 Right Monitor, ...).
Mode and object columns drawn only for visible lines.
Sound page (bit 4): effects, music and voice volumes as percent (value / 100).
Subtitles line (4249): the bit 131072 is inverted here, so the On state is shown when the bit is clear (probably a 'subtitles off' flag).
Verbose ship computer (4213) reads the setting from C150.GetVerbose().
Gameplay page (bit 1) options: auto save in stations, warp tunnel, fast menu, subtitles, confirmation on eject and station announcements, run in background.
Bit 8388608 is 'Disable War Reports' (4289).
Artificial life line (2020:42) is selectable only when the game is modified and plugins exist; otherwise greyed out.
Script options: each registered script entry is added as a line with id 9900 plus its index, if the script still exists (FindScript).

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the three option pages according to the page mask: gameplay lines (SETA, gravidar range, game flags, run in background, script options), graphics lines (gamma, field of view, post-process, view distance), audio volume lines, and the monitor section that lists the layout monitors with their objects and modes.

2259.name: MenuOptions

2261.doc: Text entry menu that changes the player's web user name (C150.GetWebUserName / SetWebUserName). Same labels as the ship rename (texts 35:1100057..1100059). Its object body id is 483. Probably the player's name shown in the game's own menus and multiplayer lists.

Create.doc: Opens the rename menu for the player (g8) with the current web user name as default.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the rename menu as the next menu in a chain.

GetContext.doc: Returns the UI context id 1012 (text entry).

GetName.doc: Returns the menu title text 35:1100057 'Change Name'.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns the body id 483 used for the menu's object view.

comments.text: CheckStringForCheats: a cheat code typed as a name is refused silently

ReturnPressed.doc: Confirm: names containing cheat strings are rejected (CheckStringForCheats) and the name is not changed; otherwise it is stored in C150.

2261.name: MenuRenamePlayer

2262.doc: Text input menu for a personal log entry, titled Log Entry (35:1102503, prompt 35:1102504). Parent C2252 (text input base). On confirm the typed text goes to the player's log through g8.LogString. No dobj or page 2006 name.

Create.doc: Opens the text input with the prompt 'Input Log Entry:' (35:1102504), empty default text and a 540 wide field (probably pixels). arg1 is not used.

CreateNext.doc: Same as Create, but as the next menu after the given previous menu. arg2 is passed to the base; the third argument is not used.

GetName.doc: Returns the menu title 'Log Entry' (35:1102503).

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns object body id 483.

ReturnPressed.doc: Writes the typed text (inherited field m84 of C2252) to the player's log and closes the menu.

2262.name: MenuLogEntry

2263.doc: Ship-upgrade submenu of the equipment dock (page 2006 class 2263, child of C2217). Lists the selected ships that can be equipped in one batch (text 35:1102512 Upgrade ships). Created by the equipment dock menu; it draws a summary of the chosen ships and their bodies.

Create.doc: Creates the menu through the base C2217 Create, then sets up the ship list.

CreateCommon.doc: Common constructor path that just returns the object.

CreateCommonShipEquip.doc: Stores the ship list and mode for this upgrade menu, takes the first ship of the list as the current one, and resets the list state.

CreateNext.doc: Creates the next menu in a chain through the base C2217 CreateNext, then sets up the ship list.

GetName.doc: Returns the menu title, text 35:1102512 (Upgrade ships).

GetObjectBody.doc: In single-ship mode returns the body id of the current ship's type; otherwise uses the base body. Returns -1 when the current ship no longer exists.

comments.text: group mode: keys are handled by the base C2217 Input
scrolling is allowed only in info mode (m5 == 2)

Input.doc: Keys 758/766 and 759/767 scroll the info text up and down, 762 and 763 page up and down, and 753 opens the group submenu. Other keys go to the base menu when not in single-ship mode.

MenuAction.doc: In single-ship mode opens a new C2263 in group mode for all the ships in m130 (equip several ships); otherwise the base action.

comments.text: single-ship mode only: the header, then the body of the first ship (group mode returns to the base menu at 0x12000b)
shields are counted per type; the table key is type + 1, because -1 means an empty slot
shield and laser lists show a 'None' line when the object has none (text 35:4511, 35:4512)
wares listed by g46 flag bit 1 (ware type 16, probably ship extensions); the count comes from GetWareTypeCountWithPredefined
end of the info panel; the single select line is OK (35:679)

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the menu: in group mode a count line (equip N ships at once), in single-ship mode the current ship's shields and lasers, and the list of wares it can take. Falls back to the base C2217 SpecialUpdate in group mode.

2263.name: MenuUpgradeShips

2265.doc: Text entry menu that renames a ship. Shows the current name and a new-name field (texts 35:1100057 'Change Name', 35:1100058, 35:1100059). On confirm it sets the ship's name and closes. Created with the ship as the parent object; default text length is 50 when not given.

comments.text: labels: 35:1100058 'Current Name', 35:1100059 'New Name'; the ship's name is the default text

Create.doc: Opens the rename menu for a ship. arg2 is the max name length (50 when 0).

CreateNext.doc: Opens the rename menu as the next menu in a chain. arg4 is the max name length (50 when 0).

GetContext.doc: Returns the UI context id 1012 (text entry).

GetName.doc: Returns the menu title text 35:1100057 'Change Name'.

ReturnPressed.doc: Confirm: writes the new name to the ship (m33) and closes the menu.

2265.name: MenuRenameShip

2266.doc: Freight exchange between two objects (page 35:1102402 'Freight Exchange'): the player's ship (leftObject) and another ship or station (rightObject) move wares, passengers and marines to each other through a trade bar. Opened from the exchange target list (class 2305). Not named in dobj; listed under MENU_PLAYER. Also used for freight drones (CreateFreightdrone).

0.doc: packed ware id (type<<16 | subtype) or passenger/marine object of the highlighted row
0.name: selectedItem

1.doc: cargo volume of one unit of the selected item
1.name: unitVolume

10.doc: first party of the exchange, the player's ship by default
10.name: leftObject

11.doc: second party of the exchange
11.name: rightObject

12.doc: 1 for freight drone mode or forced open (set by CreateFreightdrone and ForceOpen)
12.name: freightDroneMode

2.doc: 1 when both objects can carry the selected item
2.name: canTransferBoth

3.doc: signed units to move: positive into leftObject, negative into rightObject
3.name: transferAmount

4.doc: cargo volume of the selected item in leftObject
4.name: leftWareVolume

5.doc: cargo volume of everything else in leftObject
5.name: leftOtherVolume

6.doc: free cargo space of leftObject
6.name: leftFreeVolume

7.doc: cargo volume of the selected item in rightObject
7.name: rightWareVolume

8.doc: cargo volume of everything else in rightObject
8.name: rightOtherVolume

9.doc: free cargo space of rightObject
9.name: rightFreeVolume

ClickTradeBar.doc: Moves the transfer amount by the clicked delta in units (converted from volume), clamped by the free space of leftObject and the stock of rightObject.

comments.text: left side is the player's ship (g9)

Create.doc: Opens the exchange between the player's ship and the given object.

CreateFreightdrone.doc: Opens the exchange for a freight drone: sets freightDroneMode and creates the menu.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the exchange as the next dialog after previousMenu, with the player's ship on the left.

CreateNextCarrier.doc: Same as CreateNextRemote, used when the source is a carrier.

CreateNextRemote.doc: Opens the exchange as the next dialog between two given objects.

CreateRemote.doc: Opens the exchange between two given objects.

ForceOpen.doc: Sets freightDroneMode (m116) and returns the menu so the caller can open it even when nothing is selected (probably).

GetObjectBody.doc: Body of the selected ware type, or -1 when no row is selected.

comments.text: class 1700 objects (passengers/marines) have no ware video

GetObjectVideoID.doc: Video id of the selected ware type. Returns nothing for objects of class 1700.

GetSelectedWareWares.doc: Always 0: wares inside containers are not listed here.

comments.text: the base trade bar input runs first
757: all of rightObject's units, limited by leftObject free space

Input.doc: Keys while the trade bar is active: 757 moves the maximum toward leftObject, 756 the maximum toward rightObject, 761 and 760 step the amount up and down. Silently ignored outside the menu state (m5 != 2).

comments.text: passenger into leftObject: needs a cabin ware 16:39 on leftObject
passenger into rightObject: needs a cabin ware 16:39 on rightObject
success speech: marine or passenger voice, text 1286 (probably the generic transfer line)
fail speech: voice line 3943/24
ware major 8 = lasers: laser bays and TradeWare when the player buys
ware major 9 = shields
ware major 10 = missiles
ware 16:25 (id 1048601): restarts the grid manager (C605.RestartGrid), probably power or life support
ware 16:39 (id 1048615): life support check on the side that loses it
g46 bit 256: life support check on the side that gains the ware
result voice: 1274 installed, 1275 removed, 1286 otherwise

MenuAction.doc: Confirm key: applies the pending transfer. Passengers and marines (class 1700) move between the two objects; a passenger transfer needs a cabin ware (16:39) on the receiving side. Other wares move with TradeWare (lasers, to the player), AddShield, AddMissile or AddWare. Plays the result speech and refreshes the menu.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Clears the transfer amount when the selection moves, then calls the base handler.

comments.text: layout code 61

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the title (text 35:1102402 'Freight Exchange') and clears the trade state before the base setup.

comments.text: column x: 256 for the right side amounts, 306 for the left side amounts
g46 per-ware flag table: bit 1 hides a ware from this list
row colour: 0 = both sides can carry it, 4 = greyed out
unit volume of the selected row
m106 set when both objects can transport the row
text 4502 'None(Goods)' when the goods list is empty
section for installed ship extensions: ware major 16 with g46 bit 1 and without bits 4 and 8
text 4503 'None(Ship Extensions)' when empty
passengers and marines are exchanged only when both sides are capable
selection changed: reset the transfer amount and step size
trade bar lines: the left and right names, then counts after the pending transfer
volume text 1102540 'F:' (short form) when the total is above 9999, else 1102510 'Freight'

SpecialUpdate.doc: Redraws the exchange: the union of wares both sides hold, grouped by ware major type 16 down to 8, with per-side counts and volume. Greys out rows that one side cannot carry. Lists passengers and marines when both sides can carry them. Shows the trade bar for the selected row. Shows text 35:1102408 when the other object has no exchange targets.

SpecialUpdateMarines.doc: Lists the marines of one side with their skill stars. Selecting a marine sets up the trade bar with the volume of a marine (ware 16:107).

comments.text: row colour 1 = selectable when the other side is passenger capable, else 4
passenger is on the left side when the list belongs to the right side

SpecialUpdatePassengers.doc: Lists the non-marine passengers of one side. Selecting a passenger sets up the trade bar with the volume of a passenger (ware 12:22).

2266.name: MenuFreightExchange

2267.doc: Jump destination menu (child of the 2202 menu base; title text 35:4237 'Jump destination'). Lists gateless sectors the jump drive can reach with the energy needed for each, and offers 'Select from map' for the galaxy map. Used by JumpDriveMenu.

0.doc: sector the jump is planned from, set by CreateNextScript
0.name: originSector

Create.doc: Creates the menu for the player ship (g9).

CreateNext.doc: Creates the menu as the next menu of arg1 for the player ship.

CreateNextScript.doc: Script variant of CreateNext: stores arg4 (or the sector of arg3) as the origin sector for the menu.

comments.text: first menu of the chain (m0 == 0) starts the jump toward arg1

CreatePrevious.doc: Creates the menu as the previous menu. When this is the first menu (m0 == 0) it also starts the jump to arg1 through JumpDriveMenu.

GetCoordString.doc: Formats an index as a letter (index / 10) and a digit (index % 10), e.g. C7.

GetName.doc: Returns the name of the jump drive ware (16/35) from its text id.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns the object body for the jump drive ware type (16/35).

Input.doc: Default input handling.

comments.text: select from map: map 2228 centred on the origin sector (or the current sector)
with an origin sector the choice is stored in m3 and the menu stops (probably the result read by the caller)

MenuAction.doc: Executes the chosen line: 'Select from map' opens the galaxy map at the origin sector; a sector (2001) or warp gate (2014) is used as the jump destination, or returned as the result when an origin sector exists.

SpecialMenu.doc: Calls the base menu setup without changes.

comments.text: sectors without an owner are not listed
packed coordinate for display: x * 3270 + y * 179 split into three letter/digit codes; probably the galaxy grid code, not the map position

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the menu: the header with the jump energy cost, then one line per reachable gateless sector owned by somebody, with its coordinates and energy cost.

2267.name: JumpSectorMenu

2268.doc: Trade menu of a station or ship for the 'Trade Utilities' list (page 2006 text 35:1102458). Shows two tabs (class 5004 and 5008 objects) of wares the station offers, with availability and docking checks. The context menu docks at the station, buys or sells there (commands 7, 81 and 82). Probably the menu behind the station's trade screen.

0.doc: object the prices and availability are checked for; default is the player ship
0.name: refObject

1.doc: ware key of the selected line: type << 16 | ware id
1.name: selectedWareKey

comments.text: ware type 16 counts the predefined ware of the utility's product id

CheckInstalled.doc: Returns whether a utility is installed for the reference object: the utility itself when there is no reference object, the ware type count for a station, or the player's equipment for the player ship (2079).

Create.doc: Opens the trade menu for a target object with refObject as the reference object.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the trade menu as the next menu in a chain. arg4 is the reference object.

GetIcon.doc: Returns icon 6 on tab 0 and 5 on tab 1.

comments.text: tab cycling loop: wraps over the two tabs and stops at the first installed one
609: ware info (C2319.OpenWareInfo) for the selected ware, failure sound otherwise

Input.doc: Key handler. 760/761 switch tabs left and right, skipping tabs that are not installed. 673/674 select tab 0/1 directly. 576 tracks the object on the monitor, 610 opens its details. 609 opens the ware info of the selected ware.

comments.text: reference object defaults to the player ship when missing or a 2079 object
button 1: details, input code 610

MenuAction.doc: Opens the context menu for the selected line: 'Info' (35:812, code 610) and, for a station, the trade actions: 2 'Dock At Station', 3 'Buy At Station' (tab 1 only), 4 'Sell At Station' (tab 0 only).

comments.text: choice 1: ware information for the selected ware
choice 2: 'Dock At Station' = ExecuteCommand 7 on the selected object
choice 3 'Buy At Station': command 81 with the ware key and object (65543 = 0x10007)
choice 4 'Sell At Station': command 82 with the same arguments

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Runs the chosen trade action. 1: ware info; 2: dock (command 7 on the selected object); 3 'Buy At Station' and 4 'Sell At Station': commands 81 and 82 as script commands with the ware and selected object. Speaks line 1264 (player) or 131 (others).

comments.text: button greyed out when docking is not possible or not allowed
button 3 needs command upgrade 81
button 4 needs command upgrade 82

OnContextMenuUpdate.doc: Enables the trade buttons. Buttons 2 to 4 need the station to allow docking for the reference object; button 3 needs command upgrade 81 and button 4 upgrade 82.

comments.text: a utility that is not installed: NotifyNotInstalled and no change

SelectTab.doc: Switches to tab 0 (class 5004) or tab 1 (class 5008). Fails with a not-installed notice when the utility is not installed. Sets the menu object to the tab object and runs the base SelectTab.

comments.text: product 33 opens tab 0, product 32 opens tab 1
every ware line in the target's menu lines becomes known to the player (g8.SetWareKnown)

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the title (35:1102458 'Trade Utilities'), selects the tab from the product id of the target (33 = tab 0, 32 = tab 1), marks the listed wares as known to the player, then runs the base SpecialMenu.

comments.text: column x positions: 240, 290, 340, 389 and the right-aligned value column
tab 1 only: race may trade this ware type with the station's owner
docking must be allowed and possible for the reference object
greyed name when the reference object cannot transport this ware type

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the list: text lines (type 0), headers (type 1) and ware lines (type 2) with five columns. A ware line is greyed out when the reference object cannot trade it or docking is not possible.

2268.name: MenuTradeUtilities

2269.doc: Ware transfer menu: loads wares bought at a station into one of the player's ships ('Load into', text 35:1102461). Lists ships of the player that have free cargo room for the ware (class 2032 transport ships). Confirming buys the amount from the station and adds it to the chosen ship; the price is taken from player money.

0.doc: ship chosen in the list, receives the wares
0.name: selectedShip

1.doc: ware key: type << 16 | ware id
1.name: wareKey

2.doc: stored argument from Create/CreateNext; not read in this batch
2.name: extraArg

3.doc: total credits to pay for the purchase
3.name: price

4.doc: station the wares are bought from
4.name: station

5.doc: number of units to load
5.name: amount

Create.doc: Opens the menu for a station, ware key, price and amount.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the menu as the next menu in a chain.

GetName.doc: Returns the title text 35:1102461 'Load into'.

GetRaceBody.doc: Returns the race body of the player's owner.

Input.doc: Key handler: delegates to the default select input.

comments.text: the ware is added to the ship; the money leaves the player's account at the same time

MenuAction.doc: Buys the ware: adds the amount to the selected ship, subtracts the price from player money, plays the sound, and closes the menu.

comments.text: speech: ware name, then line 1273

PlayBought.doc: Plays the purchase sound (955) and speaks 'Loaded <ware>' with speech line 1273 in a fork.

comments.text: wareKey: type in bits 16..23, ware id in the low 16 bits
name of each candidate ship is drawn; the selected one is stored in selectedShip

SpecialUpdate.doc: Lists the player's transport ships (class 2032) that can take amount of the ware, and shows the ware and amount in the info line. Ships owned by others are listed only when hired.

2269.name: MenuLoadWare

2270.doc: Ware menu for 'Unload' (text 35:1102462): lists the cargo of a ship or station that can be built or unloaded (ware types 5 and 6). Choosing a ware opens the build-station menu (2216) in the sector, when the object is in the player's sector, not docked, and has an id.

0.doc: ship or station whose cargo is listed
0.name: wareSource

Create.doc: Opens the menu for a ship or station. Resets the selected ware.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the menu as the next menu in a chain.

GetName.doc: Returns the title text 35:1102462 'Unload'.

comments.text: ware type 6 and 5 map to their own body id

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns the body id of the selected ware type, or 190 when no ware is selected.

Input.doc: Key handler: delegates to the default select input.

comments.text: guard: object exists, a ware is selected, its environment is a sector equal to the player's sector, it has an id, and it is not docked
2216 CreateNextForBuildStation: mode 29 is the build-station mode

MenuAction.doc: Opens the build-station menu (2216, mode 29) for the selected ware when the object is in the player's sector, not docked and has an id. Otherwise plays the failure sound and closes.

comments.text: ware key split: type in bits 16..23, id in the low 16 bits; only types 5 and 6 are listed

SpecialUpdate.doc: Lists each ware of types 5 and 6 with its count, one line per unit. Shows the object name and id in the info line.

2270.name: MenuUnloadWare

2271.doc: Script editor menu. Lists the MSCI scripts of the game (C700 scripts), shows a script's commands and their arguments, and edits them: insert, delete, cut, copy, paste, comment, add or remove arguments, call other scripts, rename and copy scripts. Its states also show script statistics and the debug options of the reference object. Child pickers are 2272, 2273 and 2274. Base class 2203. No dobj name.

0.doc: typewriter position in the intro text; -1 once it is done (statistics view)
0.name: introCharPos

1.doc: 1 once the intro text has been shown in this session
1.name: editorStarted

10.doc: cut or copied command or argument
10.name: clipboard

11.doc: command group record shown in state 4 (name text in page 2005)
11.name: commandGroup

12.doc: index of the parameter the cursor is on in the command line
12.name: paramIdx

2.doc: editor screen id: 0 intro and statistics, 1 script list, 3 commands of the edited script, 4 command groups, 16 help, others are child pickers
2.name: editorState

3.doc: script object (C701) being edited
3.name: editedScript

4.doc: 1 when the edited script changed since it was opened
4.name: modified

5.doc: argument value being built for a command argument
5.name: argBuffer

6.doc: sorted list of script names shown in the script list
6.name: scriptKeys

7.doc: script record selected in the list, or command spec in state 14
7.name: selectedEntry

8.doc: number of argument parts entered so far
8.name: argCount

9.doc: clipboard kind: 1 command, 0 argument
9.name: clipboardIsCommand

AddParamClickArea.doc: Adds a click area for one parameter of the selected command line. The x position is computed from the column (m28) and the column width (m56).

comments.text: Line id 8 toggles the global debug information flag.
Debug-mode cycling; the switch order depends on the sign of the direction.

ChangeValue.doc: Cycles the script debug mode of the selected script (or the global task 702) by one step: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 for forward, reverse for backward. Key 8 toggles debug information instead.

comments.text: command 102 (call script) with a type-5 parameter: parameter types come from the called script's argument list
command 104 with parameter type 30: treated as a fixed parameter type

CmdParInput.doc: Starts the argument picker for parameter arg2 of the command pair arg1 ([0] command head, [1] parameter flags). Parameter types 2, 3, 6 and 8 open the nested value picker 2272 with the current value; other types open the Script Input picker 2273. Returns the child menu, or 0 when the parameter takes no input.

Create.doc: Opens the editor with the help state (16) before the first use or the statistics state (0) after it. Resets the modified flag, the clipboard and the typewriter position, reinitialises the editor structures, then calls the base Create.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the editor in the given state for the script arg3; a state of 0 uses the default for this session. Resets the same fields as Create and calls the base CreateNext.

CreateNextEdit.doc: Opens a new script object created from the template arg2 in the command editor (state 3). With a name it sets the name and the default description (text 1265:53) and marks the script modified.

CreateNextSelCmd.doc: Opens the command group picker (state 4) for script arg2, remembering the group record arg3 in commandGroup.

comments.text: state 2: a new script name was entered; open the editor for it
state 14: the picked value goes to the command spec picker 2274
state 7: find script by name
state 9: copy the current script under the new name
state 10: the command is inserted or replaced; calls to script 102 open the script choice, 104 gets a fixed flag layout
a command with parameters asks for each parameter (state 11)
state 13: a script call (command 102) takes the chosen script's parameter list
state 11: store one parameter value and move to the next free parameter (flag 2 = fixed)
state 12: argument entry; first part is a type, then a value, then the argument is appended or replaced

CreatePrevious.doc: Receives the value from the child picker that was open and applies it according to editorState: new script name, copy or find script, rename or describe the script, add or replace a command, add call targets, set argument values, add a new argument. Returns the child menu or the base result.

Disable.doc: Disables the menu only when it is no longer in its initial state (m5 != 0).

GetContext.doc: Returns the help context id 1018 for the script menu.

GetName.doc: Menu title: the command group name (text page 2005) in state 4, otherwise text 1265:0.

comments.text: states 0 and 16: fast refresh only while the intro text is being typed

GetUpdateDelay.doc: Refresh interval: 50 ms while the intro types out, 1000 ms on the statistics view before the start, 10000 ms in the other states.

comments.text: key 881 on the list: state 7 (find script), opens the name picker 2272 with kind 2
key 883 on the list with a selected entry: state 14, opens the object picker 2273 with kind 22
key 888 in state 3 on a command line: inserts an empty command {2} before the cursor
key 888 on an argument position: inserts a new argument named argN, with the next free number
key 889 deletes the selected command or argument; on the list it asks to delete the script (text 1265:41)
key 890 cut: a command goes to the clipboard with clipboardIsCommand = 1
key 890 cut of an argument: clipboardIsCommand = 0. Note: paste (892) only handles commands, so a cut or copied argument cannot be pasted
key 891 copy of a command is stored; copy of an argument is not stored
key 892 paste: only a command clipboard is pasted (m95 == 1)
key 893 removes an argument slot of a call command when the cursor is inside the argument list
key 894 inserts an argument slot before the cursor; the new slot gets flag 1

Input.doc: Key handling by editorState. 752 aborts (OnAbort); 753 accepts (MenuAction); 758-759 and 766-767 move the cursor; 760-761 move the parameter cursor in state 3; 762-763 page; 881 starts a find-script picker from the list; 883 starts a script call target pick; 886-887 comment and uncomment; 888 inserts a command or a new argument slot; 889 deletes; 890 cuts; 891 copies; 892 pastes; 893-894 remove or add an argument slot.

comments.text: Editor state flag is set before the sample plays and the menu refreshes.
Case 2: reload script caches and run the setup scripts.
Cases 3 and 8: change the highlighted debug value (see ChangeValue).
Case 4: clear script debug messages of the selected script or of the global task (702).
Case 6: enter state 16 (leave menu) and play the login sample.
State 1: script list. Entry with index 0 creates a new script, others edit the selected one.
State 3: command list of a script. Negative line ids are headers: -1000 version, -1001 description, -1002 extra menu, below that the script arguments.
Command line: parameter flag bit 2 marks a read-only parameter, which cannot be edited (sample 956 as feedback).
Free line: open the command picker (state 10) from C700.GetCmdMenuDefs.
State 4: picked a command. Expression type 8 opens a sub-menu; otherwise the command array and its parameter flags are built.
Parameter flag array is built only when the command has parameters; flag 262144 in the command flags is passed to it.
Pack the new command array and flags into m3 (state word).

MenuAction.doc: Acts on the selected line of the script menu, depending on the menu state m88: 0 main list (reload scripts, debug switches, clear debug messages, open the script list, leave), 1 script list (new or edit a script), 3 command list of a script (edit a parameter, add a command), 4 command picker (insert the chosen command), 16 leave.

comments.text: Box id 1 is the delete-script confirmation; answer 1 deletes.
Box id 2 is the save-script prompt; answer 1 saves, answer 8 (cancel) keeps the editor open.
Script does not resolve: show the 'Script Error' box with the parser message.

NotifyMsgBoxReturn.doc: Handles the answer of a message box. State 1 deletes the script on confirm. State 3 saves the script after it is resolved (or shows the error box), then closes the editor if the answer was not cancel.

comments.text: State 16 leave: login sample if the menu was in login mode, otherwise logout sample.
Unsaved script: open the 'Save Script' box and wait for its answer.

OnAbort.doc: Back/abort handler. Leaving state 16 restores the login or logout sound. In the script editor, unsaved changes ask for a save first (text 1265:19), otherwise the editor is closed.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Resets the highlighted parameter index when the selected line changes, then calls the base handler.

comments.text: Read-only parameter: click is ignored.
Selecting a different parameter plays the select sample; a repeat click runs MenuAction.

OnClickArea.doc: Click on a command parameter: the first click selects the parameter, a second click on the same one runs MenuAction. Read-only parameters are ignored.

comments.text: Read-only parameter: the hover is ignored.

OnMouseOverClickArea.doc: Hover over a command parameter highlights it, unless the parameter is read-only (flag 2).

SetCurrentLineAsCmdLongLine.doc: When the current line directly follows the long-line marker of the previous command, extends that command's line count by one and clears the marker (probably for commands written over several text lines).

SetEditorStarted.doc: Sets editorStarted so the intro text is not typed again.

SortScriptNames.doc: Fills scriptKeys with the names of all scripts and sorts them by name.

SpecialMenu.doc: Resets the scroll counter and, on the script list (state 1), sorts the script names first.

comments.text: intro: the typewriter shows the first 54 lines of text, m86 is the character position
statistics page text is hard-coded English
debug options: 3 = script debugging of the reference object, 0 Off, 1 Log, 2 Trace; the global option is shown without an object
reference object destroyed: debugging shows ???
additional debug information On or Off
state 16: help text 1265:201 and 1265:202
state 3: header is the edited script's name; the version and description lines use entries -1000 and -1001
script call target: a type 2 or 11 value is shown as is, other values as text 2010 and 2011 pairs
command lines are rendered by TransformSourceTextForOutput; the current line is highlighted

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the current screen by editorState. State 0 types out the intro, then shows the script statistics and the debug options of the reference object or the global runner. State 16 shows the help text. State 1 lists the scripts with their version and size. State 3 lists the edited script's name, version, description, call target, arguments and command lines. State 4 lists the commands of a command group.

2271.name: ScriptEditor

2272.doc: Text and number input box of the script editor (page 1265: 'Input Script Name', 'Input Label Name', 'Input Argument Name', 'Input Number'...). Built on the text input menu base (2252). Validates the entered value for the input kind (number, identifier, free text) and checks that script, label or argument names are unique. Returns the value to the caller through the menu result.

0.doc: what is being entered: 3 number, 0/10001 variable or argument name, 1/6 label, 7 script name, 2/-10 text, 8 comment
0.name: inputKind

1.doc: script object whose argument names and labels are checked for duplicates (probably)
1.name: editedScript

2.doc: value before editing; an unchanged argument name is allowed
2.name: originalValue

3.doc: extra info line drawn under the box, may be empty
3.name: infoText

4.doc: validation message shown after a rejected entry; cleared on the next key
4.name: errorText

comments.text: Kinds: 3 number (prompt 1265:5, digits and minus); 0/1/6/7/10001 identifiers (letters, digits and dot); 8 comment (80 chars); -10 and 2 and default: free string (80 chars, prompt 1265:17).
Inside the identifier group: 0 variable name (1265:6), 10001 argument name (1265:25), 1/6 label name (1265:14), 7 script name (1265:3).

CreateNext.doc: Opens the input box for kind arg2 with the given script (arg3), current value (arg4) and info text (arg5). Picks the prompt text and the maximum length per kind, sets the allowed character set and calls the base CreateNext.

GetName.doc: Returns the input title stored by the base class (m90).

comments.text: Any key other than the one that opened the box clears the error text.

Input.doc: Clears the error text on any key except the current one, then passes the key to the base input handler.

comments.text: Signed integer check: ^-?[0-9]+$ (kind 3).
Identifier check: letter first, then letters, digits or dots.
Argument names (kind 10001): the name must be new (not equal to the original value m98) and not already an argument of the script.
Duplicate argument name: message 1265:104 'Argument name already exists!'.
Script names (kind 7) must not exist yet: C700.FindScript. Message 1265:101 'Script name already exists!'.
Label names (kind 6) must not exist yet in the script labels. Message 1265:102 'Label name already exists!'.
Kind 8 (comment) accepts any text.
Nothing matched: message 1265:103 'Invalid format!'.

ReturnPressed.doc: Validates the entered text for the input kind. On success it stops the menu and returns a typed value {type, value} to the caller (number type 4, names as 1, argument names as 131074, numbers as 5). On failure it sets the error text and plays the fail sound.

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the base input box, then the info text (m99) under it if set.

Update.doc: Redraws the input box and the error text (m100) in red, then sets the cursor column to m31.

2272.name: ScriptTextInput

2273.doc: Script Input picker (text 1265:7). Lets the player choose one argument of a script command: a constant, variable, label, script, command, signal, ware, factory type or object, and returns it as a typed {type, value} array. Opened by script-editing menus (probably 2271 and 2274) and by the command console; it opens the list menu 2275 or galaxy-map pickers 2216/2228 for object choices. Base class 2202. No dobj name.

0.doc: parameter kind id of the argument being picked (GetParDefFlags index, or a special picker kind)
0.name: selectKind

1.doc: script whose variables and labels are offered; 0 when none
1.name: scriptObj

2.doc: text shown in the info line at the bottom of the menu
2.name: infoText

3.doc: typed {type, value} array of the entry last chosen; returned on stop
3.name: selectedValue

4.doc: 1 when opened from the command console (CreateNextForCmdConsole)
4.name: cmdConsoleMode

5.doc: 1 when the menu runs in user-input mode (SetGetUserInput)
5.name: userInputActive

6.doc: 1 while the user-input menu is open; cleared when it closes
6.name: userInputOpen

7.doc: context object for user-input picks (sector or object)
7.name: userInputContext

8.doc: result array of user input, {type, value}; default {0, -1}
8.name: userInputResult

9.doc: when set, galaxy pickers get the reference object (base field m33)
9.name: galaxyUsesRef

CreateNext.doc: Opens the picker for a parameter kind as the next menu of previousMenu. Stores kind, context object, script (variables and labels) and info text, clears the return value and the cmd-console flag, then calls the base CreateNext.

comments.text: no list for this kind: plain CreateNext path (console stays as parent)

CreateNextForCmdConsole.doc: Opens the picker from the command console (cmdConsoleMode = 1). If the list menu cannot open, falls back to the base CreateNext. Otherwise it links itself as the next menu of the console and a fork deletes the console when this picker closes.

comments.text: first switch: wraps the value by kind (m20). 65542/65543/65544/65553/65562 are type codes of the value (probably object, sector, ware, constant, label)
kind 52: position vector, each coordinate divided by 500 (probably map units)
second switch: kinds 56-58 pick the type (object class 2001 or other)
user-input mode: copy the result or the default {0, -1} into userInputResult, then close

CreatePrevious.doc: Builds the value handed back to the calling script command. The chosen value is wrapped as a typed argument for the current kind (for example {65542, sector}), or as an expression tree for kinds 21, 46-48, 52. In user-input mode it fills userInputResult and closes; otherwise it calls the base CreatePrevious.

CreateUserInput.doc: Opens the picker in user-input mode for another menu. A fork polls the active menu every 50 ms: when this picker becomes active it opens the select list, and it kills itself when the menu stack no longer holds it. Returns this, or nothing when Create fails.

Disable.doc: Disables the menu only when it is no longer in its initial state (m5 != 0).

GetName.doc: Menu title: text 1265:7 (Script Input).

GetUserDesc.doc: In user-input mode returns infoText as the description of the current request; otherwise nothing.

GetUserInputReturn.doc: In user-input mode returns userInputResult; otherwise nothing.

Input.doc: Key 800 closes the menu and is consumed. Other keys go to the default select input.

comments.text: kinds -106..-100, -101, 0, 4, 15 return the chosen value; other codes are navigation entries

MenuAction.doc: On Enter: if a list menu is open for the current entry (OpenSelectMenu probe returns 0), stores selectedValue as the return value and stops the menu. Entries with codes -106..-100, -101, 0, 4 and 15 are value entries.

NotifyMsgBoxReturn.doc: Answer of the message box opened for kind 63. Yes stores {4, 1} as the result, no stores {4, 0}, and the menu closes.

OpenGalaxyMenu.doc: Opens a galaxy-map picker in the given map mode for a sector. Uses the reference-aware picker 2216 when galaxyUsesRef is set, otherwise 2228.

comments.text: sector for galaxy pickers: userInputContext in user-input mode, otherwise the reference object or the player's sector (g8)
dispatch on the pick kind; kinds 3/10 and 2/11 open the nested value picker 2272 with a type code, -102 to -103 likewise (0, 1)
kinds 31/32 open the list with their own command kind, others use kind 33 (signal list)

OpenSelectMenu.doc: Opens the next menu for pick kind arg1 (the value of m20 on Enter). With probe set, returns 1 without opening when the kind is supported. Galaxy-map kinds resolve the sector first: the user-input context, the reference object's sector, or the player's sector. Returns 1 when a menu opened, 0 otherwise.

SetGetUserInput.doc: Switches the menu into user-input mode with a context object, a default result array and the galaxyUsesRef flag. Returns this.

comments.text: list is rebuilt from scratch: m20 = -1 means nothing chosen yet
kind 30 (operations): entries are {15, op} values; op 65555 is skipped
variable entries are offered when the script is known and the kind's parameter flags include 131072 or 327680 (probably: argument may be a variable); kind 64 is always included
variable entries: header 1265:11 Available Variables; values are {131074, index}
no variables: prints '-- (Script Variables) --' (text 35:4531)
header 1265:34 Constants; constants with index below 100 are listed, except non-object ones for kind 20
constants are listed in reverse sorted order; values are {131075, constId}
header 1265:7 Script Input
-101 with {0, 0} is the 'null' entry (text 1265:33)
flag 262144 = the kind allows the generic Number entry (1265:8)
kinds 25 and 28: entry {131074, -2147483647} is a reserved variable index, text 1265:36 (no return value)
kind 28: entry {131074, -2147483646} is a second reserved index, text 1265:47
kind 64: two fixed entries TRUE (2002:10, value 10) and FALSE (2002:9, value 9), type 131075 (constant)
kinds 31/32/other: header text picks command (1265:50), signal (1265:51) or both (1265:52)
kind 1: label entries {1, name}; -103 is the New Label entry (1265:12)
kind 7: scripts listed by name, values {1, name}
kinds 10000 and 62: parameter definitions with flag 1048576 (not 20); parameter 53 is skipped for kind 62

SpecialUpdate.doc: Fills the select list for the current selectKind. Kinds cover operations (30), script variables and labels, scripts, parameter definitions, constants (53), signals and commands, and the fixed entries (<Number>, <String>, <Variable>, <New Label>, null, Operations). Adds header lines and the filter tab bar's related entries.

UserInputOpen.doc: In user-input mode returns userInputOpen; otherwise returns nothing. Used by the menu system to tell whether this picker is still open for user input.

2273.name: ScriptInputMenu

2274.doc: Execute Command Script menu (text 1265:29). Runs a script command with arguments: it asks for each argument in turn through the Script Input picker 2273, then starts the script (or runs it synchronously) on the reference object or on the global script runner (702). Opened by script-editing and object menus (2271 and others, probably). Base class 2203.

0.doc: command descriptor array: [0] description, [5] argument names, [7] argument {type, default} list
0.name: commandSpec

1.doc: bit flags: 1 run synchronously, 2 command console, 4 cancel result, 8 start frozen, 16 speak, 32 no object, 64 prefilled, 128 callback, 256 keep in wing
1.name: callFlags

2.doc: priority passed to the script start call (probably; debug view shows Prio)
2.name: taskPriority

3.doc: index of the argument being asked for, also count of filled values
3.name: argIndex

4.doc: flat {type, value} pairs of the arguments collected so far
4.name: scriptArgs

5.doc: script id for ThisScriptID calls (0 for the default start)
5.name: scriptId

6.doc: preset argument pairs; -1 in the type slot means ask the user
6.name: presetArgs

7.doc: callback pair for StartScriptCallback and prefilled arguments
7.name: callbackRef

CreateNext.doc: Opens the command menu with no preset arguments; the last parameter is the initial argument list.

comments.text: flag 64: the first argument slot is prefilled with the callback pair
initial arguments fill the next free slots until the argument list is full
fork: when this menu becomes active again, if no further picker opened, return to the parent and delete this menu

CreateNextAddArgs.doc: Full constructor. In command-console mode (flag 2) it links itself to the previous menu and a fork resumes or closes it when the menu becomes active again. Otherwise it calls the base CreateNext. Returns this or the base result.

CreateNextSkip.doc: Like CreateNext, but also takes a callback pair and passes no presets.

comments.text: a value of expression type 8 is taken as the next argument
result is 0 when flag 4 is set, otherwise 1

CreatePrevious.doc: Receives the value chosen in the picker (an expression of type 8 continues argument input). Otherwise closes the menu and returns to the parent with result 1, or 0 when flag 4 is set (probably cancel). Without a parent calls the base CreatePrevious.

Disable.doc: Disables the menu only when it is no longer in its initial state (m5 != 0).

GetName.doc: Menu title: text 1265:29 (Execute Command Script).

Input.doc: Keys 762 and 763 page through the info text; other keys go to the default select input. Key 753 is handled as accept (MenuAction).

MenuAction.doc: Accept: resets argIndex and the scriptArgs buffer, then continues argument input; stops the menu when no picker was opened (the script was started).

comments.text: first info line is the command description m86[0]
long argument lines are wrapped at 89 characters per info line

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the command description, the argument list with type names and defaults, and the wrapped command text; 'No Arguments' when the command takes none.

comments.text: no reference object or flag 32: start the script with the global start call
flag 128: start through the callback pair
flag 1: run synchronously; otherwise start as a background task
reference object of class 9001 (predefined): speak its text id; else generic voice line 131
reference object is a ship (2004) or 2016: start the script on that object
voice 1264 when the object is g9 (probably the player's ship), else 131
a ship in a wing with scriptId 0 leaves its wing unless flag 256 is set

___nextArgInput.doc: Stores the argument just chosen (arg1, or nothing when 0) and moves to the next one. When all arguments are filled it starts the script and returns nothing; otherwise it opens the picker 2273 for the next argument (command console or normal) and returns its menu. Returns 0 when the script was started.

2274.name: ScriptCommandMenu

2275.doc: Picker list for the script editor (page 1265: 'Select Ware', 'Select Station Type', 'Select Ship Type', 'Select Fleet Commander', 'Select Flight Wing' and others). Shows the list of wares, station or ship types, or a fixed set of choices, sorted by name, with optional filter lines and a 3D preview of the highlighted type. Created by the wing command console (2278) for script-value entries of the given kind.

0.doc: which list to show: 13 ware, 17 station type, 19 ship type, 61/70/71 flight wing, fleet commander or global parameter, others from page 1265
0.name: pickerKind

1.doc: array of choices for the kind: packed (main type << 16 | subtype) or ids
1.name: choices

2.doc: label of the object the value is picked for (given by the caller, e.g. the fleet name)
2.name: targetLabel

3.doc: index of the chosen line; -1 until one is chosen (probably)
3.name: selectedIndex

4.doc: index of the highlighted line; -1 for none (probably)
4.name: highlightIndex

5.doc: text of the filter-type line: 35:4266 'Filter Type'
5.name: filterTypeText

6.doc: text of the filter-race line: 35:4267 'Filter Race'
6.name: filterRaceText

7.doc: text of the filter line picked last (set in AddSelectFilterLine)
7.name: selectedFilterText

8.doc: packed type code (type << 16 | subtype) of the highlighted entry for the 3D preview; 0 = none
8.name: previewTypeCode

AddSelectFilterLine.doc: Adds a filter line with label arg1, id arg2; the line is marked selected when arg3 equals arg2. A successfully added line stores its label in m90.

comments.text: Kind 13 (Select Ware): wares of main types 11, 13, 14, 15, 12, 16, 8, 10 and 9.
Kind 17 (Select Station Type): main types 5 and 6.
Kind 19 (Select Ship Type): all ship subtypes that have a body and a ship class above 0, except subtype 275.
Names: main type 6 uses the extended factory name; others use the ware name.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the picker of kind arg2 as a sub-menu of arg1, with target label arg3. Builds the choice array (wares of selected main types for 13, station types for 17, ship types for 19), sorts it by name and calls the base CreateNext.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Returns a fixed 128 pixel height for the two Yes/No picker kinds (63, 64); otherwise the base height.

comments.text: Titles per kind come from table 1265: 13 Select Ware (28), 17 Select Station Type (38), 19 Select Ship Type (39), 61 Select Flight Wing (79), 70 Select Fleet Commander (87), 71 Select Global Parameter (88), 62 Select Script Reference Type (85), 63/64 Select Yes/No (80).

GetName.doc: Returns the picker title for the kind m83 from the 1265 text table, or an empty string.

comments.text: Preview is available for kinds 13, 17 and 19 when m91 is set: the type comes from the high bits, the subtype from the low 16 bits.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns the body of the highlighted type (m91) for the preview; -1 when there is none.

GetRaceBody.doc: Returns the race body of the player faction g8.

HidesMonitor.doc: Passes the query to the base class.

Input.doc: Keys 760 and 761 switch the filter tabs (previous and next, wrapping); keys 762 and 763 page up and down the list when the menu is in state 2. Other keys go to the default select input.

comments.text: type filter chosen: the default name is 35:4266 when nothing is picked

the kind code that goes into the result (Arr2Int): 9 for kinds 13/17/19, 10 for 16, 11 for 18, 12 for 23, 13 for 24, 14 for 29, 18 for 31-33, 25 for 65, 19 for 34, 20 for 44, 24 for 62, 4 for 63-64, 5 for 71; 131075 for constants (53), 65559 for wings (61), 65542 for fleet leaders (70)
a value was selected: stop the menu so the caller reads m3

MenuAction.doc: On Enter: for filter tabs stores the chosen type or race filter in m86 or m87 and refreshes the list; otherwise stores the chosen entry as a typed argument (kind code via Arr2Int) and stops the menu when the value is set.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Resets the rotation counter m11 when the selected line changes, then calls the base handler.

comments.text: m24 nonzero = a sub-view is active (probably); then the preview is cleared.

ResetRotateInst.doc: Clears the 3D preview type (m91) when the picker is not in its list view.

SelectTab.doc: Switches the filter tab through the base SelectTab; on change resets the rotation state and the scroll counter m11. Returns 1 when the tab changed.

SpecialMenu.doc: Calls the base SpecialMenu.

comments.text: kinds 13 (wares), 17 (factories) and 19 (ware list without volume) get filter tabs: 1 = object type, 2 = race
tab 1, type filter: entries encode (objType << 16) | subType; subType 65535 = any subtype
ware groups: 589823 = type 8 (texts 58:11 Laser), 655359 = type 9 (58:13 Shield) and so on; 65535 subtype = any ware of that group
factory filters: 393216 and up = type 6 (factories), subtype = factory kind; names via GetExtendedFactoryWareName
tab 2, race filter: entries are race ids 1-19 from g7, value 0 = Other
race mask 918526: races in the mask are left out of the list when Other is chosen (probably the major races)
the two column headers for the ware list are drawn at the left and right column positions v6 and v7
race filter and subtype filter: values from the tab (v2 type, v3 race) are compared with SA_GetTypeDefaultRace and SA_GetTypeGSubType
row value: bits 16..23 are the object type (6 = factory), bits 0..15 the subtype
wares show volume (WareTypeVolume) and the TK text 1999:<tk>, not for kind 19
end of the kind switch: kinds 31-33, 53, 61, 62, 65 and 70 are sorted by name before listing; the others are listed in table order
kinds 31 and 32 filter the command list by the 1000-1099 id range (probably the ship and station command groups)
kinds 63 and 64: two fixed choices, text 1265:300 with value 1 and text 1265:301 with value 0
parameter definitions with flag 1048576 are listed; parameter 53 is skipped; entries sorted by name

SpecialUpdate.doc: Fills the list menu for the requested kind (m83): wares, factories and mines with type and race filter tabs (kinds 13, 17, 19), then simple lists for the other kinds (races, object classes, commands, signals, wings, fleet leaders, global parameters, constants, parameter definitions). Wares show a volume and a TK column; fleet leaders show their sector.

2275.name: ScriptValuePicker

2278.doc: Command console (text 2020:0 'Command Console'): shows the commands and settings of the selected object, or of a group (fleet, own ships docked in the sector, all owned ships), and the global settings when no object is selected. Also a picker (picker mode, CreateNextSelCmd) that returns a chosen command slot. Probably the menu behind the player's command console keys.

0.doc: row code being edited (negative row id, 0 = none)
0.name: editRow

1.doc: value chosen for the row in editRow (e.g. missile fire probability)
1.name: editValue

10.doc: 1 when the console only picks a command slot
10.name: pickerMode

11.doc: object set: 0 this object, 1 own ships docked here, 2 all owned ships, 3 fleet ships
11.name: scope

2.doc: unique command console entries of the command objects
2.name: entries

3.doc: number of entries in entries
3.name: entryCount

4.doc: command slot or turret index of the selected row; used by command callbacks
4.name: cmdSlot

5.doc: cmdSlot passed to CreateNextSelCmd
5.name: initialCmdSlot

6.doc: filter for GetCmdConsoleCommands (-100 = all); the target object in picker mode
6.name: commandFilter

7.doc: command list filled by GetCmdConsoleCommands
7.name: commands

8.doc: number of commands in commands
8.name: commandCount

9.doc: nonzero while a picked command waits for its callback
9.name: callbackPending

AnyFleetLeader.doc: True when at least one object is a fleet leader.

AnyNonFleetLeader.doc: True when at least one object is not a fleet leader.

AnyShips.doc: True when at least one object is a moveable ship (2134) that is not 2061.

no messages: return 0

entry layout: [0] title, [1] author, [2] age, [3] columns, [4] column spacing, [5] column width, [6] text x, [7] text lines, [8] style flags, [9] action object, [10] ondisplay value, [11] ranking (fight high 16 bits, trade low 16 bits)
escape & < > in the markup, then map square brackets to angle brackets and newlines to br
the markup is parsed as XML; a parse failure gives an empty placeholder entry
style table: bit 16 line end, 32 left, 64 right, 128 centre, 256 justify, 4 selectable line, 1 and 2 and 8 change the flags
walk the parsed XML tree: text nodes add characters, element nodes change style or layout
escape code 27 (colour change) passes through unchanged
tags title and author store their text; text starts a new column block

colour tags: b or yellow Y, red R, green G, blue B, cyan C, magenta M, grey A, white W
push the current element on the stack and descend into children
escape [E] becomes the colour escape 27
column width: (587 minus the spacing) divided by columns, at least 120; 587 is the text width
text x: right-aligned 64, centred 128, justified 256, else left
title limited to 620 pixels
text wrapped to the column width

start on the Xbox tab when the pad is enabled in the engine

CreateNext.doc: Base sub-menu creation. Clears the target object (m33) and sets the footer text (m111) before calling the base class.

CreateNextCustom.doc: Opens the custom menu as a sub-menu of arg1 with title arg2, footer text arg3, item list arg4 and result buffer arg5.

CreateNextCustomInfo.doc: Opens the custom menu in info layout as a sub-menu of arg1. Same as CreateNextCustom; arg6 is the info row count (stored as m108 = arg6 + 2).

CreatePrevious.doc: Return handler: calls the base CreatePrevious with no arguments.

comments.text: The current row must be a -4 switch with a value list of at least one entry.

CustomMenuSwitchValues.doc: Cycles the value of the current -4 switch row by arg1 (+1 or -1) through its value list; the value wraps around. Returns 1 when a switch row was changed, 0 otherwise.

DisplayCustomMenuHeading.doc: Draws a heading row made of columns (see SplitTextArray) in the head line.

GetMenuHeight.doc: Returns the menu height: the height of the trade menu base, capped by the row limit m115 when it is set.

GetName.doc: Returns the menu title m106.

GetObjectBody.doc: Returns -1: the custom menu has no 3D body.

GetRaceBody.doc: Returns the race body of the player faction g8.

GetTextIndent.doc: Returns the x offset of a row at nesting level arg1 (14 pixels per level).

HidesMonitor.doc: Returns 1: the custom menu hides the monitor.

comments.text: The trade menu base handles the key first; this override runs only when it did not.
Keys 757 and 756: set the trade bar value to the max (m113) or min (m114) and redraw.
Trade bar at the minimum: fail beep.

Input.doc: Key input: 757/756 jump the trade bar to its max or min; 760/761 change the trade bar or switch values by one step; 762/763 page the info panel or the selection; other keys go to the trade menu base.

comments.text: Checkbox row (-8): flips its value.
Action rows (-1 or -2 with a 5 text value): the named script runs with the row's arguments.
The named script runs with the row's arguments; a value it stores is returned through the result buffer.
Code -1: the script is asynchronous; the menu waits for CallbackEndRunScript (m119) before redrawing.
Codes -3 and -4 (for rows that are not switches): check all or uncheck all checkboxes of the menu.
The result buffer m105 receives the chosen value and its type (4 for values from switches).
Each switch row adds (21, {value}) to the result buffer.
A nonzero result closes the menu through Stop().

MenuAction.doc: Runs the selected row: toggles checkboxes (-8), cycles switches (-4), runs a named script (-1), checks or unchecks all checkboxes (-3, -4), or stores the chosen value and type in the result buffer and closes the menu.

OnChangeSelectLine.doc: Resets the selected row state (m11) when the selected line changes, then calls the base handler.

SetDefaultOptions.doc: Resets the layout options to defaults before the item list is scanned: 10 visible rows, page keys follow the previous info state, no row limit, no hover line.

comments.text: Info layout uses texture 896.

SetupTexture.doc: Base texture setup; in info layout the texture id 896 is used.

ShouldUseHoverLine.doc: Returns m118: whether the hover line highlight is used.

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets up the window. In info layout it shows the large title and a hidden texture; otherwise the base menu.

comments.text: A title heading is drawn only when the first row is not a fixed heading (type 21 with code -1).
Row type 4, code -10 is a layout option: not drawn.
Code -8 rows are checkboxes; the value is 1 or 0. The checkbox state is kept in v8 and drawn with a tick icon.
Code -9 ends a checkbox group: a section break is drawn when the group was checked.
Code -3 starts a new section.
Code -1 rows: the heading value is stored and drawn above the next row.
Codes -2, -6 and -7 are info rows, not drawn in the selectable part.
Code -11 is a full-width text row, drawn in columns when the value is a 21 array.
Code -4 is a value switch row: its current value is picked from the value list m110 (cycled by keys 760/761).
m110 set: a switch row is present, so keys 760/761 cycle values.
Code -5 is the trade bar row: min, max and current value are items 5, 7 and 9.
The info panel is only drawn when m107 is set.

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the custom menu: the title header, the selectable rows (checkboxes, switches, text, trade bar, value rows), then the info panel when m107 is set, the footer text and the trade bar when it is active.

SplitTextArray.doc: Splits a flat (type, value, x, value) array into text and column x positions; the x values are relative to the menu width (negative = right-aligned). Returns the number of text pieces.

comments.text: Items are read as pairs: a type 21 entry followed by an array row (4, code, ...). Rows of type 4 are the custom rows described below.
Layout option rows (4, -10, option, value): 1 = visible row count (m120), 2 = page keys scroll the info panel (m117), 3 = hover line (m118), 4 = fixed row height (m115).
Info rows counted for the layout: -2 text with type 21, -7 separator, -6 text with type 21 or 5 (counted with the row count of the text).
A -2 row with a plain text value: its wrapped line count is added to the info rows.
Side effect: m62 (text right edge) is recomputed here for the text wrapping of the rows.
A trade bar takes 5 rows of the panel.

UpdateCustomMenu.doc: Scans the item list for layout options (type 4, code -10) and counts info rows, then computes the visible row area (m13, m17, m18) and the scroll limits. Also sets the layout flags (m107, m109, m110, m115, m117, m118, m120). Sets m62 as a side effect.

UpdateTradeBarValue.doc: Writes the current trade bar value into the trade row (item 9) of the current row.

WriteColumnsText.doc: Draws a text row split into columns: the (text, column) pairs come from SplitTextArray and are drawn right to left.

2329.doc: Fleet menu for a fleet leader: lists the leader, the other ships of its fleet grouped by type, and the free ships of the same sector. Lets the player set a new leader, remove ships from the fleet or disband it. Also used as a ship picker (CreateNextSelectMenu) that returns the chosen ship in m3. Page 2006 names the classes; the menu title is texts 35:4758 'Fleet Ships'.

AddShipLine.doc: Draws one ship line with its icon and a status label: 'Leader' for the leader, 'With Fleet' for other fleet members.

Create.doc: Opens the fleet menu for a fleet leader; arg2 is the setup argument passed to Setup.

CreateNext.doc: Opens the fleet menu as the next menu in a chain. arg4 is the leader.

CreateNextSelectMenu.doc: Opens the fleet menu as a ship picker. arg5 is the title text; the chosen ship is returned to the caller through m3.

Destruct.doc: Forwards to the base destructor.

GetContext.doc: Returns the UI context id 1003 (fleet menu).

Input.doc: Key handler: delegates everything to the default select input.

comments.text: picker mode: returns 65542 (0x10006) with the chosen ship in m3
leader line: opens the fleet commands menu (2278) for the leader
free ship: becomes a member of this fleet at once

MenuAction.doc: Activates the selected ship. In picker mode, returns it. On the leader line, opens the fleet commands menu. On a free ship, joins it to the fleet; on a fleet member, opens the context menu with 'Remove from Fleet' and 'Set as Leader'.

comments.text: -1 close, -2 disband, -3 set leader, -4 remove from fleet, other ids passed to the ship object

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Handles the fleet context menu: -2 disbands the fleet, -3 makes the selected ship the leader, -4 removes it from the fleet; other choices go to the ship.

OnContextMenuUpdate.doc: Forwards the update request to the selected ship.

OnContextMenuUpdateInfo.doc: Forwards the info update request to the selected ship.

Setup.doc: Stores the leader and rebuilds the ship groups.

SortShips.doc: Sorts one ship group by display name. Empty or missing groups are skipped.

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the menu title (picker title, or texts 35:4758 'Fleet Ships') and the two labels, then runs the base SpecialMenu.

comments.text: remember the selected row before the list is rebuilt
a row that is selected in the list makes the leader line the active one
sector ships are shown only in the normal (not picker) menu
info text: 'View %d ship in fleet' or 'View %d ships in fleet' (35:4751, 35:4750)

SpecialUpdate.doc: Draws the header, the leader, each non-empty ship group and, for the normal menu, the free ships of the sector. The info line shows the number of fleet ships.

comments.text: nothing is grouped when the leader object no longer exists
fleet members are grouped by class; the leader itself is skipped
2142 and 2027 missile boats go to the same group as the missile ships
free ships of the leader's sector: stationary ships (2135), 2061 and fleet members are skipped

UpdateShips.doc: Rebuilds all ship groups: the leader's fleet split by class and the free ships of the leader's sector. Sorts each group by name.

2330.doc: Menu of script-provided graph actions for the current object (m33). Scripts register entries with the static AddGraph and remove them with RemoveGraph. Selecting an entry runs its MSCI script with the group key as parameters. Parent C2202. Probably the game's object graph menu.

0.doc: registered groups: [header page, header id, entries]; entry [target, script, text page, text id, column]
0.name: graphGroups

entry exists: update its text, column and group parameters
new entry appended to an existing group
new group with its first entry

AddGraph.doc: Registers a graph action for target (an object or class id) and script name, with its text (textPage, textId), in group (groupPage, groupId) at column 0-7. Replaces an entry with the same target and script, otherwise appends it.

GetGraphs.doc: Returns the whole group list, or nothing when no graph is registered.

GraphsExistFor.doc: True when at least one registered graph applies to the target. Other menus call it to decide whether to offer the graph menu (probably).

Input.doc: Default select input handling.

comments.text: entry[0] is an object or a class id; entry[1] is the script name

IsGraphFor.doc: True when graph entry arg1 applies to target arg2 (same object, or the target is of that class) and its script exists.

the player's own graphs run without a context object
context type code from the target class (probably the script object type codes)

comments.text: group is dropped with its last entry

RemoveGraph.doc: Removes the entry for target and script from group (groupPage, groupId). Drops the group when its last entry is removed.

SpecialMenu.doc: Sets the menu title (text 35:9000, not in texts_L044.tsv) and menu id 127, then runs the parent setup.

a new section starts before the first entry of each column

group header text printed once, before the first entry of the group
end of the selectable list

SpecialUpdate.doc: Lists the graphs that apply to the current object: groups with a header first, then the groups without one. Each row is selectable with the selection id group << 16 | entry.

300.doc: Galaxy-wide manager, probably the singleton C300 called statically. It indexes which stations sell (product) or buy (resource) each ware, searches stations, shipyards and gates for a trade or route, creates random planets and suns, and holds the temporary sector. It works on the 24 x 20 sector grid g6. No page 2006 or dobj name is known.

comments.text: creates the live object from the record. commands collects its start command
the new object is added to the sector stored in the record (index 4)

ActivateWarObject.doc: Creates the live object of a war record and adds it to its sector. Start commands are collected into commands for GalaxyStartCommands. Returns the live object, or nothing when it cannot be built.

comments.text: states are 0..63; a state that is already active or out of range is ignored
saves the live objects first, so that the reactivated objects load their saved data
every object of every sector record that has this state and no live object is activated
starts the commands collected from the activated objects

ActivateWarState.doc: Turns a war state on: activates every war object that has this state and no live object yet, then starts their collected commands. Returns 1 when the state was switched on.

comments.text: type 5 is a dock: only tradeables; other types take products, resources and s-resources
ware key: type in bits 16..23, ware id in the low 16 bits

AddDefaultWaresToStation.doc: Adds the default wares of the station's type code to a new station: docks get tradeables, other stations get products, resources and s-resources.

AddDocksWithWareToTable.doc: Adds to the table every dock in the galaxy that trades the ware (not owned by owner g8, optional class filter). Returns the table.

comments.text: factory id is taken from the next free id of its subtype when not overridden
main-group factories become shipyard of their race sector
dock subtypes 12 and 21 are temples (sector main station, temple stored)

AddObjectToSector.doc: Adds a freshly built object to a sector and finishes its setup by type: shipyards and main sectors for factories, the temple for a special dock, owner for stations, and formation members for ships. A station that must be rebuilt is queued to the rebuild list and destroyed instead.

AddProductStation.doc: Registers a station as a seller of the given ware keys, with the supplier object as value.

AddResourceStation.doc: Registers a station as a buyer of the given ware keys, with the supplier object as value.

comments.text: sector record: [0] = 1 (sector type), [1] x, [2] y, [4] war object id. Object records follow from index 13

AddWarSector.doc: Adds a sector to the war map with a new war object id. The sector record lists its objects after index 12.

comments.text: linear search for an unused id; ids are looked up in the war id table m14
m17 only moves upward: ids released below it are not reused until the war map is discarded

AllocateWarObjectID.doc: Returns a free war object id, searched upward from the hint m17. Returns nothing when no war map is active.

comments.text: custom game (mode -2) marks the game as modified
sector grid: 24 columns by 20 rows
factions 1..19 are created here; faction 10 is the player (g8)
each NPC faction gets its special notoriety setup
owner.SetNotoriety(other, value): notoriety of the owner toward the other faction; plus or minus 1000000 marks full friend or enemy
op count limit raised to 200000000 during the map build

Build.doc: Builds the whole galaxy: loads the default ware template and war states, creates the 24 x 20 sector grid, the factions and the notoriety matrix, the core systems, then the map objects. Mode -2 is a custom game (marks the game modified).

comments.text: mode -100: the galaxy is already built, only the sector loop is skipped
mode 11 and above: map file xmissionNN
mode -2: map name comes from the script parameter
no map name: the default map x3_universe, or the map of the game start
sector flags: 4 = core sector
sector group mask 393216 disables sector events
command maps are released after the galaxy start commands run

BuildFromEditor.doc: Builds the galaxy from the map chosen in the editor or the game start, validates gates and shipyards, and calls the galaxy setup. Argument -100 means no map (the galaxy is already built); 11 and up is a numbered mission map (xmissionNN); -2 reads the map name from the script parameter; any other value selects a game start.

BuildObject.doc: Builds one object from a galaxy record with no command or id map.

BuildObjectWithCmd.doc: Builds one object from a galaxy record and returns it, or 0 for unknown kinds. Kind numbers match object types: 3 sun (2008), 21 nebula (2043), 4 planet (2002), 17 asteroid (2012), 18 gate (2014), 28 debris (1650), 8..16 wares and goodies (2084), 20 custom galaxy object (1001), 6 factory, 5 dock, 7 ship. Nested records (factory and dock contents, ship lasers, shields and formation members) are filled in. A ship's command block is stored in commandMap, and named objects are stored in idMap.

sector references by id are stored in idMap
sector flags: 4 = core sector
sector group mask 393216 (bits 17,18): no sector events for these groups
record kind 2 sets the sector background (type, nebula index, star index)
objects that are not new sectors get SafePosOnActivate for kinds 5, 6, 17, 28
transform applied only when a sector and transform are given

BuildObjects.doc: Builds the objects of a galaxy map file (addon/maps/<mapFile>): each sector record creates its owner, size, music and mission quotas, then its object records. When onlySector is given, only that sector is built and its positions get transformed by the given matrix.

the object was alone in its group: the group is released
the target group is created when it does not exist yet

ChangeWarObjectID.doc: Moves a war record to another war object id group. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the target group is a sector group, nothing when the record is not found.

CheckWarState.doc: True when war state bit warState is set in the mask. Bit 0 is stored in the second word, as the two-word layout in SetWarState requires.

ClearWarMap.doc: Clears the war map table (sector object to war data).

ware copy skips types 8 and 9 (goodies and internal wares)
a custom galaxy object (kind 2073) also gets copies of the ships it holds

CopyObject.doc: Creates a copy of an existing object (used to save and restore sector contents). Returns the new object for supported type codes; returns 0 for type 18 (gates) and unknown types.

CreateRandomPlanet.doc: Creates a random planet (class 2002) in a sector: with a 1 in 4 chance only one coordinate is random and the other two are 0, otherwise all three are random. Its subtype and colour are random; then it is added to the sector.

CreateRandomSun.doc: Creates a random sun (class 2008) with a random colour and adds it to the sector. Positions follow the same pattern as CreateRandomPlanet with a smaller range.

comments.text: cell 23,19 of the grid is reserved for the temporary sector

CreateTemporarySector.doc: Creates the temporary sector in grid cell 23,19 (or reuses the existing one) and sets its owner to the faction in g7[14].

comments.text: SelfDestruct reason 21 (probably: removed by a war state change)

DeactivateWarObject.doc: Removes the live object of a war record. The object is destroyed later, in a fork.

Destroy.doc: Destructs all sectors of the grid, the managed object m13 and the faction objects, and clears the tables. Sets global g21 to a sentinel value (-2147483648), purpose not known.
