template keys (type << 16 | subtype) from the default ware table m7, sorted
only docks (5) and factories (6) get templates

factories also get their resources (section 6) and products (section 7)
tradeables (section 8) are written for every template

mode bit 2: skip sectors without any flagged object (editor flag 1)
lists of every object kind in the sector, checked for flagged objects in mode bit 2

sector header, t=1. Type codes used below: 2 background, 3 sun, 4 planet, 5 dock, 6 factory, 7 ship, 8-16 wares, 17 asteroid, 18 gate, 20 custom object, 21 nebula, 23 section group, 28 asteroid field. Mode bit 1 adds id = -handle
gates are sorted by id before they are written

saves the live objects first, so that their current state is written
file name uses the universe name (gUniverseName)
sectors are read as gSectorGrid[x][y]; only sectors with an owner and a war record are written
five passes: 0 wares (types 8-16), 1 custom objects (type 20), 2 factories, 3 docks, 4 ships
wares are written only in pass 0

dock or factory line with the war state mask ws and optional name n

FindAllMarinesInTraining.doc: Adds to the table every marine in training at a dock in the galaxy and returns it.

FindAllMarinesWaitingPickup.doc: Adds to the table every marine waiting for pickup at a dock in the galaxy and returns it.

FindAllShipyards.doc: Returns the shipyards (class 2037) of the galaxy that can sell the ware (any ware if the filter is -1). Shipyards of owner g8 are skipped.

FindNearestGate.doc: Searches outward from the origin sector one route ring at a time and returns the first gate found, or 0 when no sector in the ring has one.

FindNearestGateForSector.doc: Finds the gate of a sector that leads toward the destination sector along the route. Falls back to any gate of the sector when no route exists.

comments.text: ships for class 2004, docks for 2007, factories otherwise

FindNearestObject.doc: Walks the sector grid outward from the given object and returns the nearest object of a class (ships, docks or factories by class id) within maxRange route sectors. Objects marked NoFind are skipped; an optional owner id restricts the result.

maxRouteLen 0 = search only the origin sector

ware category match for stations (type<<16 | category), flag 0x80000000

flag 0x80000000 on ships: only race-covered ships

FindObject.doc: Searches the galaxy for objects matching a filter set and returns the best match, or an array of matches when flag 0x40000000 is set. Candidates come from sectors within the route-length window around the origin; filters cover type, subtype, class, owner, race, relation to the requester, war state, docking, scan state and yield. Returns 0 when nothing matches.

3001.doc: Singleton (class object 3001) that runs the BBS quest offers and the story quests of the player. Quest objects are the classes 4001 to 4999, one per quest id; each quest is a 3101 instance once offered. Keeps the plot flag table and the tutorial id. Set is probably called once at game start (not verified).

0.name: firstQuestId

1.name: lastQuestId

2.name: questionSectorId

3.name: bbsOffers

5.name: bbsQuests

6.name: nextBbsUpdateAge

BBSQuestAborted.doc: Aborts an accepted BBS quest: sets state 2, removes its message, drops it from the accepted table and destroys it after 100 time units.

BBSQuestFinished.doc: Finishes an accepted BBS quest: sets state 5, removes its message, drops it from the accepted table and destroys it after 100 time units.

CallInfiniteLoop.doc: Forwards the argument to the global CallInfiniteLoop (debug helper).

CatchWare.doc: Offers a dropped ware to the accepted quests. Returns 1 when one of them catches it.

CheckBBSQuests.doc: Checks every accepted BBS quest. A quest whose Check result is neither 2 nor 5 (rejected or finished) is set to state 6 (updated).

DestroyBBSQuest.doc: Destroys a BBS quest object: resets the story state to 1 when it was 8, removes its incoming message, then deletes it.

EjectWare.doc: Asks the accepted quests to eject a ware. Returns the first non-zero result, or 0.

FindBBSQuests.doc: Rolls for each quest that is an incoming message and not yet used. A quest that passes its roll is created and either accepted at once (offer result 4) or stored as a BBS offer. Does nothing when the player is dead.

GetAnswers.doc: Passes the answer list through all accepted BBS quests. Each quest may change the running result (arg3); stops at the first negative value.

GetBBSOffers.doc: Returns the table of BBS offers currently shown.

GetBBSQuests.doc: Returns the table of accepted BBS quests.

GetEnvironmentTrack.doc: Returns the environment music track from the first accepted quest that has one, or 0.

GetNumQuests.doc: Returns the highest quest id in use (m1).

GetQuestion.doc: Asks the accepted BBS quests for a dialog question and returns the first non-zero answer, or 0.

GetQuestionArray.doc: Returns the first non-zero question array of the accepted BBS quests, or 0.

GetQuestionSectorDialogID.doc: Returns the dialog id of the question sector.

GetQuestionSectorX.doc: X coordinate of the question sector (from the sector dialog id in m2).

GetQuestionSectorY.doc: Y coordinate of the question sector (from the sector dialog id in m2).

skip quests that are not 3101 messages, are already incoming, or are in story state 4 or 5

GetTutorialID.doc: Returns the tutorial id given to Set.

IncomingQuestion.doc: Creates a quest of class arg1 as an incoming message, offers it, puts it in state 4 and accepts it at once. Returns the new quest, or 0 when Create fails or the player is dead.

IsPlotFailed.doc: True when the failed bit (bit 2 of the plot's first word) is set.

NumOffersInStation.doc: Counts the open BBS offers (state 8) of quest arg1 at station arg2.

PlayerLeftShip.doc: Tells every accepted BBS quest that the player left the ship arg1.

ReceiveDialogParameter.doc: Gives a dialog parameter to the accepted BBS quests. Returns the first non-negative result, or -1.

SetQuestionSector.doc: Sets the question sector from sector coordinates.

SetQuestionSectorDialogID.doc: Sets the question sector from a dialog id.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame update: calls Vbi on every accepted BBS quest. Does nothing when the player is dead.

301.doc: Manager of AL plugins: named scripts matching al.plugin.* and !al.plugin.* (dobj: AL_PLUGINS). Each plugin has a description, a timer interval and a next-run age, and gets init, start, stop, timer, reinit and isenabled actions. Init runs once at game start; Run() ticks every second. Used by the MenuPlugins options menu (class 2292).

InitPlugins.doc: Runs the init action of every registered plugin.

LoadPlugins.doc: Runs the loader scripts that register plugins matching al.plugin.* and !al.plugin.*.

RegisterPlugin.doc: Adds a plugin script with no description and no timer. Existing entries are kept.

SetPluginDesc.doc: Sets the display text of a registered plugin.

SetPluginInterval.doc: Sets the timer period of a registered plugin in seconds. 0 disables timer calls.

Runs the control tasks: sector stats refresh at start-up, ship control per sector, job ship rebuilds, factory alerts that order rebuilds, random events, and a slow god-control state. Holds the event notoriety matrix between races. Methods of the rest of the class are in other batches.

Least common multiple of the product and input relative values sets the value base.
Type 15 product: value 25 per unit of efficiency plus one.
Type 11 (energy): output depends on the energy factors of the sector's suns (arg5 is replaced by 8 times their sum).
Values under 60 are raised to 60 by repeating the cycle.
Secondary costs: wares 8, 9, 10 and 16 use weight 6, others weight 12.
Secondary cost is zero when the ware is flagged in the g46 table; otherwise it follows the weight and relative value.

CalcProductValue.doc: Returns a table keyed by ware (product and resource keys) of the net value per hour for a station of a given factory type: product income minus input costs and secondary costs. Used to rank stations for rebuilding. Parameters: factory type id, products, resources, secondary resources, efficiency, sector, and an unknown flag.

comments.text: With a target sector, factories more than 9 jumps away are skipped
Class 2006 is Factory (page 2006); suppliers must be factories of the same subtype

Fill level of the factory and suppliers in per mille (1000 = full)
Alert age renewed: next check after twice the statistics cycle

CheckEvents.doc: Polls every active god event. Check result 3 aborts the event, 4 finishes it.

comments.text: Ships owned by g8 are left alone.
Unrebuildable job with no leader: self-destruct, or command 34 when inside a sector (class 2001).
Otherwise the job is (re)started.

ControlJobShipTask.doc: Starts once a background task that checks job ships of other races. Ships whose job cannot be rebuilt and that have no job leader are destroyed, or sent off with command 34 when they sit in a sector.

comments.text: Only owners whose mask has neither bit 64 nor bit 128 (probably not player-controlled) get ware pickups
Each flying ware is considered with a 1 in 4 chance per pass
Command 24 (probably ware transport): a ship already ordered to take this ware is not given another
Transporter must be class 2034, not owned by a race in mask 15360 (races 10 to 13, probably excluded), and free for default jobs
100 ms pause before the ship pass

Ships with command 12 or 33, or under attack, are not sent for repair

Without a shipyard, the pirates (g7[8]) use their own docks

No repair place: ships without an object id regenerate 10 percent of max hull per pass

ControlShipsOfSector.doc: Controls the ships of one sector: flying wares are assigned to free transport ships (command 24, probably ware transport); ships without a command start their job, or are sent to a shipyard or dock for repair when hull is low; ships without a repair place regenerate 10 percent hull per pass.

CreateEvent.doc: Creates one god event for a slot index, a sector and an event kind mask, and accepts it. Class slots need a positive priority and a free count. Script slots ask their script for a priority first. Returns the new event object, or 0.

EventAborted.doc: Marks a running event as aborted (state 3), removes its message, calls Abort and destroys it after 100 units.

EventDestruct.doc: Destructs a god event, removes it from the active list, decrements the active count of its slot and deletes it.

EventFinished.doc: Marks a running event as finished (state 4), removes its message, calls Finish and destroys it after 100 units.

GetAlertFactories.doc: Returns the factory -> alert age table of an alert key.

GetEventNotoriety.doc: Event notoriety from race a towards race b (matrix m10).

GetJobShipRebuildCount.doc: Returns how many rebuild entries are queued for a job id. A per-job count table is rebuilt from the queue when it is empty or when called without caching allowed.

comments.text: Step interval: 3000 s plus up to 3000 s random
m23 below the target: bit 1 and bit 2 are switched on at random chances from SE_LinFunc
m23 above the target: bit 1 and bit 2 are switched off at random chances
After 220 steps without a change both state bits are inverted

GodControlTask.doc: Background loop, one step every 50 to 100 minutes. It moves the two state bits of m24 at random, with chances based on how far m23 is from m22, and inverts both bits after 220 steps without a change.

comments.text: m10 is a 20 x 20 matrix indexed by race ids 0 to 19

Init.doc: Creates the state tables and the 20 x 20 event notoriety matrix, then starts the background tasks.

comments.text: Base period 22500 units, randomised by plus or minus half.
Fewer than 15 wrecks: the oldest wreck is removed.
Wreck age: a wreck older than about 108000 units (a third in core sectors) plus 3600 is removed.
Skipped: no owner, owner has mask 192, cooldown running (m3), or sector flag 2.
List of nearby trade partners for this sector.
Owner race mask 1216 is skipped.
A ware needs at least 6 valid samples; fewer ends the scan of this station.
Average fill below 30 percent of max store: supply shortage (flag 8), else flag 2. Below 7 percent: urgent (flag 16).
Product fill above 70 percent of max store: surplus (flag 1), else flag 4. Above 93 percent: urgent (flag 16).
Pause before the events are evaluated.
Urgent entries (flag 16) fire event 0x40000100 on the sector for the flagged stations, unless the m24 bit 2 filter is set; cooldown 36000.
Wares sorted by their imbalance; imbalances under 65536 are dropped.
Owner race; race 8 is replaced by a random race.
Event kind mask v12 is picked from the sign of the buy and sell balances and the trade flows; the constants are bit masks.
Sector flag 1 clears bit 128 of the event kind mask.
The first candidate sets a random threshold; later candidates must beat it.
Half or more of the trading stations involved: bit 256 is set.
Bit 2^30 is always set for this event (0x40000000).
Cooldown of 36000 units for this sector.

InspectSectorTask.doc: Background economy task of GODENGINE (dobj name). Every 22500 units, about, it picks a random sector: it first trims old wrecks, then samples the factories and products of an owned sector, finds trade partners nearby and fires economy events (shortage or surplus) through SelectEvent, with a 36000-unit cooldown per sector. The core of the sector and station analysis.

IsFactoryAlerted.doc: True if the factory is in the alert table of the alert key.

comments.text: GetState is not a method of class 6100 in this batch: probably a native call.

MsgButtonCallback.doc: Forwards a dialog button choice to a god event of class 6100. Returns the event's state directly for states 0, 3 and 4, else the result of its Select.

comments.text: Due time = now + 360000 times the station's rebuild counter (entry field 17).
Queued rebuilds start only while there are TL ships (m2) and the active count is under the target.

RebuildControlTask.doc: Starts once a background task that, about every 300000 units, moves active stations back into the rebuild table with a due time, then starts queued station rebuilds while the active count is below a target. The target is interpolated from the start factory count (m22) and the TL ship count, probably.

comments.text: Entry not due yet (entry[0] is the due time).
Job cannot be rebuilt and no leader ship is alive: entry dropped.
Job changes sector on rebuild: local counts at the old sector are decremented first.
Local job: the new sector's local counts are incremented.
Civilian job group (3): ship is set civilian and not shown as enemy.
Local ship is removed from the civilian removal queue.
No ship could be created: retry after a random delay up to 200 units.

RebuildJobShipTask.doc: Starts once a background task that works through the job-ship rebuild queue: creates replacement ships, starts their jobs and removes finished or invalid entries. Failed entries are retried after a random delay.

RebuildLocalShips.doc: Creates the local job ships that a sector is missing (its local job counts minus the desired counts), sets their speed limit and civilian flags, and adds them to the job table. Parameter is the sector.

comments.text: Period about 1200000 units, randomised by plus or minus 120000.
Products of active stations are marked as produced.
Loop over the 24x20 sector grid.
Trade stats of each sector add to the ware balances.
Factories per sector: built plus queued, minus player-owned and start factories.
Totals: start factories (m22) and built factories (m23).
Target: 110 percent of start factories.
No factories left in a sector: a rebuild starts with 1 in 20 chance.
Any negative ware balance in the entry's inputs stops the candidate.
Product not produced anywhere and 1 in 4 chance: rebuild starts.
Enough factories already, or 1 in 10 chance: candidate dropped.
Surplus (balance above 100000 with jitter) or unused ware: candidate skipped.
Total factories at or above the target: no new rebuilds.
Lean mode when existing factories are below two thirds of the target.
Trade-partner search from the factory's sector within 8 sectors; score comes from partner trade flows.
Score adds half the partners' trade flow.
Sector with fewer than 20 factories: score scaled down.
Queue size limit: 80 percent (lean mode) or one third of the m2 table size (class 2032 ships); the list is capped at 5 times that.
Ware whose balance is within 100000 (scaled in lean mode) is reserved: its inputs are added to the balance.
Factory count of the sector is incremented for the queued station.

RebuildLogicTask.doc: Background task that decides which stations and factories to rebuild. Every ~1200000 units it totals the trade balances and factory counts over the 24x20 sector grid, scores the stations in the rebuild table and queues the best ones, capped by the number of TL ships and by the factory target (110 percent of start factories).

RegisterScript.doc: Registers a script-driven god event under its script name. Runs the script's init (or reinit) command, reads its maximum event count from 'maxnr', and stores the slot in the event table.

Reinit.doc: Re-reads the god-engine setup. Runs the god.setup scripts, initialises the event classes 6102 to 6108 that exist, drops script events whose script is gone, reads the 'god engine skip fixed' value from god.conf into m18 and sets the event priorities.

RemoveAlertFactory.doc: Removes a factory from the alert table of an alert key.

comments.text: Sector has a live object or update focus: postpone removal by another 300 units.
Ship leaves its home sector's job count before self-destruct.

RemoveLocalShipTask.doc: Starts once a background task that destroys queued civilian ships when their timeout passes, postponing while their sector is occupied or under update focus.

comments.text: Only civilian ships of class 2004 without an object id are queued.

RemoveRequest.doc: Schedules a civilian ship that has no live object id for removal 300 time units from now (checked by RemoveLocalShipTask).

comments.text: Quota already reached for a rebuildable job: nothing is queued.
Due time = now + half the job's spawn time + random jitter.

RequestRebuild.doc: Queues a replacement for a lost job ship, unless the job can be rebuilt and its quota is already filled. Returns 1 when queued, nothing otherwise. The queue entry is {due time, job id, owner race, job leader, home sector}.

comments.text: Non-local job: the home sector loses one desired job ship.
Ship was not flagged for rebuild: no queue entry.
Unrebuildable job without a leader: nothing is queued.

RequestRebuildByShip.doc: Called when a job ship is lost: removes it from its job, updates the home sector's desired count and queues a rebuild if the job allows it. Returns 1 for a job ship, 0 otherwise.

comments.text: One specific ware (type 11, id 1048577) is scaled by 603729/65536.

ResourcePerCycle.doc: Estimates how many units of a resource a station consumes per production cycle, from the relative values of the product and the input. Returns 0 when the ware has no product.

comments.text: Record not in the queue: look for it in the active list and destroy that live station.
Record not in the active list either: look in the rebuild table of class 303.
Nearest wreck to the old position is self-destructed (code 17).
Shields are added by default.

RespawnStation.doc: Rebuilds a station from its record: finds the record in the rebuild queue, the active list or the rebuild table, removes the nearest wreck, then recreates the factory with its products, resources, efficiency and rotation. Returns the new station, or 0 when no record is found.

RestartJobShip.doc: Restarts the job of every ship that is not hired and not owned by g8, for one job id.

RestartTask.doc: Stops all background tasks and starts them again.

comments.text: Check period 600 s plus up to 10 s random
10 s pause between alert keys

RunCheckAlertsTask.doc: Starts the alert check loop once. Every 600 to 610 s it runs CheckAlertedWare for each alert key and queues rebuild orders for the wares found short (AddRebuildOrder).

RunRandomEventTask.doc: Starts once a background task that every 22500 units, about, picks a random sector. For a sector with an owner and without flag 2 it asks SelectEvent for any event kind, then runs ControlShipsOfSector on that sector and on the player's sector.

SelectEvent.doc: Chooses one god event at random, weighted by priority, among the slots that match the sector and the event kind mask, then creates and accepts it. Class slots weigh their EvaluatePriority, script slots the prio result. Returns 1 when an event started, 0 when none fired.

SetShipsToRebuildCacheEnabled.doc: Clears the ship rebuild cache and sets its enabled flag (m21).

ShouldRebuildJobShip.doc: Returns 0 when a rebuildable job has no room left: quota minus live ships minus queued rebuilds is negative. Returns 1 otherwise, and always 1 for jobs that cannot be rebuilt.

comments.text: Disabled while flag m24 bit 1 is set.
Build script arguments: position in 500-unit cells, station class, factory id, sector, owner.
The wreck nearest to the site is self-destructed (code 21).
Builder reached the site: the station is created from the record, as in RespawnStation.
Build effect: override effects 1 and 2 flash on the new station, then are cleared.

StartRebuild.doc: Starts rebuilding a destroyed station from its record. Picks the nearest eligible TL ship (class 2032, within 600 route units) as builder, runs its command-32 script to fly there, then recreates the station as RespawnStation does. Returns 1 when started, 0 when the command script is missing, nothing when disabled or invalid.

StartTasks.doc: Forks the start-up: waits about 60 s (plus up to 20 s random) until the galaxy is built, refreshes the fight and economy stats of every sector, then starts the control tasks.

StopTasks.doc: Kills every background task whose id is stored in the task fields, then clears those fields.

Vbi.doc: Calls Vbi on every running event (state 1) each frame.

302.name: GodEngine

303.doc: Singleton that respawns destroyed ships, asteroids and stations in the universe after a delay (dobj: REBUILD). Ships are tracked from a scan at game start, asteroids and stations are queued when destroyed. A background task wakes every 60 s and recreates whatever is due. RequestRebuild is called from the object destructors.

Init.doc: Clears all tables, scans the galaxy for rebuildable ships and starts the rebuild task: every 60 s it rebuilds due ships, stations and asteroids and removes them from the queues.

class 2019 (probably M-class big ship) needs a free dock port of that subtype
Create(x, y, z, subType, race)

start the post-rebuild script with the sector as argument

RebuildShip.doc: Recreates a lost ship of the given race and class in or near a sector (REBUILD feature). Non-Khaak races build it at the nearest shipyard, which must have a free dock port for capital classes and must not be the player's current environment; Khaak (race 7) spawn it at a random spot in the sector. Returns 1 on success, 0 if no shipyard or port is available.

race 8 (pirates) only when game feature bit 4 is set

place the base at a random point around the sector centre

RebuildStation.doc: Recreates a destroyed station/factory from a saved rebuild record (array: class, subtype, sector, race, position, rotation, wares, factory id, efficiency, name id, ship counts). Pirate bases are moved to a random free sector; stations of other types are queued with GodEngine.AddStationToRebuild. Returns 1 if rebuilt or queued, 0/nothing otherwise.

RequestRebuild.doc: Queues an object for rebuild. Ships: only tracked ones not owned by the player; delay 5..9 min for Kha'ak (race 7), 15..29 min otherwise. Rebuildable asteroids: 3..10 days. Stations/docks flagged for rebuild and not player-owned: 6..24 h. Returns 0 if the object is not accepted, else 1.

comments.text: race mask 192 = Xenon and Kha'ak (races 6, 7)

ScanGalaxyShips.doc: Fills the tracked-ship table: ships of sectors that have gates (or belong to the Kha'ak) that are big ships (2073, not 2142) or Xenon/Kha'ak fighters (2034), owned by races 1-7 or 18. Each is mapped to its home sector (TLs: their home sector).

303.name: Rebuild

304.doc: Singleton service that slowly recharges the shields of NPC ships outside the player's sector (probably the off-screen shield regeneration). Ships register with Add() together with a per-tick recharge amount; a background task wakes every 3 seconds and applies it.

0.doc: ship -> shield amount restored per 3 s tick
0.name: rechargeTable

1.doc: id of the recharge background task, 0 when stopped
1.name: taskId

class 2016 (station) keeps shields as counts per type; expand into one entry per shield
no usable shields or no generator: cannot recharge
demand exceeds generator output: scale each shield's share down

Add.doc: Registers a ship for off-screen shield recharge. Computes the recharge per tick from the ship's power generator (x3) and the efficiency/power usage of its shield types, capped by generator output. Removes the ship if nothing can be recharged.

comments.text: ships with an object id are simulated by the engine, so skip them
SetReloaderShield sets the shield without the usual effects

Init.doc: Allocates the table and forks the recharge loop (every 3 s). Removes ships that no longer exist, are active in the 3D world (have an object id), have no sector or are already at full shield.

Remove.doc: Unregisters a ship from the recharge table.

304.name: ShieldReloader

305.doc: Singleton service that slowly repairs the hull of damaged ships and stations in sectors outside the active simulation. A background task wakes every 10 seconds and adds each registered object's repair amount (about 1% of max hull + 1).

0.doc: object -> hull points restored per 10 s tick
0.name: repairTable

1.doc: id of the repair background task, 0 when stopped
1.name: taskId

Add.doc: Registers a damaged object for slow hull repair; amount per tick is maxHull/100 + 1. Removes it if already at full hull, not in a valid environment, or owned by the player.

comments.text: environment must be a ship (2004) or dock (2007); player-owned objects are not auto-repaired

Init.doc: Allocates the table and forks the repair loop (every 10 s). Drops objects that vanished, are at full hull, not located in a sector/ship/dock environment, or are owned by the player race.

Remove.doc: Unregisters an object from the repair table.

305.name: HullRepairer

306.doc: Singleton that keeps a table of temporary NPC merchants attached to stations: each has a name, the wares it wants to buy, the wares it offers, funds and a trade-rank requirement. Merchants are generated for a station, shrink as the player trades with them and expire after about 45 game minutes. Created from the script that handles merchant trading (see AddMerchant call in the main story code).

0.doc: table: merchant name -> [name, station, wantedWares, offeredWares, funds, tradeRank, expireTime, station]
0.name: merchants

comments.text: record: [0] name, [1] station, [2] wares wanted (ware code -> amount), [3] wares offered, [4] funds, [5] trade rank, [6] expire age, [7] station copy

AddMerchant.doc: Registers a merchant record unless the name exists. Expire time is the current age plus 0..616 s.

CleanMerchant.doc: Removes empty entries from both ware tables; removes the merchant if either table became empty. Returns 1 if removed.

ExpireMerchants.doc: Deletes merchants older than 2696 s since their expire time was set.

GetMerchantByName.doc: Returns the merchant record or nothing.

comments.text: second loop repeats the first one over merchant[3]; likely meant merchant[2] (wanted wares): the offered wares are counted twice

GetMerchantFunds.doc: Estimated worth of a merchant: average prices of the wares in its offered-wares table plus its cash.

GetMerchantMaxPrice.doc: Highest price a merchant pays: average price above 85% fill, else interpolated from 120% of the max price down to the average.

GetMerchantMinTradeRank.doc: Minimum trade rank needed to deal with a merchant, derived from the merchant's rank value (<10: -100, <800: 0, <30000: 33333, else 3333).

comments.text: the loop bound re-rolls SE_Random each iteration, so the number of generated names is not fixed (quirk)
mask 1216 = races 6, 7, 10 (Xenon, Kha'ak, player)

GetMerchantNameByStation.doc: Picks a merchant name for a station: generated pilot names of the station's race plus names of pilots of ships docked or parked there (excluding races in mask 1216), duplicates removed, one chosen at random.

GetMerchantNamesForStation.doc: Returns an array of the merchant names at a station.

GetMerchantsForStation.doc: Returns an array of all merchant records at a station.

GetUsableWares.doc: Returns a table ware code -> total container size of all wares the sector's non-shipyard factories (resources and products) and docks (tradeables) handle.

comments.text: ware type -> base probability in 1/1000

GetWareBaseProbability.doc: Base per-mille probability that a merchant deals in a ware, by ware type (lasers 65, shields 95, missiles 230, ... type 16 software 0).

GetWareBuyProbability.doc: Per-mille chance a merchant wants a ware: base probability scaled by the free storage fraction.

comments.text: 14000 = typical hold volume limit

GetWareOwnedAmount.doc: Random amount of a ware a merchant offers: limited by availability / relative value and by the merchant's rank, and capped to about a 14000-volume hold most of the time.

GetWareSellProbability.doc: Per-mille chance a merchant offers a ware: base probability scaled by the filled storage fraction.

GetWareStoragePercent.doc: Percentage of the sector's storage capacity for a ware that is filled (all factories handling it plus docks). Returns 1 if there is no capacity.

GetWareValue.doc: Price of a ware in a sector: max price below 15% fill, else interpolated from max to min price by fill percentage.

GetWareWantAmount.doc: Random amount of a ware a merchant wants to buy, based on the station storage fill, minimum price and the merchant's rank.

MerchantGotWares.doc: Called when the player sold wares to the merchant: reduces the amount it wants and cleans the record.

MerchantSoldWares.doc: Called when the player bought wares from the merchant: reduces the offered amount and cleans the record.

comments.text: drops expired merchants first
rank = player's trade ranking +-65%, clamped to 40..2000000; 12.5% of merchants get a random rank up to 1.5M
mode 0 = wants the ware, 1 = offers it, 2 = skip (already decided on the other side)
funds = random(rank*26) + 4576

PopulateMerchants.doc: Creates 6..13 random merchants for a station that has none yet. For each, picks a name and a trade rank (87.5% around the player's trade ranking, otherwise a wide linear range) and rolls for each usable ware whether the merchant wants it or offers it.

ResetMerchantExpire.doc: Restarts the merchant's expire timer at the current age.

remove the wares from the ship with a negative count to InstallWare
place each eject object behind the ship, at a distance of twice the sizes of both objects

EjectWare.doc: Base class: does not eject wares. Returns 0.

GetAbortedText.doc: Aborted text (text 4 of the text page).

GetAnswers.doc: Base class: returns the running answer result unchanged.

GetClassType.doc: Returns the class id of this base class (3100).

GetEnvironmentTrack.doc: Base class: no environment music track. Returns 0.

GetFinishText.doc: Finish text (text 3 of the text page).

GetLocation.doc: Returns the environment saved with the quest.

GetLogbookAbortedText.doc: Logbook text written on abort (text 7 of the text page).

GetLogbookText.doc: Logbook text written on accept (text 5 of the text page).

GetQuestionArray.doc: Base class: no question array. Returns 0.

GetUpdateText.doc: Update text (text 2 of the text page).

PlayerLeftShip.doc: Hook called when the player leaves the ship. Empty in the base class.

Prepare.doc: Picks a random speaker face (1 to 5) and records the current environment.

ReceiveDialogParameter.doc: Base class: parameter not handled. Returns -1.

SellWare.doc: Sells arg4 units of a ware from the seller to the player at the seller's unit price. Money and ware moves are applied to both sides.

Set.doc: Empty hook for subclasses to set up their data.

SpeakText.doc: Speaks a text with priority 150 in a forked task, so the caller does not wait.

AddListener.doc: Registers a cursor listener object with a callback mask (1 NotifyClick, 2 NotifyMouseMove, 4 GetCursorIcon) and a priority, keeping the list ordered by priority (high first).

CenterCursor.doc: Puts the cursor in the centre of the clip box.

CheckListenerCallbacks.doc: True if the object implements every callback its mask promises.

CleanupListeners.doc: Drops listeners whose object no longer exists or lacks the promised callbacks.

comments.text: 0x6000 = release flags: clear the held flag
press: ignore if already held
only listeners with callback bit 1 (NotifyClick)
after a release the remaining listeners are told the cursor is elsewhere

Click.doc: Mouse button event. Press events are dispatched once per press; flags 24576 (0x6000) mark release events, which are dispatched to all listeners (the first is told the position, the rest get -1,-1). A listener returning true consumes a press. Always returns 1 for handled events.

DisableFollowSteering.doc: Counts disable requests (true) and releases (false). On the first disable it remembers whether follow steering was on and switches to pointer mode; on the last release it restores follow steering.

GetKeepAutopilot.doc: Flag that keeps the autopilot on (m21).

GetLongTermSteeringMode.doc: Steering mode, reporting 1 while follow steering is only temporarily disabled.

comments.text: camera flags |= 8228
cursor instance flags2 |= 512|16384|4096 (overlay drawing)

Init.doc: Creates the interface scene and its camera (priority 200), loads the cursor body (gui_master), places the cursor in the screen centre, and sets the default pointer icon 1100.

IsCursorLocked.doc: True when the cursor is locked (m7).

IsCursorVisible.doc: True unless the hidden mode (2) is active.

IsFollowSteeringDisabled.doc: True while at least one disable request is open.

LockCursor.doc: Locks the cursor: hides it, stops steering and click handling.

MoveCursorAbsolute.doc: Puts the cursor at a position and dispatches the move.

MoveCursorRelative.doc: Moves the cursor by a delta and dispatches the move.

OnMonitorChanged.doc: Called when the active monitor changes; refreshes steering for its mode.

OnMonitorModeChanged.doc: Re-evaluates steering for a new monitor mode and resets follow steering if the monitor has no active control.

ResetFollowSteering.doc: Back to pointer mode unless the cursor is hidden.

SetClipping.doc: Resets the clip box to the full screen.

SetCursorIcon.doc: Switches the cursor icon. For the pointer icons 1100,1103-1105 the icon centre offset is half the icon size so the hotspot is centred.

comments.text: X2_SetControlMatrix(axis, function, set, flag): mode 0 = pointer axes

SetMouseMapping.doc: Maps mouse axes 512/513 to control functions per steering mode: pointer (11/12), follow steering (13-16), hidden/mouse look (1,2,4,5).

SetSteeringMode.doc: Public setter: while follow steering is disabled (count>0) a request for mode 1 is remembered and mode 0 is used instead.

ShowTooltipAtCursor.doc: Shows a tooltip next to the cursor.

ShowTooltipAtCursorWithDelay.doc: Shows a tooltip at the cursor (offset 20,8) in the main monitor's cockpit, optionally delayed.

UnlockCursor.doc: Unlocks the cursor and shows it if visible; in mode 1 refreshes the position.

UpdateCursor.doc: Clamps the cursor to the clip box, moves the icon, refreshes steering and sends NotifyMouseMove to the listeners (the first to accept it stops the chain, the rest get -1,-1), then refreshes the icon.

UpdateCursorIcon.doc: Asks the listeners (those with callback bit 4) for a cursor icon at the current position; the first non-zero answer wins, else the default pointer 1100.

UpdateCursorSteering.doc: Tells the engine whether the mouse steers the ship: follow steering is active in mode 1, and cockpit steering only if the active monitor is in cockpit view and the cursor is not hidden. Not active while the cursor is locked.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame: refreshes the cursor icon unless hidden.

comments.text: mode 1 without active monitor control falls through as mode 0
leaving mode 2 makes the cursor visible again
hidden mode releases the held-button flag

__SetSteeringMode.doc: Applies a steering mode: 0 pointer, 1 follow steering (needs an active-control monitor, else falls back to 0), 2 hidden cursor. Updates cursor visibility, monitors, mouse mapping and engine steering.

6001.doc: Table of AI ship jobs. Job definitions come from addon\types\Jobs.txt (JobWings.txt for wing groups; per-universe variants by g10). Each job holds quota, scripts, race mask, flags and upgrades; the class creates, places and tracks the job ships, and is used by GodEngine (class 302) to rebuild them. Not named by dobj; the name is derived.

0.doc: job id -> attribute array (slots listed in LoadConfigFile comment)
0.name: jobTable

1.doc: job id -> {ship -> ship} of ships currently assigned to the job
1.name: jobShips

2.doc: shopping list id -> cached array of ware keys (type << 16 | subtype)
2.name: shoppingLists

3.doc: wing group id -> list of job ids that spawn together (JobWings.txt)
3.name: jobWingGroups

ActivateJob.doc: Enables rebuilding of a job (flag bit 1) and builds its initial ships.

AddShip.doc: Adds a ship to the job's ship list.

comments.text: Quota above the ship index: race is the index-th race bit of the mask (race 8 skipped); otherwise a random race of the mask
No sector to place into: rebuild requests are made without a sector
Sector pick: up to 3 random tries, then the first sector below the per-sector limit (slot 1)

BuildInitJobShips.doc: Spawns the initial ships of a rebuildable job: the quota (slot 0) is spread over the sectors from GetSectorListForJob, respecting the per-sector limit (slot 1).

CanRebuild.doc: True if the job is rebuilt by the rebuild logic (flag bit 1, slot 37).

CanUseByRace.doc: True if the race object may use the job (race mask, slot 28).

comments.text: Ship classes 2135 take the location as first constructor argument
Race 8 ships keep the original race as pilot subrace
Race 8 ships (probably pirates): upgrades scale with the player's fight ranking title
Wares with flag bit 1 in g46 are not copied as default equipment
Cover race is cleared when slot 28 has bit 256 and slot 37 has no bit 4
Ship docks at the dock object if docking is possible: by the dock chance (slot 23) when atDock is set, otherwise when the location is a sector
Slot 22 bit 2 skips placing the ship in the sector
Job start script (slot 3) runs with the ship, job id and sector as arguments
No environment (sector): the ship is destroyed again
Slot 37 bits: 2 invincible, 32 average speed, 64 disables race logic
Jobs with a wing group id (slot 8) also spawn that wing group

CreateShip.doc: Creates one ship of a job: class from the subtype, position, race, upgrades, hue, default equipment, job script and wing group. Placed in location, or at dockObject when docking is allowed. Returns the ship, or 0 on failure.

CreateShipforJob.doc: Chooses a subtype for the job and race and creates the ship with CreateShip. Returns 0 if no subtype fits.

comments.text: A new sector is picked when none is given, or when the sector has reached the per-sector limit (slot 1)
Shipyard search for jobs with slot 22 bit 1 and a dock chance: races with notoriety above -10000 use a shipyard of the subtype's race
Race 8 (probably pirates) uses its own docks that can take the subtype
Otherwise a station with a free dock port is chosen by the dock chance (slot 23)
Slot 22 bit 4: a random gate of the sector, not for race 7
Slot 22 bit 8: placed between two random gates or stations of the sector (probably)
Slot 22 bit 16: placed at a random offset from the sector's center, scaled by its size (probably)
CreateShip(location, dock, subtype, job, x, y, z, race, showEffect, 0, warId)

CreateShipforJobAtObject.doc: Creates a job ship of a race in a sector, at a shipyard or dock if one fits, else at a gate, between two points or at a random offset. Sector is chosen at random when none is given. Returns the ship or 0.

comments.text: Member count: random between 75 % and 125 % of the quota
Peace-time members are counted as desired job ships of the sector and added to the job
Creation failed without war: a rebuild is requested for the job

CreateWingGroup.doc: Spawns the members of a job wing group around the leader ship. Each job gives 75 to 125 percent of its quota. In a war (warId not 0) members register as war objects; otherwise they are counted as desired job ships and added to the job. A failed member becomes a rebuild request.

GetActivShipList.doc: Returns the ship list of a job (name keeps the original spelling).

GetAggression.doc: Aggression of a job's ships (slot 33, in percent).

GetChangeSectorOnRebuild.doc: Flag bit 16 (slot 37): a rebuilt ship may move to another sector.

GetComment.doc: Comment text of a job (slot 39). LoadConfigFile never stores slot 39, so this returns nothing (possible bug or unused).

GetFightskill.doc: Fight skill of a job's ships (slot 35, in percent).

GetJobCount.doc: Number of jobs in the table.

GetJobScript.doc: Script run by the ships of a job (slot 2).

comments.text: The race is re-rolled when it cannot build this subtype, or with the chance in slot 19
Race 1 (except type 8) and race 5 are built as race 8 (probably pirates); the original race is kept in originalRace
GetDefaultShipSSubTypeFromGType2(type, race, originalRace, sizeClass)

GetJobShipSubtype.doc: Picks the ship subtype for a job and race: the fixed subtype (slot 13), or a random subtype matching the size mask (slot 16), race flags (slot 15) and type mask (slot 14). Returns -1 when nothing fits.

GetJobShipsPerSector.doc: Number of job ships in a sector: the local ship count for local jobs, otherwise the desired job ship count.

GetJumpRange.doc: Jump range of a job's ships (slot 10).

GetMorale.doc: Morale of a job's ships (slot 34, in percent).

GetQuota.doc: Number of ships a job wants (slot 0).

comments.text: Race 8 is always skipped; races with notoriety below 0 towards raceId are skipped unless the special flags are set

GetRandomRaceFromRaceMask.doc: Picks a random race from a race mask. Race 8 (probably pirates) is never chosen. When raceId is given, races with negative notoriety towards it are skipped unless the mask has flags 524544. Returns 0 if no race is left.

comments.text: Fixed sector: only usable if it is not disabled for job init
Slot 20 bit 31 inverts the filters below: sectors are kept when they fail them
Sector skipped when it already holds the per-sector limit (slot 1) of this job's ships

GetSectorListForJob.doc: Returns the sectors where a job may place ships for a race, as a set {sector: sector}. A fixed sector (slot 21) gives a single entry; 0 if that sector is disabled for job init. Returns nothing for an invalid job.

GetShipCount.doc: Number of ships currently assigned to a job.

comments.text: Ware types 5 to 16 are scanned
Ware key packs type << 16 | subtype

GetShoppingList.doc: Returns the ware keys (type << 16 | subtype) of the job's shopping list, computed once per list id and cached in m2.

GetTextID.doc: Text id of a job's name (slot 4).

GetTradeskill.doc: Trade skill of a job's ships (slot 32, in percent).

GetUNameID.doc: Universal name id of a job (slot 5).

Init.doc: Loads the job tables, resets the per-job ship lists and the shopping list cache, and applies the job flags.

IsJobID.doc: True if the id is a positive job id that exists in the job table.

IsLocalShip.doc: True if the job's ships are local (flag bit 8, slot 37). Local jobs are counted per sector.

IsShipJobShip.doc: True if the ship is in the job's ship list.

comments.text: A per-universe file is used when g10 is not the default x3_universe
Loop stops before the last line, so a final line with no line break is never read (possible bug)
First line holds the file version; later columns exist only in newer versions

Slot layout: 0 quota, 1 max ships per sector, 2 job script, 3 config script, 4 text id, 5 uname id, 6 name override id, 7 name flags, 8 wing group id, 9 shopping list id, 10 jump range, 11 idle rate, 12 spawn time, 13 ship subtype (-1 random), 14 ship type mask, 15 race flags, 16 size class mask, 17 hue, 18 saturation, 19 race re-roll chance %, 20 sector filter flags, 21 fixed sector (x << 16 | y), 22 spawn flags, 23 dock chance %, 24 cargo upgrades, 25 speed upgrades, 26 other upgrades, 27 rotation accel offset, 28 race mask, 29 shields, 30 weapon value, 31 weapon flags, 32 trade skill, 33 aggression, 34 morale, 35 fight skill, 36 unused here, 37 job flags, 38 job group
Default script lookup: '!job.<name>' first, then 'job.<name>'; a job without script is skipped
Config script lookup: '!config.<name>' first, then 'config.<name>'
Flags default 64 when the config version is 4 or newer; bits 1, 2, 4, 8 are read from the next four columns
Subtype name is resolved with SA_GetSubTypeByName; -1 when absent
Flag word defaults to 2 when no bit was set
Bit 31 set from a column: negative flag bit
Old config without the newest columns: flag 64 is added to the sector filter (slot 20) when races 17 and 18 are not in the mask
Bit 30 flag from the last column
Group columns of newer files: group id 1, 2 or 3 in slot 38
Job stored under its id

LoadConfigFile.doc: Parses addon\types\Jobs.txt (or Jobs.<universe>.txt) into a table jobId -> attribute array. The attribute slots are listed in the comment at the array allocation.

comments.text: Rows are read from the last to the first; row 0 is a header
First field of a row is the group id; the rest are job ids

LoadGroupConfigFile.doc: Parses addon\types\JobWings.txt into a table group id -> list of job ids that spawn together. Non-positive job ids are dropped.

comments.text: Missing ships = quota - rebuilds already pending - ships alive
Non-local jobs: each missing ship is requested as a rebuild with a random race of the race mask
Local jobs: sector grid g6 (24 x 20) is scanned for sectors holding ships of this job
Too many local ships are removed sector by sector
Too few local ships: rebuild requests go to random sectors of the job's sector list

Reinit.doc: Reloads the job files after a load and tops up every rebuildable job. Missing ships are requested through GodEngine.RequestRebuild; for local jobs surplus ships are removed and missing ones spread over sectors.

RemoveShip.doc: Removes a ship from the job's ship list.

comments.text: Clears bit 1 (can rebuild) for group members

UpdateJobFlags.doc: Clears the rebuild flag (bit 1 of slot 37) of every job listed in a job wing group. Those jobs are presumably rebuilt through their group.

6001.name: JobManager

Owns the three monitor objects (class 606) in fields m2, the monitor overlay scene (HUD text, radar, weapons panel, info panel) and the monitor layout bit mask. Called statically as C605.F() from the cockpit UI and from the game loop; Init runs once at start, OverlayLoop and UpdateMonitors redraw the overlay every frame.

comments.text: activation fails when the monitor has no object, or the object is neither the player's ship nor in the player's sector
active control goes to the new monitor when it can take it and the monitor is not in mode 16, and cockpit 0 is the target
view mode 8 (tracking, probably) does not raise the redraw count

ActivateMonitor.doc: Makes a monitor the active one. Returns 1 when it is active now, 0 when the target object is not visible from the player's sector (then the change waits for the overlay loop). Shows the monitor layout when needed and moves the active control to the new monitor.

ActiveMonitorTrackPrevNext.doc: Moves the tracking of the active monitor to the previous or next object.

CallInfiniteLoop.doc: Forwards to the global CallInfiniteLoop (debug helper that keeps the script in a loop).

comments.text: operator precedence: the player's ship is accepted first; the sector test applies to other ships

CanObjectGetActiveControl.doc: True when the object may take the active control: the player's ship, or a class 2004 ship that allows monitor control and is in the player's sector (class 2001 environment).

CanTrackObject.doc: True when the active monitor can track the object.

ChangeCurrentMissileType.doc: Changes the current missile type of the active monitor.

ChangeView.doc: Changes the view of the active monitor with the given mode flags (see ChangeView2 with no second argument).

comments.text: with the main monitor in mode 2 and tracking active, the view switches to the target view (260 or 516)
cycling past the last cockpit resets the view override and returns to the external view 258
the active control moves to the new cockpit when it was active or the main monitor shows cockpit 0

ChangeView2.doc: Changes the view of the active monitor. Flags: 1 cycles the cockpits of the reference object, 2 and 4096 switch the view mode of the monitor, 4 switches to tracking or the zoom, 8 and 16 clear the reference object. Second argument set means a forced change. Returns 1 when changed.

ChangeViewForMonitor.doc: Applies a view mode to one monitor: flag 1 selects mode 1, 2 resets the cockpit to 0, 4 and 8/16 handle the target and object views. Returns 1 when applied.

CheckEquipment.doc: Checks an equipment id on the active monitor's view.

comments.text: camera priority 140 for the subtitle camera
animation path 4678 drives the two subtitle bodies

CheckSubTitleInst.doc: Creates or frees the subtitle scene (camera priority 140, two animated bodies 10575 and 10576) depending on whether subtitle lines are active (m21).

comments.text: owner mask 16576 (0x40C0) must be clear; meaning probably faction/enemy status, not verified

CheckTargetTips.doc: Shows a game tip for a locked target: capturable ships (2004) when not on alert, dockable stations (2016) when not owned by a hostile mask and docking is allowed, and class 2084 objects.

comments.text: hit box of one laser slot: 75 x 32 pixels; the right 17 pixels toggle the laser group bit
missile selection box
laser group buttons: 13 pixels per group, 4 groups
auto-aim mode text: cycles from the maximum mode back to 0
fast-forward toggle via equipment 23 icon
click on the tracking info panel

ClickDisplayPanel.doc: Handles a click on the display panel: toggles turret laser groups, opens the laser or missile selection, sets the laser group or cycles the auto-aim mode, or hits the info panel. Returns 1 when the click was used.

comments.text: click in the top strip toggles game feature 4194304 (numeric hull and shield display)
speed slider: sets the desired speed of the object, stops the autopilot and fast-forward first
click on another panel activates that monitor

ClickInfoPanel.doc: Handles a click on an info panel: opens the context menu, toggles the numeric display (game feature 4194304), sets the desired speed from the speed slider, or activates the monitor. Returns 1 when used.

DisplayMarineSkillStarsInMonitor.doc: Draws one marine skill value as stars (7 pixels apart) or a dash when the value is zero.

DisplayMessage.doc: Shows a message on the main monitor.

DisplayMessageWithDuration.doc: Shows a message on the main monitor for a duration.

DoEnemyTracking.doc: Starts tracking of an enemy on the active monitor.

DoTracking.doc: Starts tracking on the active monitor.

comments.text: upgrade bonus of the ship (ware counter 1048593) is added to the speed
rotation speed shown scaled by 600 (SE_MulFix) and divided by 10; the bonus is added at 0x0eb7fe
trade container bonus of the ship is ware counter 1048592
transport class names come from page 1999 (container classes S, M, L, XL, ST)
factory resources: at most 3 are listed, else the none text 35:4501
energy factor of the sector suns; 98304 (1.5 in 16.16 fixed point) is used when there is no sector
fixed value 26 for the production cycle yield of kind 5 factories (probably)

DrawCommWindowOverlay.doc: Draws the detail page of the communication window for an item: laser (kind 8), missile (kind 10), ship type (kind 7) or ware or factory (kind 5 and 6). Arg3 is an optional ship whose upgrade bonuses are added to the displayed stats.

comments.text: symbol 267 (probably the marine icon) is drawn for class 1700 objects
marine skills are shown only for own marines or when equipment 104 is installed (probably a skill scanner)
command 609 is a hotkey command id (probably the mouse-over action); the key name comes from the key table

DrawCommWindowOverlayForObject.doc: Draws the communication window page for one object: for class 1700 (marine or similar) the name and the four marine skills with stars; for class 2134 the name, ID code and class code. Shows the hotkey of command 609 in the overlay.

DrawCommandName.doc: Draws a command name text at the top of a monitor.

DrawDistance.doc: Draws the distance to the object in km. Uses the cockpit when the monitor is in mode 1, else the reference object.

DrawHotkeyInCommOverlay.doc: Draws the key name of a command in the communication overlay, right aligned, with a marker when the key has the modifier flag 4096.

comments.text: game feature 4194304 selects the numeric hull and shield display instead of the bars

DrawHullShields.doc: Draws hull and shield percent of an object. Uses the numeric display (game feature 4194304) or the bars.

comments.text: the name line is shifted up when the panel has a second line (arg6)

DrawInfoPanel.doc: Draws one object info panel: frame icon, name, symbol, hull and shield values, ID code, and speed or distance.

DrawModeName.doc: Draws a mode name text at the bottom of a monitor.

DrawObjectIDCode.doc: Draws the object ID code right aligned at the given x.

DrawObjectName.doc: Draws the object name, colored by the selection flag.

DrawObjectSymbol.doc: Draws the object symbol in the info panel. Adds flags for own ship (8), enemy (2), active 2066 (128) and civilian ships (65536) before calling the native symbol draw.

DrawSpeed.doc: Draws the object speed in km/s right aligned.

comments.text: max speed is raised to the current speed when it is lower
desired speed as a fraction of max speed in 16.16 fixed point, clamped to 65536 (100 percent)

DrawSpeedBar.doc: Draws a speed bar: current speed fill, desired speed marker, and a frame icon. Frame icon 6 when the highlight flag is set, 7 for a negative speed, else 8.

Exit.doc: Stops the overlay and clears the monitor overlay instance array.

FireLaser.doc: Fires the lasers from the active monitor's cockpit.

GetActiveMonitorCockpitNumber.doc: Cockpit number of the active monitor.

GetActiveMonitorControlObject.doc: The reference object of the active monitor, nothing when it has no active control.

GetActiveMonitorControlObjectID.doc: Object id of the active control object, 0 when none.

GetActiveMonitorTracking.doc: Tracking mode of the active monitor.

GetActiveMonitorTrackingObject.doc: Tracked object of the active monitor.

GetAutoAimModeName.doc: Text for the laser auto-aim mode: 35:995, 35:996, 35:994, or 35:997 for unknown modes.

GetCursorIcon.doc: Cursor icon at a screen position: the display panel first, then the monitors top down. Returns 0 when there is none.

comments.text: tooltip with the ware name of the laser type in the slot
tooltip with the ware name of the current missile type, or the no-missile text 35:4633

GetCursorIconForDisplayPanel.doc: Returns the cursor icon for the display panel (1100 for a clickable area). Shows the laser type tooltip when hovering a laser slot.

GetCursorIconForInfoPanel.doc: Cursor icon over an info panel. Shows the speed tooltip over the speed slider (0 gives the stop text 10544 of page 1903).

comments.text: ignores m28 unlike the other default view functions; looks like an oversight, unverified

GetDefaultAutoMissileViewMode.doc: Default auto-missile view mode for a ship. Unlike the other defaults it ignores the relative-mode flag and always returns 272 (or 272 for the player's ship).

GetDefaultAutoTargetViewMode.doc: Default auto-target view mode for a ship (264 or 520, 264 for the player's own ship).

comments.text: 258 = fixed external view; 514 = same view with the relative flag (512) set
relative flag 512 is added when the relative-mode default m28 is set

GetDefaultExternalViewMode.doc: Default external view mode for a ship: a fixed view for the player's own ship and the relative view by default. Returns a view mode bit mask.

GetDefaultTargetViewMode.doc: Default target view mode for a ship, like GetDefaultExternalViewMode but for the target view (260 or 516).

comments.text: 0 percent: always the red color

GetFlashColor.doc: Returns a flashing color for low hull or shield values: the given color, or a red/yellow blinking color at low percent.

GetLeftOffset.doc: Returns the horizontal offset of the left-hand monitor layout.

comments.text: 12 = base visibility of the main monitor
51 added to the main monitor when the overlay is not hidden
11 = base visibility of the side monitors
side monitor 2 is hidden while the comm window is open
a side monitor whose object is not the player's ship and not in a class 2001 environment is hidden (returns 64 when minimized)
side monitor shows 64 when minimized, else 0

GetMonitorVisibility.doc: Visibility flags of a monitor: 12 for the main monitor (plus 51 when the overlay is shown), 11 for a side monitor, 0 when hidden by the active menu, the comm window or the overlay hide counter. Adds 64 when the monitor is minimized.

GetMonitors.doc: Array of the three monitor objects.

GetNumLayoutMonitors.doc: Number of monitors the layout provides.

GetRadarRange.doc: Radar range of the main monitor.

HideCommWindow.doc: Hides the communication window by clearing its title.

comments.text: overlay mode ids per monitor index (0, 21, 22, 19); used when drawing the side monitors
monitor 0 is the main cockpit monitor, monitors 1 and 2 are side monitors; text 35:4217 Main Monitor, 35:4102 Monitor #N
side monitors start with the default external view for the player's reference object

Init.doc: Sets the default monitor state, allocates the monitor arrays, creates the three monitor objects (class 606) and sets the default views for monitors 1 and 2.

comments.text: all monitor input is ignored while the player ship is docked
key 707 plays sound 957 when SelectNext moved to another monitor, else 956

Input.doc: Key input for the monitor shortcuts: records a pressed key (m31) with its time and held state; ignores all input while docked. Key 707 plays the next-view sound.

IsActive.doc: True when the monitor system is shown (m1).

IsCommWindowVisible.doc: True while the communication window has a title.

IsOverlayVisible.doc: True when the overlay is not hidden (m34 is 0).

IsRelModeDefault.doc: Returns the relative-mode default flag m28.

LaunchMissile.doc: Launches a missile from the active monitor's ship.

MinimizeAllMonitors.doc: Disconnects both side monitors. Returns 1 when at least one was connected.

MonitorLostActiveControl.doc: Activates the main monitor when the active control is lost on a side monitor.

MonitorLostSelection.doc: Activates the main monitor when the selection on a side monitor is lost.

MoveCockpit.doc: Moves the cockpit of the active monitor.

comments.text: modifier bits 24576 (probably modifier keys) disable the click
a click on the display panel makes the main monitor the active one unless the context menu is open

NotifyClick.doc: Handles a mouse click: ignored when the modifier bits 24576 are set or the monitors are not built. Without an active menu the display panel is tried first, then the monitors from the top one down. Returns 1 when used.

NotifyMouseMove.doc: Passes a mouse move to the monitors, top one first. Returns 1 when a monitor takes it.

comments.text: the lock applies only when the event's object is the ref object of the cockpit on this monitor
mode bit 8 (auto target): interrupt the monitor task so it retargets
target object exists: speak its name by type
types 6 and 7: spoken as a name array, with priority -1
type 18 (probably a jump object or gate): speak the destination sector name with voice 7
no target object: speak the object's text id (speech 17) if one exists
the target is marked as targeted
ships (2004), 2016 and 2084 objects are recorded as known wares

NotifyTargetLock.doc: Reacts to a target lock event. If the locked object is the active cockpit's ref object, it switches auto-target monitors to it, speaks the object's name and shows tips. Also marks the target as targeted and records ships, stations and class 2084 objects as known wares.

comments.text: enemy aim is on: re-run enemy tracking on the main monitor
speech 13 with priority 4 (probably a 'target lost' line)

NotifyTargetLost.doc: Reacts to a lost target lock. If the lost object is the active cockpit's ref object, it interrupts auto-target monitors or announces enemy aim. Speaks a warning if the player is not in enemy-aim mode.

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Forwards a context-menu return to the ref object: menu ids 20 to 31 are laser turrets, id 10 is missiles.

OnContextMenuUpdate.doc: Forwards a context-menu update to the ref object: menu ids 20 to 31 are laser turrets, id 10 is missiles.

comments.text: monitor 1 is the active one: switch back to the main monitor

OnCursorInvisible.doc: Notifies the monitors that the cursor is hidden; activates the main monitor when side monitor 1 was the active one, then hides the brackets and refreshes the visibility.

OnCursorVisible.doc: Notifies the monitors that the cursor is visible, shows the overlay brackets when no regular menu is open, and refreshes the visibility.

comments.text: menu id 20 + turret number: laser menus use ids 20 to 31

OpenLaserSelection.doc: Opens the laser context menu for a turret of the ref object. Returns 0 when there is no active ship or it is docked, or when the menu is empty.

comments.text: the overlay loop runs in a fork; it is started once and interrupted with TI_Interrupt 605 on later calls

OpenLayout.doc: Reopens the layout: starts monitor 0 (and monitors 1 and 2 when active), stops and disconnects the rest, then refreshes the overlay and starts or interrupts the overlay loop.

OpenMissileSelection.doc: Opens the missile context menu for the ref object. Returns 0 when there is no active ship, the ship is docked, or the menu is empty.

OpenMonitor.doc: Opens a view on one monitor and shows the monitors. Ignored when the monitor index is not in the layout.

comments.text: a running loop task is killed first
zoomed monitor: caption position scaled by the monitor zoom (247 and 189 at zoom 1.0)
switch on the monitor view mode: each case gives a caption text from page 35 (970..985) or 2020 for the mode names; 1 is the plain view
view mode bit 4096 hides the caption
view mode bit 8 (tracking view, probably) shows caption 2020:34 while the target is lost or the signal is lost
view mode bit 16 (probably the target view) shows caption 2020:35 in the same way
cockpit name id 0..6 selects the weapon-panel icon ids (328..342) of the cockpit
cockpit name text from page 2021
after more than 5 loops with pending changes, both pending counters are cleared
idle: wait 400 ms scaled by the time warp; interrupted by TI_Interrupt 605

OverlayLoop.doc: Background loop that redraws the overlay every frame. For each monitor it updates the view, the signal state (lost or found, disconnect), and the mode caption text. It sleeps 400 ms (scaled by the time warp) when no change is pending. Only one copy runs; a new call kills the old task.

RefObjectEvent.doc: Handles a ref-object event. Increments the event counter and interrupts the monitor task to redraw.

ResetMonitorZoom.doc: Resets the zoom of the active monitor to 1.0 (65536).

comments.text: the active control is released from the old monitor unless it is the main monitor's control

RestartAllMonitors.doc: Makes the main monitor the active one again: releases the active control of the old monitor, resets the mode of the main monitor, reopens the layout and restarts the grid.

RestartGrid.doc: Restarts the grid of the active monitor.

RestoreAllMonitors.doc: Shows the monitors and restores every minimized side monitor that is not signal-lost. Returns 1 when any monitor was restored.

comments.text: loop over the visible monitors; the wrap goes back to monitor 0

SelectNext.doc: Activates the next monitor that is connected and has a signal, wrapping to the main monitor. Returns 1 when the selected monitor changed. Does nothing without a layout.

SetActiveMonitorTracking.doc: Sets the tracking mode of the active monitor.

SetCommWindowTitle.doc: Sets the communication window title (empty when no title) and redraws it.

SetCurrentMissile.doc: Sets the current missile of every visible monitor that shows the given ship.

SetLayout.doc: Sets the layout bit mask and recounts the layout monitors: one for the main monitor plus one per set bit.

comments.text: overlay X = 161 + offset, minus 8 px when the offset is non-zero (layout pixels, probably)

SetLeftOffset.doc: Sets the left-hand layout offset. Repositions the main cockpit overlay and updates the side viewports and visibility when the monitor is active.

SetNavMap.doc: Sets the navigation map state of the main monitor.

SetOverlayVisible.doc: Hides (arg false) or shows the overlay with a nesting counter (m34), then refreshes the visibility.

SetPov.doc: Sets the point of view of the active monitor.

SetPovAbsolute2.doc: Sets an absolute point of view with two angles.

SetPovAbsolute6DOF.doc: Sets an absolute point of view with six degrees of freedom.

comments.text: mode bits 8..15 are cleared and 256 (POV) is set

SetPovFromInput.doc: Sets the point of view from player input. A camera that is not a POV type is first switched to the POV view (flag 256); a value of -1 with the POV centered sets -2.

SetRadarOverlayVisible.doc: Refreshes the visibility after a radar overlay change. The argument is not used.

SetRadarRange.doc: Sets the radar range of the main monitor.

SetRelModeAsDefault.doc: Sets the relative-mode default flag m28 used by the default view functions.

comments.text: switches to the custom view mode 4128 first; fails when that is not possible
camera offset defaults to 0,0,0 when none is given

SetViewCustomRef.doc: Sets a custom cockpit view reference: position or object (flags 32, 16 use the given values; flags 2, 64 for the second pair), the view flags, and the camera offset. Returns 1 on success.

SetZoom.doc: Sets the zoom of the active monitor. Returns its result.

ShowCommWindow.doc: Draws the communication window frame with a title and makes it visible.

comments.text: monitors cannot be shown without a layout (m5 == 0)

ShowHideMonitors.doc: Toggles the monitors on or off when a layout exists, reopens the layout and returns the new state.

ShowMonitors.doc: Shows the monitors if they are hidden and a layout exists. Returns 1 when it changed the state, else nothing.

comments.text: duration is scaled to 2/3 of the given value
a zero duration is computed by GetTextDisplayDuration from the text, with 70 as its base argument
a new subtitle is shown for 1500 ms before the first line advances
an appended line is shown for 1000 ms
with several lines, the duration is divided by the number of lines left minus one

ShowSubTitleText.doc: Shows a subtitle line (text array) for a duration. Arg3 forces the line to replace the current subtitle; arg4 is the priority. A line with the same priority is appended to the current one.

comments.text: subscribes to cursor events of class 502 with listener id 20 (probably the monitor control)

StartMainMonitor.doc: Starts the main monitor on the player's ship in cockpit view mode 1, opens the layout, makes it the active control and subscribes to the cursor (C502) events.

comments.text: zoom 65536 = 1.0 (no zoom)

StartMonitor.doc: Resets the zoom of a monitor to 1.0, makes it visible, updates its viewport and sets its visibility flags.

comments.text: viewport covers the screen between the border widths

StartOverlay.doc: Creates the overlay scene (600), its camera and viewport, and the scene state 605 on first use.

comments.text: weapons panel cache reset: forces a full redraw of the weapons panel on the next update
video overlay is shown unless the active menu hides monitor 2

StartOverlayCockpitInst.doc: Creates the cockpit overlay instances (radar, info panel, weapons panel and the monitor video) and resets the weapons panel cache when the weapons panel is created.

comments.text: monitor_text_zoom body when the monitor is zoomed (zoom above 1.0, 65536 = 1.0)
flags 512 | 65536 | 16384 | 4096 for monitor 1 text; 8192 instead of 4096 for monitor 2

StartOverlayInst.doc: Creates the text instance of a side monitor and sets its body and position from the monitor zoom (zoomed text when zoom is above 1).

comments.text: zoom of the monitor selected by the cancelled activation is reset to 1.0

StopActivation.doc: Cancels a pending monitor activation (task m30): resets the zoom of the selected monitor and makes the active monitor the selected one.

StopAllMonitors.doc: Stops the three monitors (highest index first), clears the active monitor, releases the active control of the main monitor and schedules a layout refresh.

StopMonitor.doc: Hides and stops a monitor. Used by OpenLayout and the monitor shutdown path.

StopOverlay.doc: Frees all overlay instances, the overlay camera and the overlay scene, and resets m9.

StopOverlayInst.doc: Frees the overlay instances of a monitor index; index 0 frees the cockpit instances (radar, info, weapons, video). Resets m9 when it was the zoomed monitor.

StopSubTitleText.doc: Clears the subtitle lines and redraws the subtitle bar.

SwitchAutoMissileRefObj.doc: Sets the ref object of every monitor in auto-missile mode (16) to the given object and interrupts the monitor task.

SwitchAutoTargetRefObj.doc: Sets the ref object of every monitor in auto-target mode (8) to the given object and interrupts the monitor task.

SwitchMonitorViewRelObjs.doc: Switches the reference object of every monitor to its next related object.

SwitchViewCameraType.doc: Switches the camera type of the active monitor. Returns its result.

ToggleActiveControl.doc: Toggles the active control of the active monitor. Returns 1 when the control was taken, -1 when it was released, 0 when nothing changed.

ToggleGrid.doc: Toggles the grid of the active monitor.

ToggleLaserTargetMode.doc: Cycles the laser target (auto-aim) mode of the active monitor.

ToggleMonitorZoom.doc: Toggles the zoom of the active side monitor (not the main monitor).

ToggleRadarMode.doc: Toggles the radar mode of the main monitor.

TrackingAllowed.doc: True when the active monitor allows tracking.

6100.doc: Base class of the god-engine story events (no dobj name). GODENGINE (class 302) creates them through SelectEvent and CreateEvent, one slot per event type. Each event has a sector, a priority and a state: 0 new, 1 running, 3 aborted, 4 finished. Concrete events are 6101 (script-driven) and 6102 to 6105 (Khaak, conflict, attack logic, probably).

0.doc: sector the event applies to
0.name: targetSector

1.doc: extra parameter table from the caller, or empty
1.name: eventParams

10.doc: event kind mask given at creation
10.name: eventMask

11.doc: concurrent event limit; never assigned in this batch
11.name: maxEvents

12.doc: creation index, returned by GetID
12.name: eventIndex

13.doc: 1 when the forced bit 2^30 is in the event mask
13.name: isForced

2.doc: target ware id passed by the caller
2.name: targetWare

3.doc: game age when the event was created
3.name: createTime

4.doc: 0 new, 1 running, 3 aborted, 4 finished
4.name: eventState

5.doc: story progress flag; non-zero blocks new events
5.name: storyState

6.doc: priority set by SetPriority; not read in this batch
6.name: priority

7.doc: set to 0 in Init; never read in this batch
7.name: reserved7

8.doc: event type number (slot id, 2 to 8 for class events)
8.name: eventId

9.doc: text page of the event, from its class
9.name: textPage

Abort.doc: Called when the event is aborted. Empty in the base class.

Accept.doc: Called when the event is created and accepted. Empty in the base class.

Check.doc: Returns 1 while the event is alive. Returns 3 to abort, 4 to finish (polled by CheckEvents in GODENGINE).

comments.text: The event class 6100 plus the index must exist and derive from 6100.
Accepted: an event other than the script event (6101) starts as running (state 1).

Create.doc: Creates the event of type 6100 plus index, if that class exists. Stores sector, mask, ware, parameters and creation time, then runs Evaluate. Returns 1 when the event is accepted.

Destruct.doc: Called before the event object is deleted. Empty in the base class.

Evaluate.doc: Decides whether the event can start. Base class returns 0; subclasses override.

EvaluatePriority.doc: Returns the weight of this event for SelectEvent. 0 means it cannot fire now. Base class returns 0.

Finish.doc: Called when the event is finished. Empty in the base class.

GetClassType.doc: Returns the class id 6100 of the base event.

GetScriptName.doc: Name of the event's script. Returns 0 in the base class.

GetTextPage.doc: Text page of the event description (field m9).

Init.doc: Sets the event type number and clears the state and the reserved field.

IsForced.doc: True when the event is forced (field m13).

Select.doc: Handles a dialog choice for this event. Returns 0 in the base class.

Set.doc: Called once after Init in Reinit. Empty in the base class.

SetPriority.doc: Stores the priority set by the god.conf pass in Reinit.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame hook for running events. Empty in the base class.

6101.doc: A god event driven by a script (event type 1). GODENGINE (class 302) creates it for a script slot registered in RegisterScript. The script's commands init, accept, abort, destruct, timer, setenv, killed, attacked and captured run through C700.RunScript or StartScript.

0.doc: script object the event calls
0.name: scriptHandle

1.doc: copy of the slot's script parameter array
1.name: scriptParams

2.doc: list of target objects, or 0
2.name: targetStations

3.doc: slot key, returned by GetEventID
3.name: eventKey

4.doc: ships and stations this event listens to, with callback kind
4.name: listenedObjects

5.doc: script name, the same key as the slot
5.name: scriptName

6.doc: task id of the timer loop, 0 when stopped
6.name: timerTask

7.doc: timer period in time units, 0 disables the timer
7.name: timerInterval

Abort.doc: Runs the script's abort command synchronously.

Accept.doc: Runs the script's accept command when the event is created.

AddEventListenerToObj.doc: Makes this event listen to a ship (2004) or station (2016) with a callback kind. Returns 1 when the listener is added.

CallScript.doc: Runs one command of the event script with a 'command' name and a parameter table. With arg2 set it runs synchronously (RunScript), otherwise it starts a task (StartScript).

comments.text: No timer and nothing listened to: the event is done and is aborted.

Check.doc: Returns 3 (abort) when the event has no timer and no listened objects, else 1.

comments.text: Script handle and listen array are required; otherwise creation fails.

Create.doc: Creates a script event from a slot record: keeps the script handle, the script parameters and the target list, then calls the base Create. Returns 1 on success.

comments.text: Timer task is killed first, if it still exists.

Destruct.doc: Stops the timer, removes this event from all listened objects and runs the script's destruct command.

Evaluate.doc: Script events are always accepted by the base check. Returns 1.

GetEventID.doc: Returns the slot key of the event (its script name key).

GetScriptName.doc: Returns the script name of the event.

GetTargetStations.doc: Returns the target object list of the event.

comments.text: Object kind for the script: 65542 for a ship, 65543 for a station.
Event kinds: 4 setenv, 32 or 2048 killed, 16 attacked, 1024 captured.

NotifyObjectEvent.doc: Forwards an event of a listened object to the script as setenv, killed, attacked or captured, and drops the listener when the object is gone or killed.

RemoveEventListenerFromObj.doc: Stops listening to an object. Returns 1 when it was listened to.

SetTimerInterval.doc: Sets the timer period and restarts the timer, except in the base event type 6101 itself.

comments.text: The timer command runs only while the event state is 1 (running).

Timer.doc: Starts once a loop that calls the script's timer command while the event is running, every m21 time units. Stops when the interval is 0 or the task is gone.
