Init.doc: Creates the table of running cutscenes.

Input.doc: Passes an input event to every running cutscene; returns 1 when one consumed it.

IsPlaying.doc: Returns 1 while any cutscene is playing.

Play.doc: Plays a movie cutscene without freezing the player.

comments.text: waits in 100 ms steps while the cutscene reports IsPlaying

PlayAtPos.doc: Plays a movie cutscene and blocks until it ends. Replaces any running cutscene with the same id.

PlayWithFreeze.doc: Plays a cutscene and freezes the player for its duration.

Remove.doc: Stops and frees the cutscene with the given movie id, if running.

StartPlayWithFreeze.doc: Starts a cutscene with the player frozen and returns the cutscene object without waiting.

StartPlayWithFreezeAtPos.doc: Starts a cutscene at a position and returns its object without waiting.

Stop.doc: Stops the cutscene with the given movie id; returns 1 if one was running.

StopOneScene.doc: Stops one scene of the cutscene with the given movie id; returns 1 if one was running.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame update of all running cutscenes; removes and frees the ones that have ended.

620.name: CutsceneMovies

621.doc: Cutscene player object (dobj: CAMERA) created by CutsceneMovies for one movie: plays the cut list of a movie, drives the cameras, environment takes and events. Only the class header and fields are named in this batch; its methods are in the next batch.

AddEvent.doc: Adds a scripted event to the callback table under key arg1 (key becomes element 0).

AddEventToTable.doc: Appends an event to the list stored in a table under a key (creates the list).

AddFrame.doc: Adds an event to the frame table; key is the take frame at which CutEvent 'frame' triggers it.

comments.text: type 3 = sun, 4 = planet (adds fog), 21 = nebula

CopyObjects.doc: Copies sector objects into the cutscene space (position, rotation, flags, light colour, planet fog or nebula parameters). Stops at the first object owned by the player.

comments.text: switch picks scene+camera pair; the 3rd field (14) = space type 5/2/3/1
galaxy scene flag 4; system scale 1e-5 so the galaxy renders as a far backdrop
galaxy camera flags |= 0x400034, &= ~8

Create.doc: Creates a cutscene player for a mode: 11 = third cut scene, 7 = second cut scene, 8 = second composite scene, otherwise the main cut scene with galaxy and dust scenes plus an environment-map camera. Allocates the table state, a space object and a take, and wires the scenes.

comments.text: frame < 0 means the take is being skipped; only these commands still run
frame: run the event registered for this frame once
callback <id>: run the event registered under id
jump <cut> <variant>: clears the playlist and restarts with another cut
speak <textId> [face key]: speak a line; without arguments uses the pending event -1
endspeak: restore normal time speed
sfx <id> [duration]
startmovie <id> [texture 61] [flags]: plays a movie onto a texture
fadein <ms> [r g b]: fade from colour
fadeout <ms> [r g b]: fade to colour
firelaser <shooter> <target> [weapon] -> event type 1
firemissile <shooter> <target> <missile> -> event type 4
setcollision <obj> <on> -> event type 8
objecteffect <obj> <effect> -> event type 9
killobject <obj> <type> -> event type 10

CutEvent.doc: Receives text commands from the cut take (J3D events) and acts on them: frame, callback, jump, speak, endspeak, sfx, startmusic, startmovie, stopmusic, fadein, fadeout, firelaser, firemissile, setcollision, objecteffect, killobject. Negative frames (take being skipped) only run the commands that must happen anyway.

Destruct.doc: Frees the take, space object, all instances of the dust scene and every cut still in the cut table.

comments.text: main type 4 = planet
background type 1 = stars, 2 = nebula
flag 65536: no extra galaxy light

DoGalaxyTake.doc: Starts the galaxy-backdrop take and fixes up its instances: planets flagged, background star/nebula bodies swapped to the sector's, size 5 000 000, pass and alpha set. Adds a white light unless flag 65536.

DoOverlayTake.doc: Creates the overlay scene, camera and take for the given cut (used for movie screens).

EventAutoFire.doc: Schedules repeated laser fire events from startFrame for duration frames; spacing random in [min, max).

EventCheckObjects.doc: Schedules type-18 object check events at frame 1 for the given path objects.

EventFadeEffect.doc: Schedules per-frame alpha events fading an object linearly from startAlpha to endAlpha over a number of frames; exact end handling for fully visible (>250) or invisible (<10).

comments.text: interval between shots is 8-10 or 11-13 frames

EventFireGroupAtGroup.doc: Schedules random laser fire from every turret of each shooter to random targets of another group over a time span.

EventMakeInvincible.doc: Looks up each object but does nothing (empty loop, dead code).

EventSetInvisibleFromStart.doc: Schedules an alpha-override 2 event at frame 1 so the object starts invisible.

comments.text: event[1] is the event type
type 18: check that a path object exists (result unused)
type 19: start music event[2] with fade event[3]
type 1: fire laser event[2] at event[3] with weapon event[4]
type 11: only fires when the target is in turret range
type 12: shooter fires at the nearest enemy
type 2: create laser object and move it into container slot
type 13: fill all laser slots of the ship; turrets (g.subtype 3 or 4) use laser type 20
type 3: create object (type 9, wares) into container
type 4: shoot missile; guidance bit 4 = swarm of 8, bit 2 slow spacing 250 ms
type 8: collision on/off via object flags 1024 and flags2 1024
type 9: show object effect
type 10: kill object
type 14: speak line {voice, text} with a face; default face by voice id via the table below
speech flags: 16384, +4096 if face given, +131072 and face 1 for mode 1
type 6 deliberately falls through into type 5 after disabling answers
type 5: speak a question from the speaker
type 7: init answer choices of the dialog menu
type 16: set/clear instance flag2 0x8000000
type 15: alpha override on whole instance tree

HandleEvent.doc: Executes one scripted cutscene event {id, type, args...}. Arrays of events are expanded recursively. Types: 1 fire laser, 2 add laser to container, 3 add object, 4 shoot missile (multi-missile volleys for guidance bit 4), 5/6 speak question (6 also disables answers), 7 init answers, 8 set collision, 9 object effect, 10 kill object, 11 fire if in range, 12 fire at nearest enemy, 13 equip lasers, 14 speak with face, 15 alpha override, 16 flag toggle, 18 check object, 19 start music, 20 stop music.

Input.doc: Input filter during a cutscene. Key 752 (skip/Escape) ends the cut (waits for finish if flag 32 is set, silencing speech) and key 800 is swallowed while a menu is open. Returns 1 when consumed.

comments.text: flag 1: hide monitor scenes during the cut
flag 8: composite scene visible
flag 2: galaxy scene on
flag 4: sector scene on
flag 64: dust off
flags 512..16384: copy suns, planets, nebulas, gates, stations, asteroids
take id = cut id + 1000
flag 2097152: movie cut (id 6399); 1048576: movie cut id/10
flag 131072: dust scene on
benchmark hook after one second
flag 16 is the only flag passed to the take in normal cuts (skippable)
pending event type 7 entries are executed at the end
restore music: combat if alert else sector (not while warping)

PlayThread.doc: Main loop of a playback: for each cut in the list shows the scene layers selected by the flag bits, copies sector objects, sets scene parameters, starts the take and waits until it finishes, then resets the layers and moves on. Afterwards cleans up scenes, restores music and the benchmark counters.

ProcessEventTable.doc: Registers every list in the table as frame events (AddFrame).

ResetSceneMovie.doc: Frees the movie in a forked task.

ResetSceneParameters.doc: After a cut: stops the movie that SetSceneParameters started for cuts 6700-6709 (movies 900-909).

comments.text: cut 811 plays movie 841 before the main one; the movie id stored for cleanup is overwritten afterward

SetSceneMovie.doc: Plays a movie onto a texture during a cut. For cut 811 an extra movie 841 is played first. Stops composite effect 3 after playback.

comments.text: speech events: {14, voice id, text id, mode} at the given frame
8100..8310: force a 1024:576 aspect inside the viewport (letterbox)
6004: intro quote - random text 1701:1..68 drawn on texture 19
m22 = 1 turns the dust scene on for this cut (field set by cuts that have dust)
6601: orange fog and the overlay take 6333 (monitor screen movie)
6200: dark green fog and music 6200
6300: with variant 2 plays movies 900..909 in sequence then fades out and stops
6173: twelve type-8 collision events at frame 1
overlay take for the cut (6480/6421/6401/6402/6333 are overlay cut ids)
6225/6230: sequence of type-9 object effect events
6624: EAX room change after 6 s
6399/6400: movie cut flags 2097152 / 1048576 added

SetSceneParameters.doc: Per-cut setup keyed by the cut id: resets fog, flags and aspect, then registers speech events (event type 14: {voice, text id, 1} at a frame), fog, EAX rooms, music, movies or special scene tweaks for the individual story cutscenes (6xxx = intro/story scenes, 8xxx = mission cutscenes).

comments.text: PlayMusicWithFade(track, 2000 ms, 1)

SetSceneParameters2.doc: Second setup stage (called one tick after play start): starts the music fade for cuts 6001 (8301), 6002 (8302), 6003 (8303) and schedules a stop-music event at the end of the cut.

comments.text: a number first means a single cut was passed; wrap it into a list
already playing: replacing the current cut by stopping its take

StartPlay.doc: Starts playing a cutscene list. arg1 may be {cut, flags, events}, {cut, variant, flags, events} or an array of those. Registers the events in the event table and starts PlayThread in a fork (freezing the player when requested), or stops the take if a play is already running.

Stop.doc: Stops the current take. Same code as StopOneScene.

StopGalaxyTake.doc: Frees the galaxy take and its light.

StopOneScene.doc: Stops the current take (the playlist continues with the next cut).

StopOverlayTake.doc: Frees the overlay take, cut, camera and scene.

Vbi.doc: Per frame: copies the cutscene camera rotation and focus onto the galaxy camera and updates the dust scene.

621.name: Camera

622.doc: Game-over sequence handler. Plays the game-over cutscene with music when the player dies, then leaves the game. Used by Client when the player is killed (see PerFrameInput in class 501).

0.doc: 1 while the game-over sequence runs
0.name: gameOverActive

1.doc: J3D take handle stopped on Kill
1.name: takeHandle

comments.text: music track 13 = game over
cutscene/movie player: play scene 11
tells the client to leave the game

GameOver.doc: Switches to the game-over music, plays cutscene 11 and then leaves to the main menu. A forked timer fades to black after 20 seconds if the cutscene is still playing.

GetMode.doc: Returns 1 while the game-over sequence is active.

Kill.doc: Aborts the game-over sequence (called when the player skips it): stops the take, silences music, and leaves the game.

StartGameOver.doc: Marks the sequence active and forks GameOver.

622.name: GameOver

623.doc: Singleton that builds stations and complexes for the player (dobj: BUILD_FACTORY; called as C623.Build and C623.BuildComplex). StartBuild is called by the build menu with the build plan.

0.doc: 1 while a build task runs, 0 idle
0.name: mode

1.doc: object being built, if set
1.name: buildTarget

2.doc: build state, unused in this part
2.name: buildState

comments.text: buildInfo layout: [0..2] x,y,z; [3] sector; [4..6] rotation angles; [7] type code (gtype<<16 | subtype); [8] asteroid (mines only)
gsubtype 5 = mine built on an asteroid
for asteroids of type 17 re-match the factory type to the race default
builder must be in the player's current sector
phase list: 6311 = replace asteroid with mine, 6310 = plain build cutscene
yield only counts if the mine produces the asteroid's resource
m1 holds the current build phase (6310 or 6311)
gtype 5 = dock/station, otherwise a factory class
6311: mine over an asteroid; old asteroid is destroyed and rebuild disabled
achievement ACH_BUILD_FACTORY when a factory (gtype 6) was built
game tip 19 shown after the player owns 3+ stations

Build.doc: Player builds a station, dock or factory (dobj BUILD_FACTORY.Build): runs a cinematic with the builder ship, creates the object from a build-info array and lets the builder fly home. For a mine (gsubtype 5) the target asteroid is destroyed and replaced by the new factory with the asteroid's yield as efficiency.

comments.text: map plain factory subtypes (228-232, 439) to complex hub subtypes (223-227, 440)
2044 = Complex class
collect the factories of a part that is already a complex
first existing complex is reused as the result; the other one is destroyed
failed to connect the factories: discard the new complex
ACH_BUILD_COMPLEX needs 5 or more connected factories

BuildComplex.doc: Joins two player factories into a complex (dobj BUILD_FACTORY.BuildComplex). Maps the basic factory subtype to the complex hub subtype, merges the factories' connections into a class 2044 complex object, then unlocks ACH_BUILD_COMPLEX when at least five factories are connected.

CanBuildComplex.doc: True if two factories may be merged into a complex: distinct player-owned factories, neither in a complex hangar, both with connection points and closer than 500 * global parameter 99 (default 20000).

Finish.doc: Skips the running build cutscene: fades to black and sends input 752 (escape) to the cutscene player.

Kill.doc: Menu-style kill hook: clears the build-mode flag and agrees to be killed.

comments.text: plan[7] is the station ware (main<<16|sub); class 7/8 = complex hubs

StartBuild.doc: Starts a station build. Closes menus, counts statistic 5070 (stations built) and forks BuildComplex for station classes 7 and 8 (complexes) or Build for others. Returns 1 when started.

623.name: BuildFactory

624.doc: XML-driven cutscene (director) object: a set of sequences, shots, cuts, audio and camera tracks with timing nodes. Created by CutsceneManager from addon cutscene XML, activated, then driven by Vbi. Holds its own scene and camera handles. Only part of its methods are in this batch.

0.doc: maximum run time in ms when no dynamic event is used (5000 by default)
0.name: timeoutMs

1.doc: absolute time when Activate was called
1.name: startTime

15.doc: cut instance id -> instance entry, owns cut objects
15.name: cutInstances

19.doc: list of events that can end the cutscene when set
19.name: dynamicEvents

2.doc: cutscene name, default text includes the object id
2.name: name

25.doc: B3D scene of this cutscene, created in Create
25.name: sceneHandle

26.doc: B3D camera of the cutscene, full screen
26.name: cameraHandle

3.doc: key passed to NotifyCutsceneEvent on activate and destruct
3.name: notifyKey

4.doc: bit 1 lock control, 2 lock input, 4 hide menus (SetUIClose)
4.name: lockFlags

6.doc: shot id -> shot table (AddShot)
6.name: shotsById

9.doc: sequence id -> [timing, shot ids, shots, ...] (AddShotSequence)
9.name: sequencesById

comments.text: default timeout 5000 ms when there are no dynamic events
fast forward is stopped when a cutscene starts

Activate.doc: Starts the cutscene: validates the identifiers, prepares the playback list and environments, applies lock flags and hides menus when bit 4 is set. Sets the 5 s timeout unless dynamic events are used.

AddCut.doc: Registers a cut (a cutscene model with its scene and named animations). Returns 1, or nothing if the id is taken.

AddCutAnimRequest.doc: Requests playback of a named animation of a cut instance at a given timing. Returns 0 if the instance or the animation is unknown.

AddCutAnimation.doc: Adds a named animation (first and last frame) to a registered cut. Returns 1 if added.

AddCutInstance.doc: Places an instance of a registered cut on the timeline with start and end timing and an offset source. Returns 0 if the cut is unknown.

comments.text: kinds 0 and 1 fall through to kind 2 after the sector check

AddEnvironment.doc: Registers an environment for a shot. Kind 0 or 1 requires a sector object (2001); kind 2 accepts any object. Returns 1 on success.

AddMovingEntity.doc: Adds a node to the list of moving entities (kinds: 3 camera, 6 cut instance, 9 viewport, 10 and 11 transitions) and updates it once.

AddMusicTrackChange.doc: Registers a music track change node on the timeline. Returns 1 when added.

comments.text: scope prefixes such as Director. are stripped from both names

AddReferenceGroupMember.doc: Adds a named reference to a reference group (group -> reference -> one-member list). Returns 1, or 1 without change if the reference is already in the group.

AddRenderTarget.doc: Registers a rectangle of a texture as a render target for text. Returns 0 if the rectangle is outside the texture or the id is taken.

AddRenderText.doc: Registers a text node that draws a localised text (page and id from texts_L044) into a render target.

AddShot.doc: Adds a shot to a sequence: shot id, timing field and a camera or environment number. Returns 0 when the shot is already in the sequence.

AddShotSequence.doc: Adds an empty sequence with the given id and timing node; returns 1, or nothing if the id exists.

comments.text: timeline node layout is [timing, kind, payload]; kind 0 = sample, 1 = speech, 2 = music track

AddSoundEffect.doc: Registers a sample sound-effect node on the timeline. Returns 1 when added, nothing if the node id is already taken.

comments.text: empty subtitle string is replaced by 0 (no subtitle)

AddSpeech.doc: Registers a speech node: a voice line played through the voice module with an optional subtitle id.

AddTimingDiffNode.doc: Registers a timing node (kind 2) whose value is the difference of two other timing fields.

AddTimingNode.doc: Registers a fixed timing value (kind 0) that other timing fields can refer to by id.

AddTimingSumNode.doc: Registers a timing node (kind 1) whose value is the sum of two other timing fields.

CheckEnvFilter.doc: Returns the filter record of a type-1 environment, creating it on first use (flags, object table). Returns 0 for other environments.

CheckForDynamicWait.doc: Registers a node whose duration is not known yet (negative) in the dynamic wait table m22, so the timeline waits for it.

CheckTableForValidIDs.doc: Checks the keys of one table: no ':' or '@', and no key already in the seen table. Returns 1 if all keys are valid.

Create.doc: Constructor: creates the empty tables, the B3D scene and its full-screen camera, and names the object with its id.

comments.text: copy flags: 1 planets, 2 suns, 4 asteroids, 8 debris, 16 wrecks (probably)
mask 22 includes bits 2 and 4 again, so suns and asteroids are copied twice; wrecks (16) are only copied through this bit (probable bug, check)

CreateCloneEnvironment.doc: Creates a copy of a sector environment: a new sector with the same background and copies of the selected object kinds (planets, suns, asteroids, debris, wrecks). Returns 1 on success.

Destruct.doc: Destructor: notifies the event system, frees cut instances, shots and camera assets, the scene, and releases locks set by lockFlags.

EnvironmentsActivate.doc: Activates the scene of every type 0 and 1 environment, creating and activating its clone environment if the environment has clone flags.

EnvironmentsDeactivate.doc: Deactivates and destroys the scenes of all environments, including their clones.

ExecutePlaybackOp.doc: Runs one playback operation: starts a node (isEnd 0) or stops it (isEnd 1) according to its op type.

FindSequenceContainingShot.doc: Returns the sequence record that contains the given shot id, or 0.

FindShot.doc: Searches all sequences for a shot id and returns its shot record, or 0.

FindShotSequence.doc: Returns the sequence record for a sequence id.

FreeCameraB3DAssets.doc: Frees the cameras and the dust scene of a shot record and clears their slots.

GetCameraDistance.doc: Computes the distance from the shot camera to its reference for a timing, using the camera's distance calculation.

GetCameraFOV.doc: Computes the field of view of the shot camera for a timing, from the reference radius and the camera distance.

GetCloneEnvironment.doc: Returns the clone sector of an environment, or 0 if there is none.

GetEnvironmentSector.doc: Returns the sector of an environment of type 0 or 1, 0 for other types, nothing if the environment is unknown.

GetEnvironmentType.doc: Returns the type of an environment (1 and 0 are the scene types used by EnvironmentsActivate), or -1 if unknown.

GetImpossibleEventID.doc: Returns the placeholder event id @never_occurs for timings that must never fire.

GetLastKnownPos.doc: Returns the last known position of a reference (zero position if never set).

GetLastKnownRadius.doc: Returns the last known radius of a reference, 1 if never set.

GetName.doc: Returns the cutscene name.

GetNodeDuration.doc: Returns the duration of a timeline node in ms, or -1 if it is not known yet. Results are cached in m18 under duration:<id>.

GetNodeEndTime.doc: Returns the absolute end time of a timeline node (start plus duration), or -1 if either is unknown.

comments.text: a shot without its own timing starts after the shots before it in the sequence order

GetNodeStartTime.doc: Returns the absolute start time of a timeline node in ms, or -1 if it is not known yet. Results are cached in m18 under start:<id>.

GetNodeStartTimingField.doc: Returns the raw timing field (timing expression) of a node, looking it up in the sequence, audio, cut, text and transition tables.

GetReferenceCenter.doc: Returns the centre of a reference: for a group, the weighted average of its members' positions; for a single object, its position in the sector. Keeps the last known positions for missing members.

GetReferenceRadius.doc: Returns the radius of a reference: for a group, the largest distance from the centre to a member plus the member's radius.

GetSceneAnchor.doc: Returns the world position of a named anchor (path anchor_<name>) of a cut instance.

GetShotCameraPos.doc: Returns the world position of the shot camera, or {0, 0, 0} if the camera is missing.

GetShotCameraRefRot.doc: Returns the position and rotation of the shot's reference object in its sector. Sets the error flag m5 if the reference is a group name without a single object.

comments.text: visited table: the same timing evaluated twice in one chain means a cycle
kind 1 is A plus B, kind 2 is A minus B

GetTimingValue.doc: Evaluates a timing expression to ms. Accepts a number, start:, end:, duration:, onevent: (time of the event, or -1), timing: nodes (sum and difference). Returns -1 for unknown or cyclic references (the visited table guards against cycles).

GetValidTimingField.doc: Converts a timing value to a timing field string: empty becomes "0", a number becomes its decimal string.

Graphics_AllocCamera.doc: Allocates a cutscene camera in a scene with a priority, full-screen viewport and default position. Returns the camera or 0.

Graphics_AllocInst.doc: Allocates a 3D instance of a body in the cut scene and sets its visibility flag. Returns the instance.

Graphics_AllocScene.doc: Allocates a 3D scene named after the cutscene for an auto-generated part of the cutscene. Returns the scene.

comments.text: no path instances (cut not started): sets the error flag m5 and returns

Graphics_PlayCutAnimation.doc: Plays a named animation on all path instances of a cut instance, using the frame range of the animation.

Graphics_SetCameraFullScreen.doc: Sets a camera viewport to the whole screen (0 to 65535 in both directions).

InsertPlaybackOp.doc: Inserts one playback operation into the queue m19, keeping the queue sorted by time.

InsertPlaybackOpsForTransition.doc: Queues the start (edge 0) or end (edge 1) fade operations of a shot transition, timed relative to the shot's start or end.

InsertPlaybackOpsFromNodeTable.doc: Queues start and end operations of every node in a table, for a given op type. Audio nodes (type 4) get no end operation.

IsDynamicSeqAbortedByEvent.doc: True if the dynamic sequence timing is aborted by the named event.

IsDynamicSeqTiming.doc: True if a timing string is an internal dynamic sequence timing.

IsDynamicShotTriggeredByEvent.doc: True if the dynamic shot timing is triggered by the named event.

IsViewportActive.doc: True if the sequence has an active viewport entry in the moving list (type 9).

MakeDynamicSeqTiming.doc: Builds the internal timing string for a dynamic sequence that starts on the named event.

MakeDynamicShotTiming.doc: Builds the internal timing string for a dynamic shot that starts on the named event.

comments.text: a dotted name (Director.x style) is rejected; the scoping is stripped in SetObjectReference only

MapObjectReference.doc: Resolves a reference name to an object. @playership is the player ship; a name with a dot is not supported and sets the error flag m5.

NodeDurationDependsOnEvent.doc: True if the duration of a node depends on the named event.

NodeStartDependsOnEvent.doc: True if the start of a node depends on the named event.

comments.text: op types used in the queue: 1 sequence viewport, 2 shot, 4 audio, 6 cut instance, 7 cut animation, 8 text, 10 transition in, 11 transition out

PreparePlaybackOplist.doc: Rebuilds the playback queue m19 from all timeline nodes. Each queue entry is [isEnd, nodeId, opType, time], sorted by time.

RemoveMovingEntity.doc: Removes every moving entity matching a node id and kind.

SetDirectorKey.doc: Stores the director key of the cutscene (the key that identifies this cutscene in its XML) and returns 1.

SetEnvironmentFilterFlag.doc: ORs a flag into the object filter of an environment. Returns 0 if the environment has no filter.

SetEnvironmentFilterObject.doc: Marks an object as filtered out for an environment (its key is set in the filter's object table). Returns 0 if the environment has no filter.

SetInputLock.doc: Adds lock flags (1 control, 2 input) to lockFlags.

SetLastKnownPos.doc: Stores the last known position of a reference.

SetLastKnownRadius.doc: Stores the last known radius of a reference.

SetObjectReference.doc: Binds a script reference name (scoping prefix stripped) to an object.

comments.text: record slots: 0 position source, 1 orientation source, 2 reference source, 3 look-at object, 4 distance source, 5 shake source, 6 overlay texture, 7 overlay parameter, 8 camera handles, 9 flags (probably)

SetShotCamera.doc: Stores the camera data of one shot in its record (position, orientation, reference, distance, shake, overlay). Returns 1 on success, 0 if the sequence or shot is unknown.

comments.text: first shot of a fixed sequence needs no blend

SetShotPosMerge.doc: Sets the blend end time and blend curve of a shot so the camera moves smoothly from the previous shot. Does nothing for the first shot of a non-dynamic sequence.

SetShotSequenceViewport.doc: Sets the sequence viewport as two value sources (offset and size, class 660). Returns 1 on success.

comments.text: switch: edge 0 goes to shot slot 3, edge 1 to slot 4; any other value fails

SetShotTransition.doc: Sets the fade transition of one edge of a shot: edge 0 = start, 1 = end. fadeType 1 fades to black, 2 fades to white. Returns 0 for an invalid edge.

SetUIClose.doc: Sets or clears the hide-menus flag (4) in lockFlags.

SpecificNodeDurationDependsOnEvent.doc: Checks the duration timing of one node kind for dependence on an event (same kinds as SpecificNodeStartDependsOnEvent).

comments.text: shot not found in any sequence: unexpected, sets the error flag m5

SpecificNodeStartDependsOnEvent.doc: Checks the start timing of one node kind (1 sequence, 2 shot, 4 audio, 6 cut, 7 cut animation, 8 text) for dependence on an event.

comments.text: speech with a subtitle id (v2[2]) has an empty branch: the subtitle is never shown (possible unfinished code)

StartAudio.doc: Starts an audio node: a sample (type 0), a speech line (type 1, in a fork so it runs in parallel), or a music track change (type 2).

StartCutInstance.doc: Creates the 3D instances of a cut for each model path and records named anchors (paths called anchor_<name>). Adds the instance to the moving list.

StartCutInstanceAnimation.doc: Starts a named animation of a cut instance.

StartSequenceViewport.doc: Starts the viewport of a sequence if the sequence exists.

comments.text: environment flags: bit 1 = no galaxy camera, bit 2 = no dust scene, bit 4 = clear the camera's flag 16 (probably)
camera flag 16 = clear, 4096 and 32768 set for the dust camera; 262144 and 8388608 set on the sector camera

StartShot.doc: Starts a shot: allocates its galaxy, sector and dust cameras (depending on environment flags), applies overlays and the viewport, and queues the shot's end. Sets the sequence's current shot.

comments.text: 129 is the text-block option flags passed to the renderer (probably alignment and wrap)

StartText.doc: Draws a text node into its render target and marks it as a dynamic wait if its duration is not known yet.

StopCutInstance.doc: Frees the 3D instances of a cut instance.

StopShot.doc: Stops a shot: keeps the last camera pose on the sequence, frees the shot's camera assets, removes its moving entries and clears the overlay.

comments.text: -16711423 is the clear colour 0xFF00FF01 (probably a chroma key)

StopText.doc: Clears the render target rectangle of a text node.

StripDirectorScoping.doc: Returns the part of a name after its last dot (removes the Director. style scope prefix).

TimingDependsOnEvent.doc: True if a timing expression depends on the named event: an onevent:<name> spec, or start:, end:, duration: of a node, or a timing node built from those.

comments.text: a dynamic sequence aborted by this event ends now; its fade and ends are scheduled from the event time
viewport not active: the sequence starts at the event instead of the shot

TriggerDynamicEvent.doc: Fires a named event at the current time: records it, then reschedules every sequence, shot, cut, text and transition that depends on it.

comments.text: fallback focus when the computed focus value is not positive

UpdateCamera.doc: Per-frame camera update for one shot: blends position, orientation and distance from the sequence's last pose during the blend, applies shake and focus, updates the dust scene and stores the last pose. Sets the error flag m5 if any value source is missing.

UpdateCloneEnvironments.doc: Keeps the clone sectors in sync with the original: copies the position, rotation, speed and flags of objects in the sector, creates clones for objects entering the sector and self-destructs clones of objects that left it.

UpdateCutInstance.doc: Moves every path instance of a cut instance to its path position plus the instance offset at the given time.

UpdateMovingEntity.doc: Updates one moving entity for the current time by its kind: cut, camera, viewport or transition.

comments.text: opType 10 is the transition-in (slot 3, start edge), anything else is transition-out (slot 4, end edge)
fadeType 1 fades to black (0), type 2 to white (0xFFFFFF)

UpdateShotTransition.doc: Per-frame fade for a shot transition: sets the fade colour and alpha on the shot cameras (alpha falls linearly over the fade time).

UpdateViewport.doc: Applies the viewport of the currently active shot of a sequence.

UpdateViewportExplicit.doc: Sets the viewport and aspect ratio of the shot cameras from the sequence viewport values at the given time (fractions of the screen size).

ValidateIdentifiers.doc: Checks that all object ids of the cutscene are unique across the tables and contain no ':' or '@'. Returns 1 when valid.

comments.text: returns 1 while the cutscene time is before the end time m0

Vbi.doc: Per-frame update of the cutscene. Updates moving entities and cloned environments, runs due playback operations, and returns 1 while the cutscene is still running (before the end time, or with pending operations or dynamic waits).

624.name: Cutscene

625.doc: Registry of the running cutscenes (C624) by name. Starts and stops them from the XML files and hides the game overlay while any is running. Probably the singleton behind the in-game cutscene calls.

0.doc: cutscene name -> Cutscene (C624) object
0.name: activeCutscenes

1.doc: overlay visibility saved when the first cutscene starts
1.name: overlayWasVisible

EnsureInitialized.doc: Creates the cutscene table if it is missing.

GetActiveCutscene.doc: Returns the running cutscene with this name, or nothing.

StartPlayingCutscene.doc: Loads the cutscene from its XML, activates it and hides the overlay. Returns the cutscene object, or 0 if loading or activating failed. Returns nothing when this cutscene is already running.

StopCutscene.doc: Removes and frees a running cutscene; restores the overlay when no cutscene is left.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame update: stops the cutscenes whose Vbi reports that they are done.

625.name: CutsceneManager

626.doc: Loads a cutscene definition from addon/cutscenes/<name>.xml into a cutscene director. Only the first cutscene element is read; it fills the environments, presentation, director key and client options. Returns 1 on success, 0 on any error.

ExtractAlphaBetaRadius.doc: Reads yaw (alpha), pitch (beta) and distance (radius) of a camera node, as value sources with defaults (angles given in degrees, shifted to 16.16). Returns {yaw, pitch, distance}.

ExtractAlphaBetaRadiusNested.doc: Like ExtractAlphaBetaRadius, but supports begin/end child nodes: then returns a two-keyframe source interpolating between two angles-triples; otherwise a single angles source (C671).

ExtractAttributeConst.doc: Returns a constant tuple source (C661) with attribute 'name' transformed by the context, or with the default value if the attribute is missing.

ExtractAttributeNum.doc: Returns the attribute 'name' of a table, or the default if it is missing.

ExtractAttributeObjRel.doc: Returns a relative tuple (C668) for attribute 'name' of a node, relative to a reference object ('size' scale); falls back to a default (arg5 if given, else the default value arg6).

ExtractAttributeRelCoords.doc: Reads x/y/z attributes (with defaults) as three values relative to the reference object's size and returns them as a C668 tuple.

ExtractAttributeStr.doc: Returns the string attribute 'name' of a table, or the default if it is missing.

ExtractBeginEndSubnodes.doc: Returns {beginNode, endNode} if the node has both a 'begin' and an 'end' child, else 0 (or nothing if it has fewer than two children).

ExtractCycleDelay.doc: Returns the 'delay' attribute used for cycling keyframes (default 0).

ExtractCycleMode.doc: Maps the 'cycle' attribute (none/repeat/bounce) to 0/1/2; returns the default if missing or unknown.

ExtractEnvironmentOptions.doc: Builds the environment option bit mask: background black = 1, transparent = 5; nebulaeffect none = 2.

ExtractInterpolation.doc: Maps the 'interpolation' attribute (none/linear/smooth) to 0/1/2; returns the default if missing or unknown.

comments.text: class 661 = constant tuple: evaluate once and free it, store as a constant keyframe

ExtractKeyframeSet.doc: Finds a child named 'name' and builds a keyframed value source (class 662) from its 'keyframe' children, with cycle mode and interpolation. Constant tuples are evaluated immediately; other sources are kept as live sources. Returns 0 on error or if not found.

ExtractNamedSubnode.doc: Returns the first child of 'node' whose tag name equals 'name', or 0.

ExtractNestedCoordOffset.doc: Camera position offset for camera_panto: reads x/y/z (or begin/end nodes) relative to the reference; when absent a random offset (about +-190..340, +-160..270, 1400..1500) is used. Returns a (possibly keyframed) position source oriented to the reference.

ExtractNestedNum.doc: Reads a number from attribute 'attr1' of the node itself, else from attribute 'attr2' of its child named 'childName'; returns the default if neither exists.

ExtractObjRelNested.doc: Reads an object-relative distance-like value either from begin/end child nodes (keyframed over time) or from a single value source / attribute.

ExtractTupleValueSource.doc: Builds a tuple source from 'value' children: if all use 'exact' it is a constant tuple (C661), otherwise a mixed tuple (C668) of exact and relative (percentage of scaleref/scaleinfo) values.

ExtractValuesource.doc: Finds the child 'name' of a node and converts its first sub-element into a value source object; returns 0 if absent.

comments.text: offset: base source plus adjust source (sum)
orbit: center (default origin), distance, elevation, start/stop angle (default 0..360), required 'time'
reference: object position (optionally with x/y/z offset in scale units) oriented in ecliptic/object space
angles: yaw/pitch/distance triple, default distance 10000
autozoom: needs sequence and shot names in context
peek_camerapos: reads the current camera position of the shot

ExtractValuesourceInner.doc: Converts the first child element of a node into a value source object (classes 660..677) depending on its tag: value, keyframes, offset, orbit, reference, transform_relative, bias_relative, anchor, angles, static, autozoom, autodistance, peek_camerapos, make_camangles.

GenerateLockedOrientedAngles.doc: Random angles as above, but oriented in the object's frame and held static (used while locking on in camera_find).

GenerateRandomAngles.doc: Random look angles for camera_find: random yaw, pitch 60 minus random, and a distance up to 20% below the given one relative to the object size. Returns an angles source (C671).

GetAutoBeginEndTiming.doc: Returns the end time for begin/end keyframes: the 'time' attribute, otherwise the shot's duration from the cutscene, otherwise the given default.

InvalidNode.doc: Called for unknown XML nodes; empty in the release build (error reporting removed).

comments.text: instantiate_cut: position is a value source (keyframes, reference, ...)
render_text: text is page/line from the text files, drawn onto a render target

LoadActions.doc: Parses the 'actions' section: cut instances and animations, rendered text, shot sequences (static and dynamic), sound effects, music track changes and speech lines. Each is registered on the cutscene object.

comments.text: context flags: 61440 = angles in degrees->fixed, 61441 = value<<16, 61442 = divide by 360, 61443 = keyframes use interpolation options
camCtx slots 3/4/5 = default interpolation, cycle mode, cycle delay
camera_orbit: camera circles the reference object at distance/elevation between start and stop angle
camera_flyby: linear offset past the object, with distance and elevation
camera_panover: pans along the side of an object; 'showing' picks the object face, 'pan_direction' the movement
pan axes (v52..v54) are chosen from the shown side so pan is perpendicular to the viewing axis; v55 swaps start/end to reverse direction
camera_follow: position follows alpha/beta/radius around the object
camera_lookat: fixed point (or alpha/beta/radius) looking at lookat_reference
camera_panto: look first at reference, then pan to panto_reference
camera_flyto: fly toward the object until it fills 'fillspace' percent of the view
camera_flyfromto: start at one object, fly to another, then look at the second
camera_find: random searching look angles for 'time_search' ms, then locks on the target with decreasing jitter (time_lockon)
auto zoom from fillspace attributes (plain or begin/end nodes)
defaults when nothing was specified
final call: position, roll, look, zoom, shaking, overlay texture/tile, reference object, banking

LoadCamera.doc: Builds all value sources of a shot camera (position, roll, look direction, zoom, shaking) from a 'camera' / 'camera_<mode>' node and passes them to the cutscene (SetShotCamera). Modes: orbit, flyby, panover, follow, lookat, panto, flyto, flyfromto, find. Missing sources are defaulted (position 0, look angles {13568,0}, roll 0, zoom 2500).

LoadClientOptions.doc: Parses the cutscene's client options: 'menus' attribute (close = menus are closed during the cutscene) and 'input' lock level (none/control/input/all => 0..3).

comments.text: source may be a numeric id or a name; names are resolved with B3D_GetCutID

LoadCutList.doc: Parses the 'cuts' section: each 'cut' refers to a B3D cut (by name or numeric id) and may contain named 'animation' ranges.

comments.text: the file path is always addon/cutscenes/<name>.xml
newlines, carriage returns and tabs are stripped before parsing

LoadCutsceneXML.doc: Reads and parses the cutscene XML file of the given name and applies it to the director object (name, UI-close flag, director key, environments, presentation and client options). Returns 0 if the file or the cutscene element is missing or any section fails.

LoadDynamicSequence.doc: Like LoadSequence, but for 'dynamicshots': the sequence ends on an event ('endevent', default impossible event) and each shot starts on a trigger event instead of a fixed time.

comments.text: pass 1: resolve 'find_sector' nodes (galaxy map x/y) into named sectors
the sector the player is currently in is always available as '@playersector'
environment_explicit: builds a throw-away sector object (100x100) with its own background
size attribute is in units of 500 (default 20000)
environment_implicit: reuses an already existing sector by name
scenery filter bit flags: planets=1, suns=2, asteroids=4, debris=8, wrecks=22 (22 is odd: it is 2+4+16, not a single bit; probably a bug or a composite mask)
character_display: environment type 2 shows a character face instead of a 3D scene

LoadEnvironments.doc: Parses the environment nodes of a cutscene XML: first collects 'find_sector' nodes into a name->sector table, then registers explicit/implicit environments, character displays and object groups on the cutscene object. Returns 1 on success, 0 on any error.

comments.text: distribute the leftover percentage evenly over members without a weight (-1)

LoadObjectGroup.doc: Parses an 'object_group' node: each child has an object and an optional percentage weight (1..100). Unweighted members share the remaining percentage equally; weights must not exceed 100 in total. Registers every member on the cutscene as a reference group member.

LoadPresentation.doc: Dispatches the sub-sections of a cutscene 'presentation' node: cuts, rendertargets, timings and actions.

LoadRenderTargetList.doc: Parses the 'rendertargets' section: each target maps a named texture (name or id) to a rectangle (x, y, width, height).

comments.text: context slot 1 = sequence name
context slot 2 = shot name

LoadSequence.doc: Parses a timed 'sequence' (shot sequence): creates the sequence on the cutscene, then its viewport and its shots. Each shot gets a copy of the context carrying its name.

comments.text: any node named 'camera' or 'camera_*'
transition type: cut=0, fadeblack=1, fadewhite=2; crossfade is not supported (returns 0)
no camera: only allowed for environment type 2 (character display)

LoadShotInternals.doc: Parses the children of a 'shot': camera nodes, transition_in/transition_out (cut, fadeblack, fadewhite) and takeover_position (blend from the previous shot's position). A shot without a camera is only valid if its environment is a character display (type 2).

LoadTimings.doc: Parses the 'timings' section: 'timing' nodes become plain, sum (offset_add) or difference (offset_subtract) timing nodes on the cutscene.

LoadViewport.doc: Parses the 'viewport' of a sequence (position and size value sources) and sets it on the cutscene. Fails (0) if either is missing.

MakeRelativeTuple.doc: Creates a relative-value tuple source (C668) from a list of values, each relative to a reference object and a scale kind (e.g. 'size').

OrientValuesource.doc: Wraps a value source so it is expressed in the reference object's frame: 'ecliptic' => C674 (bias relative), 'object' => C669 (transform relative); otherwise unchanged.

SetKeyframeOptionsFromContext.doc: Applies cycle mode / delay (context slots 4 and 5) and, if flag 61443 is set, interpolation options to a keyframe source.

TransformValueInContext.doc: Converts an angle-like number according to context flags: 61440 degrees to fixed angle units, 61441 shift left 16, 61442 divide by 360.

626.name: CutsceneLoader

627.doc: Small helper that animates 3D interface instances over time: linear position moves and alpha fades. Entries are kept per instance and advanced every frame by Vbi; tasks waiting for an animation to end are woken by interrupt. Initialised at startup and ticked from the main loop.

0.doc: inst -> {startTime, duration, from xyz, to xyz}
0.name: moveAnims

1.doc: inst -> {startTime, duration, fromAlpha, toAlpha}
1.name: fadeAnims

FinishAnims.doc: Completes both animations at once by jumping to the end values.

Init.doc: Clears the animation tables.

StartFadeInst.doc: Fades the alpha override of an instance to the target (1..255) over a duration in ms. Invalid current/target values count as 255.

StartFadeInstWithSpeed.doc: Fade with a rate in alpha units per second.

StartMoveInst.doc: Starts moving an instance to a target position {x, y[, z]} over a duration in ms. A zero duration moves it at once.

StartMoveInstWithSpeed.doc: Like StartMoveInst but takes a speed (units per second); the duration is distance*1000/speed.

StopAnims.doc: Cancels both animations of the instance, leaving it where it is.

comments.text: negative elapsed time (timer wrap) or finished: snap to the end value
linear interpolation from start to end over the duration

Vbi.doc: Per-frame update: interpolates positions and alpha linearly with real time; finished or time-wrapped entries are snapped to the end value and removed.

WaitForAnimsEnd.doc: Blocks the calling task until no move or fade is left for the instance.

627.name: InstAnimator

630.doc: Modal message box with a text block and one or more buttons, drawn into its own 3D scene. Opened by menus and other code via Open/ShowMessage; the result (the pressed button value) is sent to the notify object's NotifyMsgBoxReturn(requestId, result).

0.doc: 3D scene handle of the box
0.name: scene

1.doc: camera handle in the scene
1.name: camera

10.doc: icon id drawn in the title bar
10.name: titleIcon

11.doc: message text wrapped into lines
11.name: textLines

12.doc: x offset of the centred text block
12.name: textX

13.doc: array of [value, label, x, y, width] per button
13.name: buttons

14.doc: result value returned when the box is aborted
14.name: abortResult

15.doc: object that receives NotifyMsgBoxReturn
15.name: notifyObject

16.doc: caller-defined id passed back to the notify object
16.name: requestId

17.doc: index of the highlighted button
17.name: selectedButton

18.doc: 1 while the mouse is over the close button
18.name: closeHover

2.doc: instance showing the messagebox body; 0 when closed
2.name: boxInst

3.doc: left screen position
3.name: screenX

4.doc: top screen position
4.name: screenY

5.doc: box width in pixels
5.name: width

6.doc: box height in pixels
6.name: height

7.doc: x of the title-bar close button, relative to the box
7.name: closeButtonX

8.doc: y of the close button (5)
8.name: closeButtonY

9.doc: window title text
9.name: title

CheckMouseHotSpot.doc: Hit test: returns -3 close button, button index, -2 inside box but no button, -1 outside.

Close.doc: Frees all graphics, plays close sample 954 and calls NotifyMsgBoxReturn on the notify object with the chosen value; then interrupts waiters.

GetCursorIcon.doc: Cursor icon id (1100) while over the box.

GetNotifyObject.doc: Notify object of the open box, else 0.

GetRequest.doc: Request id of the open box, else 0.

comments.text: 752 esc action, 800 kill menus, 753 select action, 758-761 scroll keys

Input.doc: Keyboard handling: ESC/kill-menus (752, 800) abort, select (753) confirms, scroll left/up and right/down (758/760, 759/761) move the highlight. Returns 2 when handled.

IsOpen.doc: True while the box is shown.

comments.text: ignore clicks whose flags carry bits 0x6000 (wheel/other)

NotifyClick.doc: Mouse click: left button on a button closes with its value, on the close button aborts. Always swallows the click.

NotifyMouseMove.doc: Updates close-button hover and highlighted button, playing sample 957 on change.

comments.text: no button selected: fall back to OK

Open.doc: Opens a box with standard buttons chosen by a bit mask: 1 yes, 2 no, 4 ok, 8 a custom label (35:4270). Result value = the bit of the pressed button.

comments.text: wrap the text to 492 px
buttons are centred; each is label width + 40 wide with 12 px gaps
body gfx effects/menugfx/GUI/messagebox
sample 953 = open sound
listen to input (priority 90)

OpenCustom.doc: Opens a box with arbitrary buttons. Measures the text and labels, sizes the window (256..512 wide, max 256 high, text truncated with '...'), allocates scene, camera and body instance, and registers as input listener. Closes sidebar and context menus first. Returns 1 on success.

ShowMessage.doc: Shows an OK-only message in a fork. Unless force is set it waits until a previous box is closed.

Update.doc: Redraws window frame, close button, text lines and buttons into texture 7.

630.name: MessageBox

631.doc: Game tip / help popup system. Keeps a bit set of tips already shown (ids 1..999), queues texts and shows them one after another in a small window next to the comm window, optionally blinking the matching sidebar button.

0.doc: 32-word bit set, one bit per shown tip id
0.name: shownTips

1.doc: pending triples [text, delay ms, sidebar actions]
1.name: tipQueue

2.doc: 1 while the display fork is running
2.name: showing

3.doc: 3D scene of the tip window
3.name: scene

4.doc: camera in the tip scene
4.name: camera

5.doc: instance with the gametip body
5.name: windowInst

DisplayGameTip.doc: Shows tip text 2600:<id> once. Returns 1 if shown, 0 if the text does not exist, nothing if already shown.

DisplayKeyHelp.doc: Shows a one-line help (1903:10000+id) prefixed with the key currently bound to the command.

comments.text: wait with real time (not game time) so pause does not matter
fade the window out over 500 ms

DisplayText.doc: Shows a tip text for a duration (computed from length if <=0). Parses $...$ codes; if a tip is already showing the text is queued, otherwise a fork displays it and then drains the queue.

GameTipDisplayed.doc: Non-zero if tip id (1..999) was already shown.

GetTextDelay.doc: Display time for a text, clamped to 4000..10000 ms.

GetVKLookupTable.doc: Table from VK_ names to virtual command ids.

Init.doc: Allocates the shown-tips bit set and an empty queue.

IsWindowOpen.doc: True while the tip window exists.

comments.text: VK_SIDEBAR (648) falls back to key 431 if it maps to itself

ParseKeyCodes.doc: Replaces $VK_xxx$ tokens with the name of the key currently bound to that command; unknown tokens become '(invalid)'.

ParseTipCodes.doc: Replaces $...$ markers in a tip: $PERSONAL:$ $NAVIGATION:$ $TARGET:$ $STATION:$ $OPTIONS:$ are removed and add sidebar action codes to the output list; $COMM$ $TRADE$ $PERSONAL$ $ADVANCED$ $EXPORTSTATS$ $UNIVERSEMAP$ $CLAIM$ $MYMISSIONS$ $MYSTATUS$ are replaced by the highlighted localized menu names.

ResetGameTip.doc: Clears the shown flag of a tip.

comments.text: 88 = 'X' escape (default colour); later lines inherit the last colour escape of the previous one

ShowWindow.doc: Creates scene/camera/instance for the tip window and renders the text with the black pearl template, tracking colour escapes across lines.

StartTipActions.doc: Blinks the sidebar buttons named by tip action codes (101,102,103,105,106,111).

comments.text: comm window visible: shift 232 px down, minimised monitor: 62 px

UpdateInstPosition.doc: Places the window at the right screen edge; moves it down if the comm window is visible or the monitor 2 is shown/minimised.

631.name: GameTips

632.doc: On-screen message box for short game messages, such as autopilot refusals, missile target errors and illegal scan notices. Shown with Show(text, duration) and hidden with Hide, from many places in the scripts. Texts come from page 35 (for example 4602: 'Too close to station for autopilot command.') and page 1904. dobj name unknown.

2.doc: non-zero while the message is on screen (probably)
2.name: shown

Hide.doc: Frees the box scene, its camera and icon instance, and clears the text. Does nothing if the box is not shown.

IsShown.doc: True while the message box is on screen.

comments.text: Layout: left margin 64 px with an icon, 10 px without. Box width starts at 512 px and shrinks to the widest line.
Word-wrap the text to 512 minus both margins. 129 is the font id.
Shrink the box to the widest wrapped line plus margins.
Box is placed 150 px above the bottom of the screen, centred horizontally.
Auto-hide after 5 s. m13 is a serial counter: a newer Show() call invalidates this timer.

Show.doc: Shows the info box with a text (array of lines or a text id in arg1). arg2 is an icon id, 0 for none; an icon moves the text to a 64 px left margin. Hides any box already shown, does nothing when the player ship is killed, and schedules an auto-hide after 5 s.

comments.text: Hide only if no newer Show() happened during the fade.

StartFadeOut.doc: Starts a 1 s fade-out of the shown box and hides it when the fade ends. Does nothing if the box is hidden or already fading. A newer Show() call cancels the pending hide.

comments.text: Single-line text starts at y=15, several lines at y=10; each line steps 22 px.
A line that follows a colour code is prefixed with ESC plus the colour byte; default colour is 88.
Text colour -2960686 (default). Drawn into texture 6.

Update.doc: Redraws the box texture: the icon (if any) and each text line. Lines can change colour with ESC + character codes; the colour carries over to the next line.

632.name: ScreenMessage

640.doc: The vertical button bar on the right edge of the cockpit HUD: the main game entry points (personal, ship, navigation, target, dock, messages, options, save and load). It is opened and closed by the HUD, and its buttons open ContextMenu lists (C641). Its frame instance is registered with INS_SetSidebarInstance.

0.doc: scene handle of the bar, 0 when the bar is destroyed
0.name: scene

1.doc: camera handle inside the bar scene
1.name: camera

10.doc: number of kind 1 buttons
10.name: stackedButtonCount

11.doc: number of buttons currently blinking
11.name: blinkingButtonCount

12.doc: 1 when the bar is navigated by keyboard or was activated by script
12.name: keyboardMode

13.doc: index of the selected button, -1 for none
13.name: activeButton

14.doc: index of the button under the pointer, -1 for none
14.name: hoverButton

15.doc: real time the pointer started hovering the current button
15.name: hoverStart

16.doc: cache tag for the savegame list, reset by ResetSavegameCache
16.name: savegameCache

2.doc: frame instance of the bar, slides in and out on X
2.name: frameInstance

3.doc: screen height in pixels, refreshed every Update
3.name: screenHeight

4.doc: 0 closed, 1 closing, 2 opening, 3 open
4.name: state

5.doc: button ids in display order
5.name: buttonIds

6.doc: per button: 0 top column, 1 stacked above the bottom, 2 bottom
6.name: buttonKinds

7.doc: icon index per button, used for the drawing row
7.name: buttonIcons

8.doc: per button: 1 disabled, 2 hovered, 4 selected, 8 blinking
8.name: buttonFlags

9.doc: number of kind 0 buttons
9.name: topButtonCount

comments.text: Selecting a different button closes the open context list; the same stacked button keeps it open.

ActivateButton.doc: Selects a sidebar button by id and opens its context list. Opens the bar first if needed. Enabled buttons only; the button's OnButtonSelect runs when the list is already open for it.

ActivateButtonAndContextmenu.doc: Activates a sidebar button and, when its context list is open, activates an entry in that list.

AddButton.doc: Appends one button to the list and counts it by kind.

comments.text: defaultSlot = first empty slot for saving / newest save for loading
slots >= 10 are labelled with 1904:1007 (autosave)

AddSaveLoadEntries.doc: Adds the save (809) or load (810) slot entries as submenu buttons. Save has 10 slots; load additionally has autosave slots after a separator. Highlights the first free slot (save) or the newest save (load).

Animate.doc: Slides the frame instance to the given X at 212 units per second and waits until the move ends.

comments.text: Pointer X is measured from the bar's X position plus 32 px.
Top column buttons: 51 px high rows starting at y 34, x 9 to 53.
Stacked buttons: x 10 to 38, 32 px high, stacked from the bottom upward.

CheckMouseHotSpot.doc: Hit test for the bar. Returns 100 plus button index on a button, 2 inside the bar, 3 on the left edge strip, 0 outside.

comments.text: Release the 53 px left overlay offset reserved on open.

Close.doc: Starts the closing slide: the bar moves out to X -21 and is then killed. Closes any open context menu and releases the left overlay offset.

comments.text: Background: 38 px wide strip, full screen height.
Blinking buttons switch to state 3 for half of each second.
Top column icons: 44 px cells, source row 2 + 46 * icon index. Stacked icons: 28 x 32 cells, source row 284 + 40 * (icon index - 6).

DrawSideBar.doc: Draws the bar into its texture: the background tiles, the top column and stacked buttons with their state colours, the icons and the blinking pulse.

GetCursorIcon.doc: Shows the tooltip for the hovered button and returns the cursor icon id: 1100 over the bar, 0 otherwise.

comments.text: main type 17 whose parent is main type 28: use the parent

GetTarget.doc: Returns the object currently tracked by the active monitor (the sidebar 'Target' entry). If the tracked thing is a type-17 child of a type-28 object, the parent is used instead; returns the event object of it, or 0.

comments.text: Hidden while long-term steering is on and the active monitor does not follow steering.

GetVisibility.doc: Returns 1 when the bar should be visible: an active button, a pending message, or an overlay visible with the cursor shown. Returns nothing otherwise and while warping or killed.

GetXPos.doc: Current X position of the bar, or nothing when the frame instance does not exist.

comments.text: Button order: 101, 103, 102, 105, 106 (top column), 108, 109, 110 (stacked), 111 (bottom, save and load menu).

InitButtons.doc: Rebuilds the button list in a fixed order: 101 to 106 top column, 108 to 110 stacked above the bottom, 111 bottom. Kinds and icon rows are set per button.

comments.text: Cancel while docked: from button 108 go to 111 (save and load), otherwise select 108 (leave station).
Cancel from the leave button selects button 111.
Keyboard move: the new button's list opens (OnButtonSelect with mode 0).
Other keys while docked are hotkeys of the context menu (C641 hotkey map).

Input.doc: Handles one keyboard event for the bar. Returns 2 when the event is consumed. Cancel leaves the bar or activates the leave button; up and down move between enabled buttons, wrapping around; hotkeys of the open context menu work while docked.

comments.text: kind 0 and kind 1 are counted separately (m9, m10); the meaning of the two kinds is not verified

InsertButton.doc: Inserts a button at index into the parallel arrays m5..m8 (button id, kind, data, value 0). Kinds 0 and 1 are also counted in m9 and m10.

IsActive.doc: True when a button is selected.

IsBlocked.doc: True while the cockpit blocking screen C630 is open. Blocked buttons cannot be used.

IsOpen.doc: True while the bar is open (state 2 or 3).

Kill.doc: Closes the bar and frees its scene, camera and frame instance, and clears the cockpit's sidebar reference.

comments.text: Clicks with flag bits 0x6000 are ignored (probably release or wheel events).

NotifyClick.doc: Mouse click on the bar. A button click selects it and opens its list. A click elsewhere closes any open context menu. Returns 1 when the click is consumed.

comments.text: Pointer on the edge strip with no context menu open: stop the bar.

SetButtonBlink.doc: Turns the blink flag (8) of a sidebar button on or off. Opens the bar first when turning it on.

SetKeyboardMode.doc: Sets the keyboard mode flag of the bar.

StartLoad.doc: Forks the actual game load for the given slot.

ActivateButton.doc: Highlights the button with the given id and, if invoke is set and the menu is still open, selects it. Does nothing for disabled or unknown buttons.

AddButton.doc: Appends a button to a menu that is being built. The button is marked blinking if a matching blink request exists. hotkey (virtual key) is also mapped in the hotkey table.

AddButtonToSubMenu.doc: Adds a button to the sub-menu of parentButton. With no parent (arg1 0) it adds to this menu. Hotkeys of sub-menu entries map to {parent, button}.

AddDefaultInfoLine.doc: Adds an info line pair (label, value) for the no-selection info or for the button being refreshed. Forwarded to the sub-menu object when this menu is not building.

AddDefaultInfoLineToSubMenu.doc: Adds an info line pair to the sub-menu of the given parent button, or to this menu when no parent is given.

AddInfoLine.doc: Adds an info line pair for the button being refreshed. Forwarded to the sub-menu object when this menu is not refreshing.

AddSeparator.doc: Adds a separator line below the last button. Does nothing if the menu has no buttons or the separator is already there.

AddSeparatorToSubMenu.doc: Adds a separator to the sub-menu of the given parent button, or to this menu when no parent is given.

AddSubMenuDef.doc: Stores one sub-menu entry for a button. kind: 0 button, 1 separator, 2 info line, 3 default button. Marks the button with flag 4 (has sub-menu).

AddWeaponMenuButton.doc: Adds a button to a weapon menu and flags it as a weapon sub-menu entry (flag 32).

comments.text: Hit test uses the frame box. A sidebar with no active button shifts x by 20 px.
Frame box: from originX minus bodyOffsetX to originX plus width plus 3, vertically from originY (minus header) to originY plus height plus 3.

CheckMouseHotSpot.doc: Hit test for the mouse. Returns 0 outside the menu, 1 inside the frame but not on a button, or 100 plus button index on a button row.

CheckOtherMenu.doc: True when the open sub-menu is under the given point.

ClearObject.doc: Drops the owner reference so that no callback reaches it when the menu closes.

comments.text: A sub-menu (642) is closed first, then this menu.

Close.doc: Closes the menu and frees its scene, camera and frame instance. The sub-menu closes first. Calls the common close path.

comments.text: Fade-out: the texture around the active row is cleared; the row itself stays and fades out.
After the fade, Kill frees the scene if the menu is still fading.

CloseWithFade.doc: Closes the menu with a 300 ms fade that keeps only the highlighted row visible. Falls back to Close when no button is active.

comments.text: Blinking buttons (flag 8) swap between states on odd and even game age.
Button state colour: 0 disabled, 1 normal, 2 highlighted.
Weapon menu: request 20 to 31 lists ship lasers (ids 20000 and up), request 10 lists missiles (ids 21000 and up).
Enabled buttons use the coloured icon 449 px to the left of the greyed one.
Laser flag 64 in the FlyFX field: draw the laser's ammunition icon.
Laser stats: damage per second is damage times 1000 over reload time (1000 ms if unknown).
Missile speed and range are divided by 500 for display.

DrawContextMenu.doc: Draws the whole menu into its texture: frame, optional header, every button row with its state colour, icons, hotkeys and sub-menu arrow, and the info panel. Weapon rows show laser or missile stats.

FindBlinkRequest.doc: Returns the index in the blink list of the entry with the given owner, request and button id, or -1.

FindButtonIndexByID.doc: Returns the index of the button with the given id, searching from the last one, or -1 when it is not in the menu.

GetActiveButton.doc: Returns the highlighted button index, -1 for none.

GetBodyName.doc: Body name of the menu frame model.

GetButtonID.doc: Returns the button id at an index, or nothing when the index is out of range.

comments.text: Label area: 248 px when the menu has no set width, minus 28 px for the icon and 2 px padding.
The double angle quote marks buttons with a sub-menu.
Label too wide: the hotkey text is shortened first, then the label.

GetButtonLabelData.doc: Lays out one button row: returns a 9-entry array with the row width, label x offset, clipped label, hotkey text, hotkey-has-modifier flag and x offsets for drawing the hotkey, the sub-menu arrow and the icon.

GetButtonOffset.doc: Y offset of a button row inside the menu: 2 px top padding, rowHeight per row, 5 px per separator above.

GetCameraPriority.doc: Camera priority of the menu scene: 99 for the sidebar, 180 otherwise.

GetCurrentInfoLines.doc: Returns the info lines for the highlighted button, or the no-selection info when no button has info.

GetCursorIcon.doc: Returns the cursor icon id for a point: 1100 over the menu, 0 otherwise.

GetHotKeys.doc: Returns the hotkey table: key code to button id, or {buttonId, subButtonId}.

GetMaterialID.doc: Texture id used to draw the menu (10).

comments.text: Each info line adds 15 px to the info panel height.

GetMaxHeight.doc: Full height needed by the menu: rows, separators and info panel. Info-only menus drop 10 px.

comments.text: Weapon menus: 64 px icon area plus label width, at least 220 px. Normal menus: 30 px plus label width.
Info-only menus (info lines but no buttons) are 16 px narrower.

GetMaxWidth.doc: Width of the widest button or info line, clamped by the caller to 248 px. Weapon menus use a minimum of 220 px.

GetMousePriority.doc: Mouse listener priority of the menu (80).

GetObject.doc: Returns the owner object while the menu is open, else 0.

GetParentWidth.doc: Width of the parent menu, 0 here. Sub-menus override it.

GetRequest.doc: Returns the request id of the menu.

comments.text: An open sub-menu gets the event first.
With no active button, any key except cancel (752) closes the menu.
Cancel: when the player is docked, the sidebar's leave button 108 is activated. Otherwise the menu closes.
Docked sidebar with no other menu open: cancel selects sidebar button 108 (leave station, see C640).
Moving the highlight closes an open sub-menu first.
Hotkey table value: a button id, or {buttonId, subButtonId} to activate both.

Input.doc: Handles one keyboard event. Returns 2 when the event is consumed. Keys: 752 cancel, 760 leave the list, 761 select the active button, 753 confirm, 758 and 759 previous and next button, 762 and 763 first and last button, 766 and 767 ignored, other keys use the hotkey table.

IsDocked.doc: True when the sidebar menu (type 1) is open.

IsInMenu.doc: True for in-menu (4) and dropdown (5) menus.

IsKeyboardMode.doc: True when the menu is open and uses keyboard navigation.

IsOpen.doc: True in the open state (2) or while info is refreshed (4).

KeepAlive.doc: Resets the mouse-out timer while the menu is open and the timer is running.

Kill.doc: Frees the menu without animation when it is fading out; otherwise closes it normally.

comments.text: Clicks with flag bits 0x6000 are ignored (probably release or wheel events).

NotifyClick.doc: Mouse click. Clicking outside closes the menu unless another menu takes it. Clicking a button selects it; a sub-menu button opens its sub-menu. Returns 1 when the click was consumed.

comments.text: Pointer left the buttons: start the mouse-out timer, unless in keyboard mode or hovering the parent button of a sub-menu.
A sub-menu keeps its parent button highlighted while the pointer is in it.

NotifyMouseMove.doc: Mouse move. Moves the highlight to the button under the pointer, starts the sub-menu hover timer and the 500 ms mouse-out timer. Returns 1 when the menu consumes the move, 0 for sub-menus.

comments.text: Opens the sub-menu 642 at the right edge of this menu, level with the button row.
Request 111 (the sidebar button 111, save and load) with button 809 (save): if saving is not possible, play voice 13:43.
Plain button: clear both sub-menus, fade this menu, then report the choice to the owner.

OnButtonSelect.doc: Selects the highlighted button. A button with a sub-menu opens it (or its default entry if already open). A plain button closes the menu with a fade and reports the choice to the owner as OnContextMenuReturn(requestId, buttonId).

OnContextMenuReturn.doc: Empty default. The owner overrides it to receive the chosen button id.

OnContextMenuUpdate.doc: Empty default. The owner overrides it to refill a button before drawing (call SetButtonText, SetButtonDisabled, AddInfoLine).

OnContextMenuUpdateInfo.doc: Empty default. The owner overrides it to fill the no-selection info lines.

Prepare.doc: Opens a generic menu at screen position. inMenu selects the in-menu type (4) instead of generic (0). The first button is highlighted.

PrepareForDropdown.doc: Prepares a dropdown menu (type 5) at screen position. Keyboard mode is on and the first button is highlighted.

comments.text: Any key switches the menu to keyboard mode. The sidebar also switches C640 to keyboard mode.
Only up and down keys (758, 759) repeat. Other keys are handled once.
Repeat delay from C2200.GetRepeatDelay, initial delay from C2200.GetInitialDelay.

PrepareForInput.doc: Filters key input before a key is handled. Turns keyboard mode on when needed, and applies a key repeat delay to up and down keys. Returns 1 when the key should be handled, 0 when it is throttled.

PrepareForSidebar.doc: Prepares the sidebar menu (type 1) that the sidebar menu bar C640 uses. Keyboard mode is inherited from C640.

SetActiveButton.doc: Highlights the button at an index and resets the hover timer when the index changes.

SetButtonBlink.doc: Adds or removes a blink request for a button of the menu of the given owner and request. If that menu is open, the button's blink flag (8) is updated at once.

SetButtonDisabled.doc: Disables the button being refreshed (flag 1). Forwarded to the sub-menu object when this menu is not refreshing.

SetButtonText.doc: Sets the label of the button being refreshed. Forwarded to the sub-menu object when this menu is not refreshing.

SetDefaultButton.doc: Sets the default button by id. The default is highlighted when the menu is building.

SetDefaultButtonInSubMenu.doc: Sets the default button of the sub-menu of the given parent button, or of this menu when no parent is given.

SetKeyboardMode.doc: Turns keyboard navigation on or off and passes the change to the sub-menu.

comments.text: Nothing to show: no buttons and no info lines for the no-selection state.
Mouse events go to this menu (listener priority from GetMousePriority). Follow-steering is turned off while open.
Refresh the buttons once, then return whether the open state was reached.

Show.doc: Opens a prepared menu: allocates its scene and camera, switches it to the open state and registers it as a mouse listener. Returns IsOpen. An empty menu with no info lines is not shown.

StartNoSaveVoice.doc: Plays the voice line saying that saving is only possible in stations or with salvage insurance (text 13:43).

StartNotInDemoVoice.doc: Plays the voice line saying the feature is not functional in the playable demo (text 13:1310).

comments.text: Mouse has been away for more than 500 ms: close the menu.
Owner refills each button in turn. m30 holds the index being refreshed.
Owner gets OnContextMenuUpdateInfo with the selected button id (parent id for a sub-menu).
Highlighted button disabled: move to the next enabled one.
Hover over a sub-menu button for 750 ms opens its sub-menu.
Sidebar with no highlighted button is drawn 20 px to the left and faded to alpha 192.

Update.doc: Per-frame update. Closes the menu when the mouse has been away for 500 ms or the owner is gone. Asks the owner to refill each button (OnContextMenuUpdate), moves the highlight off disabled buttons, opens sub-menus after a 750 ms hover, computes the menu size and position, and draws.

Vbi.doc: Per-frame hook: updates this menu and its sub-menu.

comments.text: Owner gets OnContextMenuReturn(requestId, 0): closed without a choice. Not for sub-menus.

__Close.doc: Common close path: removes the mouse listener and resets the active button. A sidebar menu notifies C640; otherwise the owner gets OnContextMenuReturn(request, 0), meaning no choice.

comments.text: Generic, in-menu and dropdown menus (types 0, 4, 5) stop the sidebar. Types 1 to 3 keep it.
Weapon menus (type 3) use 42 px rows, others 28 px.
selectFirst: the first button becomes active (0), otherwise nothing is highlighted (-1).

__Prepare.doc: Common setup for every menu kind: closes the previous contents, stores position, type, owner, request, title and keyboard mode, and clears all button lists. The menu is then ready for AddButton calls (state 1).

0.name: parentButton

1.doc: width of the parent menu, pixels, used for placement

GetBodyName.doc: Body name of the sub-menu frame model.

GetCameraPriority.doc: Camera priority of the sub-menu scene (181), drawn above the parent menu.

GetMaterialID.doc: Texture id used to draw the sub-menu (14).

GetMousePriority.doc: Mouse listener priority of the sub-menu (81), just above the parent menu.

GetParentButton.doc: Returns the index of the parent button this sub-menu belongs to.

GetParentWidth.doc: Returns the width of the parent menu.

comments.text: Sub-menu type 3 for weapon lists, 2 otherwise. No title.

PrepareSubMenu.doc: Prepares the sub-menu for a parent button. weapon selects the weapon sub-menu type (3) instead of the generic sub-menu (2). The position is given in screen pixels and the rest is passed to the common setup.

660.doc: Base class of the value nodes used by cutscene cameras: each node returns a vector (or a list of numbers) for a given time through QueryEffectiveValue. Subclasses are positions, orientations, FOVs, keyframe tracks and composites. Probably no direct instances.

Destruct.doc: Base destructor, returns this.

PeekRefString.doc: Base implementation: returns 0. Subclasses return the object reference name, if any.

QueryEffectiveValue.doc: Base implementation: returns 0. Overridden by subclasses.

660.name: CutValue

661.doc: A constant value node: returns the same array for every time.

0.doc: the constant array returned for any time
0.name: constantValue

Create.doc: Stores a copy of the given array; returns this, or nothing when the array is empty.

661.name: CutConstantValue

662.doc: Keyframed animation track for cutscene values: a list of keyframes (time, value node, interpolation flag, static flag) with cycle and interpolation modes. Interpolates between keyframes at a given time.

0.doc: list of [time, value, interpolation, static] entries
0.name: keyframes

1.doc: time of the last keyframe added
1.name: lastKeyframeTime

2.doc: index of the last keyframe, -1 when empty
2.name: lastKeyframeIndex

3.doc: 0 none, 1 repeat, 2 ping-pong
3.name: cycleMode

4.doc: time added after the last keyframe before the cycle restarts
4.name: cycleGap

5.doc: number of values per keyframe, fixed by the first keyframe with the flag
5.name: valueCount

6.doc: 0 none, 1 linear, 2 smooth
6.name: interpolationMode

AdjustTimestampForCycling.doc: Maps a time into the cycle: mode 1 wraps, mode 2 ping-pongs back and forth.

AppendKeyframe.doc: Adds a keyframe at the given time with a value node. Keyframes must be in increasing time order; with the flag set, all values must have the same length. Returns 1 when added.

Destruct.doc: Frees the value nodes of non-static keyframes.

GetValuesOfKeyframe.doc: Returns the values of keyframe index: the stored array for static keyframes, else the node value at the given time.

Init.doc: Clears the keyframes and resets the last index.

QueryEffectiveValue.doc: Returns the track value at the given time: adjusts the time for cycling, then interpolates between the two neighbouring keyframes (or returns the nearest one).

SetCycleMode.doc: Sets the cycle mode and the gap after the last keyframe.

SetInterpolationOptions.doc: Sets the interpolation mode (0 none, 1 linear, 2 smooth).

662.name: CutKeyframeTrack

663.doc: Value node: the position of a named reference point of a cutscene object (for example a dock port or a centre), optionally resolved through an object reference after a dot in the name.

0.doc: owning Cutscene object (C624)
0.name: cutscene

1.doc: reference name, part before the dot
1.name: referenceName

2.doc: part after the dot, the port of a mapped object; empty when none
2.name: portName

Create.doc: Stores the cutscene and the reference name; splits 'object.port' into the two fields. Returns this, or nothing when the object is not a cutscene.

QueryEffectiveValue.doc: Position of the reference. With a port, returns the absolute position of the dock port of the mapped object, else the reference centre.

663.name: CutReferencePosition

664.doc: Value node for a circular motion around a centre: angle moves linearly from start to end over a period, the position is the centre plus a circle of the radius value, with an optional height. An alternative value can replace the motion.

0.doc: centre value node
0.name: centerValue

1.doc: value node used instead of the orbit when set
1.name: alternativeValue

2.doc: radius value node; its first element scales the circle
2.name: radiusValue

3.doc: start angle, 16.16 fixed point
3.name: angleStart

4.doc: end angle, 16.16 fixed point
4.name: angleEnd

5.doc: period of one revolution, same time units as the query
5.name: periodTime

6.doc: value node giving the height (y component)
6.name: heightValue

Create.doc: Stores the six parameters; the angles are shifted left 16 bits. Returns this.

Destruct.doc: Frees the owned value nodes.

PeekRefString.doc: Returns the reference name of the centre value.

23592960 = 360 degrees in 16.16 fixed point, so the angle is turned into cosine and sine

QueryEffectiveValue.doc: Returns the position on the circle at the given time, added to the centre value.

665.doc: Value node that returns the scene anchor point of a cutscene object, looked up by name and index.

0.doc: owning Cutscene object (C624)
0.name: cutscene

1.doc: name of the scene anchor
1.name: anchorName

2.doc: index of the anchor within the name
2.name: anchorIndex

Create.doc: Stores the cutscene, anchor name and index. Returns this, or nothing when the object is not a cutscene.

QueryEffectiveValue.doc: Returns the scene anchor of the cutscene for the given name and index.
